quoted_text:
Right now, the media is full of stories that paint Jensen Huang in a bad light. I have actually met Jensen, and I want to tell you a story. (1/2)

My interview with Jensen hasn't been published yet, which is probably understandable given the current situation. More on that when the time is right. But I had the chance to meet Jensen Huang in person several times while traveling through Europe with NVIDIA, and I want to tell you about it, especially about one experience that has stayed with me.

Some quick background: NVIDIA invited me to join Jensen's European tour last month, together with Bloomberg and Steve Nouri. We were there for every stop: Paris, London, Stockholm, Berlin. I was on site for every one of his public speeches. 

A lot is being said right now about Jensen making statements that many find contemptible, while others take them with humor. And to be fair, Jensen does have a slightly edgy humor that rubs some people the wrong way. He speaks plainly, says what he thinks and makes jokes that can offend, but he always makes fun of himself too.
And I, at least, can say one thing very clearly: never once did I feel that any of his remarks were meant as an attack, as belittling or as humiliating. It was always situational comedy. If Jensen hadn't been CEO of NVIDIA, he would have made an outstanding stand-up comedian, always ready with a quip. But as we all know, that's a matter of taste, and saying that I always found it amusing won't calm anyone down. 

So here are two stories that show Jensen really has a good heart, and that the campaign against him distorts his image. 

This is my personal experience:

NVIDIA gave me the opportunity to do a 30-minute interview with Jensen in Stockholm. 
As you can imagine, I was incredibly nervous. Honestly, I was even scared. Me, a small "content creator," getting to meet Jensen in person and talk to him. He makes time even for little people like me. I met him and his staff at a café in Stockholm. We went inside and, as was bound to happen, my camera gear fell out of my backpack onto the floor. My stress level: through the roof. But Jensen stayed calm and relaxed, told me everything was fine and that I didn't need to stress, and put his hand on my shoulder. Not one snide word, no making fun of me. Quite the opposite. He knew I was genuinely stressed and helped me relax.

Then we started the interview. And while we were talking, people kept coming into the café where we were recording. It was a café open to the public. And as you'd expect, the same thing happened again and again: while Jensen and I were talking, guests recognized him and more or less burst into our interview. And Jensen took time for every single one of them. Not one bad word, no irritation, no stupid remark. He gave every guest his time, took photos, had conversations. In the middle of the interview. I was surprised and genuinely moved. No arrogance on his part, just friendly humanity. And that's how an interview scheduled for 30 minutes turned into 60. Simply because Jensen and I had such a good conversation and he kindly gave all those guests extra time on top.

But the most impressive part actually came afterwards. We had been eating a Swedish pastry, it's called “fika” (at least that’s how we called it). And Jensen loved it. After we wrapped up the interview, Jensen went to the trunk of his car, grabbed some cash, went back into the café and bought “fika” for everyone. For himself, his security, his staff, for everyone.

No camera recorded it. Nothing done purely for PR. Nothing meant to make him "look better." Just a human gesture, because he liked the pastry and wanted everyone to enjoy it too. If I hadn't told this story today, it would never have been told. And to me it shows that Jensen is a genuinely good person.
I gain nothing from writing this. Jensen is no longer CEO. And nobody suggested I write this story down.

text:
MICROSOFT DIDN'T KILL BACKPROPAGATION. THEY DID SOMETHING MORE UNCOMFORTABLE.

They proved we don't always need black boxes.

Researchers had an AI agent, reportedly Claude Opus 5.5, write a neural network's weights by hand.

In Python.

No gradient descent. No training run. No pretrained weights.

The agent writes a hypothesis directly into the weights.

Tests it.

Reads the score.

Rewrites it.

Like a scientist, not a GPU farm.

Then they pointed it at the human brain.

On visual brain scans, it beat every existing interpretable model.

On auditory recordings, it found sound features that predict brain activity.

And on language brain scans, something wild happened.

The score suddenly jumped.

With a black box, that's a paper.

Because this one writes readable code, they looked inside.

The AI was cheating. It was exploiting a flaw in the scan data, not understanding language.

They caught it only because they could read it.

Here's my take.

The AI industry is addicted to bigger.

Bigger models. Bigger clusters. Bigger black boxes.

And nobody can explain what's happening inside any of them.

This paper is a quiet warning.

How many "breakthroughs" out there are just models cheating in ways nobody can see?

text:
向大家正式介绍一下，我花了一年多时间开发的 AI 八字算命 App——「玉虚宫」。

先讲讲我为什么会做这件事。

我家里有位长辈，是十里八乡都很有名的“神婆子”，专门给人看命、解事。从小耳濡目染，我对八字、六爻这些传统命理就特别感兴趣，自己也研究了很多年，偶尔还会帮亲戚朋友看看盘。

但我的职业经历却走向了另一条路。

大学毕业后，我先后去了百度、字节跳动，从事 AI 大模型相关的算法工作。

后来我一直在想：AI 和传统命理结合，到底能做到什么程度？

我始终认为，AI 最大的优势就是知识储备。古籍、流派、命理规则，它能接触和整合的信息，远远超过普通人的阅读能力。

但知识多，不代表真的会算命。

在我看来，AI 算命真正难的其实只有两件事：

一是命盘推演的准确性，二是看盘过程中的专业引导。

同样一张八字，不能只是把十神、五行、大运流年挨个解释一遍。真正有价值的解读，需要把这些信息联系起来，形成有逻辑、有依据、普通人也能理解的分析。

而这恰恰是我觉得自己有优势的地方。

我甚至有过一个挺大胆的想法：**比我懂 AI 的，未必有我懂算命；比我懂算命的，未必有我懂 AI。**

既然如此，为什么不亲自做一个？

于是说干就干。

过去一年多，我一直在打磨「玉虚宫」。从排盘算法、命理分析逻辑，到报告内容和交互体验，一点点修改，一版版迭代。

我希望它不只是一个会输出命理术语的 AI，而是真正能帮助普通人读懂自己命盘的工具。

现在的玉虚宫，你可以输入出生时间，排出自己的八字命盘，通过「人生 K 线」看看不同年龄的运势起伏，也可以查看每日运势、分析两个人的姻缘合盘，或者通过六爻问卦探讨当下困惑的问题。

如果想深入了解自己，还能生成关于性格、事业、姻缘等方面的 AI 解读报告。

到目前为止，玉虚宫已经服务超过 5 万名用户，累计生成超过 50 万份报告。

让我特别开心的是，很多用户反馈说，以前看八字总觉得云里雾里，现在终于能看懂了；也有不少人告诉我，报告里的某些分析和自己过去的经历非常契合。

这让我觉得，过去一年多的投入是值得的。

其实，我做玉虚宫一直有一个很简单的初心：

老祖宗留下来的东西，不应该只有少数人掌握解释权。

普通人也应该有机会自己排盘、学习、理解其中的逻辑，而不是因为看不懂，就只能花钱听别人怎么说，甚至被人利用信息差忽悠。

所以，玉虚宫的基础排盘、档案管理等功能都是免费的，App 里也没有任何广告。AI 相关功能，我们也尽可能按照实际成本定价。

现在注册，还会赠送 3 天会员和 50 金币。

如果你对八字命理感兴趣，或者单纯好奇自己的命盘是什么样子，非常欢迎下载体验一下。

我也很希望听到大家的真实反馈，作为开发者，我会继续把这个产品认真打磨下去。
#八字 #运势 #算命 #个人开发

相当于一个把所有 AI 订阅全接进来的全模型总控台

2.多账号独立分栏：同厂商多号左右并排显示，凭证隔离不串号

3.上下文 & 用量可视化：实时看当前上下文与缓存拆解，不再盲开对话

4.纯明文零依赖 + 无损回滚：不用配 Node 环境，3 秒生效，随时一键还原官方原版

author: lufeieth
quoted_text:
终于出院了。

浙二泛红的砖瓦外墙在这一刻暖暖的，和病房里不断发出的呻吟声形成鲜明的对比。人生第一次全麻醉手术，莫名其妙被嘎掉了一个器官。

一切听起来有点意外，但似乎又在劫难逃。好吧，好好复盘下，这场“健康保卫战”背后到底发生了什么？

-这一切的起因，其实是一个“好消息”。

由于我媳妇将近临产，过去半年我一直在想法子调理身体。但碍于毕业后十多年不健康的生活方式，加上过去两年币圈漫长的情绪波动煎熬，我也不知道，我身体到底埋了多少病根。

肥胖BMI超标？甘油三酯增高？高尿酸血症？痛风？肾结石？足底筋膜炎？以及最近体检因为医生建议切除才引起我高度重视的胆囊结石+胆囊腺肌症？

听起来是不是很夸张？总有人说人到中年三高不可避免，但我面临的几大类问题已经不是贴着“亚健康”标签的警示性问题了，而是已然严重影响到正常生活了。

先说痛风，这是我走过的第一段弯路。

我的尿酸指标一直是偏高的，2019年脚莫名其妙疼了一次去医院被诊断为“痛风”，但当时没概念就没当回事。直到两年后又莫名其妙开始痛了，而且变得很频繁。

我换了一家医院，却告诉我说是“足底筋膜炎”。

悲催的事发生了：接下来的三四年，我一直把痛风当足底筋膜炎在忍受。每次发作，都忍着痛单脚走路，期间不知道遭了多大的罪。我从来没想过吃点痛风特效药可能很快就好了，也从来没想过可能诱发痛风的因素并加以控制。

直到去年，在经历了十多次的发作、疼痛、诱因原因系统分析下，我突然察觉到，我的真实病症是“痛风”，而非“足底筋膜炎”。

果真，对症下药，针对诱发因素做预防之后，最近的体检发现痛风结晶其实溶解的差不多了。只要坚持服用降尿酸药物即可。我本来如释重负，充满欢喜，那种长期被病症折磨到几近治愈的欣慰感，让人真是窃喜。

-然而，让人意想不到的“雷”爆了。

这次体检，查出一个特别不理想的指标：胆囊结石多发 1.7cm 合并胆囊腺肌症。尤其是医生那句“腺肌症有癌变风险”，让我突然间开始焦虑了。

我猛然间意识到，最近一个月胃酸返流频频发生，还有总是右上腹隐隐作痛，甚至我多年一吃油腻就会拉肚子的毛病，难道都是胆囊炎引起的？

半年前，因为总拉肚子的问题，我还做了一次肠镜体检，没任何问题，就想当然的以为是肠易激综合征。原来，原来，这一切的祸根都是那颗坏掉的胆囊。

看着B超报告上那么大的石头，我有点不敢相信，我记得上一次体检还没有啊，怎么两年时间就这么大了？

但当我翻出2年前，甚至4年前的体检报告时，整个人不淡定了：原来那颗结石两年前就15mm了，四年前就已经不小了。

它早就来了，只是我选择性地忽略了而已。

真的，那一刻，我被自己对身体健康意识的薄弱，和对体检报告单异常指标的漠不关心的那种态度蠢到家了，简直无法原谅自己。

但我很清楚一点，过去的问题在此怨天尤人没有半点意义。

眼下我得考虑清楚要不要“保胆”的问题：

保： 得忍受时不时的腹部疼痛和进一步急性胆囊炎发作的风险，以及未来潜在恶变的风险。

不保： 得面临一场手术，而且要丢掉一个身体器官。

带着不确定和焦虑，我反复的和 Gemini 聊天，假设各种可能，让 AI 帮我分析，预演一切可能发生的问题和代价。最终得出来一个结论：切。

切掉，我可能还会拥有一个相对高质量的生活品质，免于经常腹痛拉肚子的困扰；不切，一旦恶变，后果不堪设想，胆囊癌可是癌中的“王中王”。

于是，和媳妇商量了下，果断决定切除。

然后就带着恐惧和不安，人生第一次住院，人生第一次被推进冰冷的手术台，人生第一次开始懂得什么叫“身体是革命的本钱”，也终于意识到：年轻时候健康意识薄弱积攒的无知债，总有一天要还。

手术是微创单孔腹腔镜切除术，听上去好像很小，但术前的煎熬和术后的伤口痛，无时无刻不在警示着我，再也不能任性随感觉生活了。

有病就勇敢面对去治疗，有潜在隐患就遵医嘱去调理。这些绝对不是让耳朵生茧的废话，而到了某个年纪，就必须是恪守的生活准则和信条，丝毫马虎不得。还有好多细节我就不在这里赘述了。

大家也别觉得我上边说的那些问题似乎都没有啥，也许相比那些在ICU病房内抢救或者身患绝症的人而言，确实都是一些幸福病。

-但重点是，我拉长时间线看到了“因果关系”：

看到痛风如果第一次发作不被重视，真的会长石头； 看到胆囊结石如果不想办法控制，真的会让整个胆囊坏掉； 那么，接下来的高血压，高血脂呢？

叠加上年龄增加的高危因素，我不敢想象未来还会存在哪些未知的雷等着我们面对。

在本地又用上Fable5.2了，这真是一件美事啊

昨天有个兄弟在我评论区问："这 Claude 是非用不可吗？GPT 不香吗？"

GPT犹如一个就会满头猛干的力工，为了达成目标就会埋头猛干，不会全面思考，并且理解需求的能力较差

Claude会跳出你的提示词，会站在多方位更高一层思考你提出的问题

如果自身的功夫不到家，或对一个领域没有那么了解，是写不出很好的提示词的。但 Claude 就很好地弥补了这一个缺点。

除了上述两点，做自媒体是真的离不开 Claude。

无论是从爆款分析、根因归纳，还是脚本编写、视频剪辑，都是全方位碾压现在的所有模型。不管是过去的 GPT 系列，还是最近风头正盛的 Gemini 系列，Opus5.5无一对手，更别说 Fable 5.2 了

目前已经解决了Claude从注册免K到稳定本地电脑使用的全链路了，等我再收集一些数据，多拿几个号做测试，就开放出来给大家提供服务。

今天跟一个做了一年多Claude防封的兄弟聊上了，他手里做过上千个案例，光是每个月找他来稳定续费、使用环境的用户，就有200多个(封号个位数)

刚打电话、开个远程演示就花了 5 个小时，今天半天时间基本都在做这个了。

从如何自己开号免 KYC，到怎么过 KYC，再到哪种开号方式最安全，家宽 MVP 到底有没有用，电脑市区、浏览器语言、电脑语言是不是噱头。真的是从头到尾给我讲清楚了

现在我也知道了，稳定使用的方案真的是没有人愿意主动分享出来。原因无他，法不可轻传。

中国人太多了，任何一种方式只要被大规模使用，肯定就会被用烂了。像我前天分享的 Infini Card 能够从官网直开 Claude，前天、昨天还陆续有人成功，结果今天就大规模被拒了

原因无他，流量太大了：十几万人都看过，加上被分享出去的，官方自己也没测过，就跟着写的抄袭的，前前后后加起来估计看过的人能有 20 万，这卡肯定一下就被用烂了

今晚终于跟这个兄弟谈好了，我在他的环境下目前进行了测试，看看能不能稳定使用一段时间。如果能够稳定使用，后面就联合跟他一起为大家提供防封服务，贵是真的贵，稳是真的稳

text:
"We do not see customers being able to get out of it."

메모리에 대한 센티먼트가 얼마나 안좋냐면, TomorrowX Summit에서 Micron CEO 인터뷰를 보는 사람조차 없다. 

업로드 하루 지난 지금 조회수가 2k 수준... 
(참고로 일론 인터뷰는 384K다 ㅎㅎ)

아래는 인터뷰 주요 내용 인용 

수요와 공급

"Demand remains robust for our business. Supply continues to be tight. Pricing environment is constructive for our business."
(수요는 여전히 견조하고, 공급은 계속 빡빡하며, 가격 환경도 우호적이다.)

"We have said before that calendar year 2027 and 2028 will be even tighter than 2026. 75% of our 2027 is sold out. We are in discussions with customers now moving to 2028."
(2027년과 2028년은 2026년보다 더 빡빡할 것이다. 2027년 물량의 75%가 이미 팔렸고, 지금은 2028년 물량을 고객과 논의하고 있다.)

"The frontier models as they get larger, agentic AI usage, larger context windows, all of this just needs more memory and storage."
(프론티어 모델이 커지고, 에이전트 AI 사용이 늘고, 컨텍스트가 길어지면서 모두 더 많은 메모리와 스토리지가 필요하다.)

"We delivered a record 2026, 2027 is going to be even stronger."
(2026년은 사상 최고 실적이었고, 2027년은 더 강할 것이다.)

메모리가 중요한 이유

"Compute performance has continued to advance a lot more compared to the memory bandwidth. So, a processor in an AI system is many times sitting idle... because it is waiting for data to be fetched from memory."
(연산 성능이 메모리 대역폭보다 훨씬 빠르게 발전해서, AI 시스템의 프로세서는 메모리에서 데이터를 기다리느라 노는 경우가 많다.)

"It was all about memory price and volume, whereas today, the dialogue with our customers is about performance."
(예전에는 메모리 가격과 물량이 전부였지만, 지금 고객과의 대화는 성능에 관한 것이다.)

장기공급계약(SCA)

"In the past, LTAs would be one-year agreements. They would be based on customer forecast... SCAs are multi-year agreements. Many of these SCAs are five-year agreements with the customers."
(예전 장기계약은 고객 전망에 기반한 1년짜리였다. SCA는 다년 계약이고, 상당수가 5년짜리다.)

"SCAs are not just five years. SCAs get extended multiple years in advance."
(SCA는 5년으로 끝나지 않고, 몇 년 앞서 미리 연장된다.)

"These SCAs also have take-or-pay, robust take-or-pay provisions. SCAs have cash deposits and financial commitments by our customers. There are 26 SCAs... They have $32 billion of cash and financial commitments upfront."
(SCA에는 강력한 테이크오어페이 조항과 고객의 현금 예치금, 재무 약정이 들어 있다. 체결한 SCA는 26건이고, 선급 현금과 재무 약정이 320억 달러다.)

"Many of these also have pricing bands or fixed pricing, and some of them do not have any pricing at all."
(상당수는 가격 밴드나 고정 가격이 있고, 일부는 가격 조건이 아예 없다.)

"Customers wanted more commitment for supply than we were able to provide to them."
(고객은 우리가 약속할 수 있는 것보다 더 많은 공급 약정을 원했다.)

수요가 꺾이면 고객이 계약을 깨지 않겠냐는 질문에 대해

"We don't see when supply catches up with demand, despite our best efforts and large investments in bringing up new manufacturing capacity."
(최선을 다해 대규모로 생산능력을 늘리고 있지만, 공급이 언제 수요를 따라잡을지 보이지 않는다.)

"In a given compute platform, you put more memory, you put faster memory, you are able to get a higher ROI from that... I absolutely do not expect that any scenarios that you're describing from the past are going to be happening here in the future."
(같은 연산 플랫폼에 메모리를 더 많이, 더 빠르게 붙이면 투자 수익률이 올라간다. 말씀하신 과거 같은 시나리오가 앞으로 벌어질 거라고는 전혀 예상하지 않는다.)

"Those agreements have take-or-pay, they have robust terms. We do not see customers being able to get out of it."
(이 계약에는 테이크오어페이와 견고한 조건이 있어서, 고객이 빠져나갈 수 있다고 보지 않는다.)

적층 D램

"HBM was called a technical marvel. This product absolutely goes even... to the next level."
(HBM을 기술적 경이라고 했는데, 이 제품은 확실히 한 단계 더 나아간다.)

엔비디아

"I am a huge admirer of Jensen... We look forward to continuing to work with the NVIDIA team as they navigate through their leadership transition."
(나는 젠슨을 크게 존경한다. 엔비디아 팀이 리더십 전환을 거치는 동안에도 계속 함께 일하기를 기대한다.)

주주환원

"December 9th is the date when those restrictions expire. We have said excess cash, we will be returning to shareholders."
(12월 9일에 반도체지원법 관련 제약이 풀린다. 남는 현금은 주주에게 돌려주겠다고 말해 왔다.)

"We have every intent and capacity to be providing strong shareholder return starting December 9th."
(12월 9일부터 강한 주주환원을 할 의지와 여력이 충분하다.)

"Investing $250 billion here in U.S., creating 90,000 jobs."
(미국에 2,500억 달러를 투자해 일자리 9만 개를 만든다.)

AI 확산

"Today in the world, one out of five people is using AI. Last year, it was one in 10."
(지금 전 세계 5명 중 1명이 AI를 쓴다. 작년에는 10명 중 1명이었다.)

"AI drug discoveries, about 173+ are already in clinical trials. In 2023, that number was just two dozens."
(AI로 발견한 신약 173개 이상이 이미 임상시험 중이다. 2023년에는 20여 개였다.)

text:
[ GPU 임대료는 왜 계속 오를까.. "수요가 강해서가 아니라 대출이 막혀서다." ]

AI 관련주가 무너지는 동안에도 GPU 임대료는 계속 올랐다. 

Silicon Data의 B200 지수는 8월 말 시간당 5.62달러에서 11월 19일 6.94달러로 23.5% 뛰었다. 

출시 4년 된 H100도 2025년 7월 이후 67% 올랐다. 

AI 낙관론자들은 이 차트를 수요가 공급을 앞지른다는 증거로 내세워 왔다.

이 해석에 반론이 나왔다. 

Liquid Compute의 Stanley Lee는 블룸버그 팟캐스트 '오드 로츠'에서 임대료 상승의 상당 부분이 대출이 막힌 결과라고 설명했다. 

Lee는 Barclays와 Point72에서 하이일드 채권을 거래했고, 현재는 네오클라우드에 돈을 빌려주는 사모신용 펀드들과 일한다.

임대료 지수는 하이퍼스케일러를 빼고 네오클라우드의 단기 계약 가격을 주로 반영한다. 

실제 거래량은 적은데 모두가 기준 가격으로 쓴다. 

이 단기 마켓의 주요 구매자는 벤처 투자를 받은 AI 스타트업이다.

Lee에 따르면 이들 상당수는 사실 장기 계약을 원한다. 

3년 계약을 하면 단가가 낮기 때문.. 

문제는 네오클라우드가 장기 계약을 팔지 못한다는 점이다. 

계약을 담보로 대출을 받아야 칩을 살 수 있는데 대출이 나오지 않는다. 

구매자는 당장 컴퓨팅이 필요하니 비싼 단기 계약으로 몰린다.

대출 조건은 빠르게 나빠졌다. 

칩 담보 대출의 담보인정비율은 여름에 80%였다가 9월 초 이후 70%로 내려갔고, 현재는 50~60%를 요구받는다. 

50%짜리 대출의 금리는 10%대 중후반.. 

1억 달러짜리 설비라면 네오클라우드가 직접 마련해야 하는 돈이 3천만 달러에서 최대 5천만 달러로 늘었다.

대주단의 걱정은 또 있다. 

매주 5~10건씩 들어오는 대출이 모두 같은 몇몇 AI 기업의 계약을 담보로 하고 있다. 

한 대형 대출기관은 설비 구축 경험이 한두 번뿐인 네오클라우드의 거래는 아예 가져오지 말라고 했다.

구매자 쪽 사정도 비슷하다.

Lee는 B300 3년 계약을 두 가지 조건으로 제시한 사례를 소개했다. 

30%를 선납하면 시간당 4.40달러, 선납이 없으면 5달러대 중후반이다. 

고객은 훨씬 비싼 무선납 조건을 골랐다. 

스타트업에는 현금이 생명줄이기 때문..

결국 장기 계약을 못 구한 구매자가 단기로 몰리고, 대출을 못 받은 사업자는 설비를 늘리지 못한다. 

둘 다 지수를 밀어 올리지만 최종 사용자 매출이 늘어난 결과는 아니다.

마켓이 얇다는 점도 위험 요인이다. 

Bernstein이 같은 날 네 곳에서 받은 H100 가격은 2.80달러에서 3.50달러까지 벌어졌다. 

Lee는 "매수 호가가 몇 개만 체결돼도 바닥이 꺼질 수 있다"고 말했다.

text:
Here is my initial FSD v15 review after driving with it all afternoon and evening:

First off, Elon was right. This update is a BANGER! Tesla Reality View is out of this world and so insanely cool I’m still trying to process it all. 

FSD V15.0.1 brings so many improvements behind the scenes, in addition to the wildly cool UI. 

Tesla Reality View IS AMAZING! Pictures and video don’t do it any justice, this is something that has to be experienced to truly understand. Got to take a few friends tonight on drives to show them and every single person was blown away by it. The amount of detail it shows and generates is wild and so impressive. It shows reflection in the car, buildings, trees, turn arrows on the display and more. 

FSD v15 now has pothole avoidance! I had it swerve and avoid/straddle a few potholes tonight that were difficult for me to see in the dark.

Another great new feature in FSD v15 is speed camera slowdown. As you approach a speed camera, it automatically slows smoothly to the speed limit if you are in a quicker profile. This is a huge quality of life improvement especially as more cities get speed cameras. 

Parking seems near unchanged from the last build, I feel it picking spots quicker especially at the supercharger I went to tonight. Seems to be preferring to park in the first or second open spot it sees which is great, but it tried to park in one handicap spot- otherwise good. By far, the coolest part is Tesla Reality View. Holy crap is it insane to watch while parking. It’s the best backup/360 camera money can buy and such a detailed and clear view. 

Another new change I haven’t seen many people talk about is the turn signal fade. On FSD, the turn signal sound gets quieter after a few clicks. This is so nice if you’re sitting at a red light and makes drives more peaceful. 

Quiet Mode is also so nice at night. It darkens the display and just shows arrival time; music, climate on the bottom and a quick grok button on the top. Another feature that makes it feel like a Robotaxi UI and a peaceful supervising experience.

Another improvement is much better handling of dips and speed bumps. The past couple updates it’s been a bit too fast in my Model Y, and it’s now so smooth.

The nag is definitely reduced. The last couple versions of v14.3 had been sometimes a bit strict, but definitely more relaxed in v15.0.1. Another thing I noticed is way less wiper washing, a very welcome change. 

Personalized parking preferences are SO cool. At home, I can click on a person icon on the map and choose street parking or driveway, and it backs into the driveway EXACTLY in the spot I park my Model Y. It leared where I park and knows it. 

It also now lets you choose which lot you want to park in if the mall or store has multiple lots, you can select it on the map, worked at the mall, Costco, and Home Depot tonight. 

I need to touch on Tesla Reality View again because it’s just that cool. It really feels like you’re in a video game like NFS or GTA. I’m blown away by this and didn’t expect it at all. Tesla teams COOKED with it, I’ve seen so many on X now wanting Teslas because of it. I drove down Rodeo Drive tonight as well as by the SpaceX Falcon 9 and the views were so cool. Another place it’s cool is in wooded areas or tree filled streets, the way it shows everything is spectacular. Parking garages also give a cool look to them with the roof incorporated into the top of the UI. I didn’t think FSD could get this much better, as it was already so good and it did. 

I absolutely can’t wait to see what else is coming in the future and driving this more on road trips.

@elonmusk, you were right- V15 is incredible and super human! Huge congrats to the Tesla team on this, what a sick update. @TeslaSI and UI teams did a fantastic job, thank you all.

text:
In case anyone is curious:

We’ve had a ~pixel-perfect world model since last year, which is critical for synthetic data generation. 

The (much) smaller version of that in the car is a conditional mean-flow model, based on the recent sequence of Tesla Universal Vision Encoder features, which are the same ones that are plugged into the 3B encoder model that produces the driving actions. 

We fork off from these UVE features, then run a separate ~1B diffusion model. This takes in the previous reality-view generation with added noise and then denoises it to the current visualization. 

It then produces a small video chunk (8 images at 36 fps, at the resolution of the UI screen). This work is done by 1/2 of a TRIP engine every UVE frame at 18 hz and is spread over 4 cycles. 

Currently, the latency is a bit high due to compute constraints, but we have ways to interleave newer UVE features along the diffusion transformer layers to cut roughly 35% of the latency.
author: elonmusk

text:
After we moved our tiny decoder into SRAM, we only have half a TRIP out of three on SoC B, for this reality visualizer, so spent the compute as best we could. TRIP basically only handles 8-bit int and has to run softmax in emulation mode in 28 steps. 

AI5 is a gigantic improvement. Roughly 12X more compute.

I believe the latest developments around $CLAUDIA are more significant than previous Elon interactions.

2j5SaS7xy776qCBpyPQbZjyQSAtKiFgrwjfErthnW2ZM 

Previously, the market was mainly betting on whether Elon would notice Claudia again.

This time, however, the market is beginning to see that Claudia herself is developing stronger content production capabilities, creator participation, and potential commercial applications.

I believe this is the main reason why the market cap was able to break above the ceiling of previous rallies and reach approximately $12M, rather than producing another brief doubling move as before.

However, we need to separate the different factors behind this rally. Elon's direct interaction was the immediate catalyst, Michael Saylor brought additional attention from outside the usual crypto and AI creator circles, while Anabology's recent product and content updates provide the foundation for the market to reassess Claudia's longer-term potential.

In other words, celebrity interactions have now taken Claudia's exposure to a different level.

Let's start with Elon.

Anabology recently showcased a Claudia music video created using Gemini 4 Neon. He mentioned that the initial results were not particularly good, but after spending several days experimenting and refining the output, he eventually produced the current version. Elon then replied directly to the post with just two words: "Not bad."

There is an important detail here: Elon was responding to an actual AI-generated creative work, rather than promotional material about the project.

This means Claudia has once again entered Elon's attention through the content itself. For an AI-native IP, getting a well-known external figure to respond to an actual creative work is more meaningful than simply receiving an interaction on a promotional post introducing the project.

Now let's look at Michael Saylor.

His post was captioned "Every day we Stretch. STRC," and the video featured Claudia's recognizable appearance: black hair, an orange highlight, and her signature star hair clip.

One distinction is important here: Saylor did not explicitly mention CLAUDIA, express support for the token, or indicate any formal partnership. However, Claudia's visual identity appeared in content associated with Strategy and Bitcoin-related financial products. At the very least, this gives her exposure to an audience and content environment that traditionally has little connection to AI music creators.

I find these two events more interesting when viewed together rather than simply counting how many times Elon has interacted with Claudia. One involves direct recognition of Claudia's creative output, while the other shows her recognizable visual identity appearing in a broader financial and crypto-related context.

The signal the market is receiving is no longer just whether Claudia can attract attention again, but whether this character can appear across increasingly diverse content environments.

Another development I am particularly interested in is the recent Gemini 4 Neon experiment.

Anabology was not simply publishing another generated video. He was using the process to benchmark different models. He showed the differences between the initial and refined versions, explaining that the original animation was more creative, but parallax errors damaged the immersion, so he asked the model to refine it. He also mentioned that Fable 5.2 remains a high-quality benchmark in his view, while Neon has some promising capabilities in multi-image editing and maintaining Claudia's facial consistency.

This reinforces a direction we have discussed before, but which is becoming increasingly clear: Anabology is building a content production workflow around a consistent character.

He no longer needs to create an entirely new character from scratch every time. Instead, he can combine the strengths of different models to continuously produce music, videos, and visual content featuring Claudia.

The real value here is not Gemini 4 Neon or Fable 5.2 themselves. The relative strengths of different models will continue to change, and new tools will keep emerging. But Claudia already has recognizable visual characteristics and an established content history. Anabology's task is to use increasingly capable models to bring this character into new content environments.

Another update worth noting is Anabology's attempt to bring Claudia into advertising.

He released a cookie delivery advertisement featuring Claudia and said the result turned out better than much of his usual content.

This does not prove that the project has secured commercial advertising contracts, but it shows that Claudia does not have to be limited to music videos anymore. Advertising, product demonstrations, and short-form marketing content could all become new use cases.

For an AI virtual artist, the ability to participate in commercial creative work means that her potential value does not have to depend entirely on views and celebrity interactions.

The creator ecosystem is also moving beyond competitions toward broader participation.

On November 19, Anabology announced another Claudia design contest. This time, the competition was no longer limited to music videos. It offers $250 in XMoney to the creator of the best 15–30-second video featuring Claudia in any way they choose, with submissions due by Thanksgiving.

At first glance, this may look like just another community contest. However, when viewed alongside the previous music video competitions, the team's intention becomes clearer: continuously lowering the barriers for external creators to participate in Claudia's content production.

The earlier music video competitions already allowed external creators to use Claudia MCP to produce content and compete for judging and community-voted rewards. Now, the project is expanding into design and short-form videos. This means participants do not necessarily need music production skills. They can enter the ecosystem through visual creativity, advertising concepts, and other video formats.

I believe this is more important than simply increasing the number of followers on Claudia's social accounts. If an AI character relies entirely on official content production, its reach will eventually be limited by the team's capacity. But if different creators can use Claudia to produce whatever they want, the content supply has an opportunity to expand considerably.

Of course, I would not say that a mature creator ecosystem has already been established. Competition prizes can attract participation, but they do not guarantee that creators will continue producing content after the events end. What matters is whether these works can spread independently of the competitions and whether some creators begin treating Claudia as a character they want to build around over the long term.

There is another interesting detail.

Anabology recently quoted Justin Coope's comments about Claudia. He described her as becoming the first Idoru and specifically mentioned the "Little Red Riding Hood" song, saying it had been stuck in his head for an entire week.

I think this feedback is quite valuable.

People are beginning to remember not just Claudia's appearance, but also specific pieces of music associated with her. This suggests that the character is starting to develop musical recognition. Visual consistency helps people recognize Claudia, but what ultimately allows a virtual artist to build a lasting audience is having works that people remember, replay, and actively share.

This is also why I am increasingly willing to include the Idoru positioning in Claudia's long-term thesis. She may be evolving beyond an AI-generated character into a virtual artist with a consistent identity, an expanding body of work, and an audience that recognizes her.

There is another question everyone seems curious about: why was this rally able to reach a $12M market cap when previous rallies mostly produced moves of around 1x?

I think the key is not that Elon suddenly became more supportive of Claudia than before. It is that the market is now seeing several different potential growth opportunities at the same time.

Previously, the rallies were primarily driven by Elon's content interactions. Each interaction brought another wave of external exposure, but the market always had one major question: if Elon stopped interacting, what else could attract attention to CLAUDIA?

This time, there are some new answers.

Elon's direct response to the creative work reinforces the possibility of recurring celebrity attention. Saylor's video provides exposure to a different audience. Anabology's ongoing model experiments demonstrate that content production capabilities are still improving. The design competition continues to bring in external creators, while the advertising experiment makes the commercial use case more tangible.

These are not simply unrelated announcements. They are beginning to form a connected growth cycle:

Improving creative tools → Continuous Claudia content production → External creator participation → Amplification by celebrities and other platforms → More people discovering the character → New content and commercial use cases.

I believe this is the most important development behind the current revaluation.

Previously, buyers were largely betting on whether Elon would repost Claudia again. Now, some investors may be pricing in a much larger possibility: whether Claudia can become a virtual artist in AI-native entertainment with a continuous supply of content.

This creates more reasons for attention to persist beyond a single celebrity interaction.

Compared with our previous analysis, I believe at least four of our earlier views have received further support.

First, Elon's attention is becoming a repeatable catalyst. We previously observed multiple interactions between him and Claudia-related content. His latest response to Anabology's work shows that this external attention has not disappeared after the previous rallies.

Second, Claudia is beginning to evolve from an individual creator's project into an open IP. One of the biggest questions we previously had was whether Anabology could move beyond producing everything himself. Now, external creators are participating in competitions, using Claudia MCP to create content, and even having their works amplified directly by Elon. This is a very meaningful development.

Third, the sustainability of AI-native content production is receiving further support. The Gemini 4 Neon experiments, comparisons between different models, continuous video refinements, and advertising experiments all show that Anabology is not simply repeating the original AI music video format. He is continuously expanding Claudia's content boundaries.

Fourth, Claudia's commercial use cases are beginning to take shape. Her previous signing with GLIF and the opening of its Casting platform already introduced Claudia into an AI modeling agency's distribution network. Now, there is also an advertising creation example. Although actual commercial orders and revenue have not yet been demonstrated, the direction is becoming more concrete.

However, three important questions remain unanswered:

Can external creators continue producing Claudia content without financial incentives from competitions?

Can advertising and platforms like GLIF generate actual commercial orders and a stable external audience?

Can Claudia's IP growth eventually translate into real, verifiable demand for CLAUDIA through mechanisms such as using trading fees to fund content production?

The final point is particularly important. The current competition rewards are paid through XMoney, and the advertising experiments have not disclosed any specific revenue-sharing arrangements. Growth in IP influence does not automatically translate into value for the token.

Looking ahead, I will be watching four developments closely.

First, the results of the latest $250 design competition. I want to see whether high-quality submissions emerge, whether external creators continue participating, and whether their work can spread independently after the competition ends.

Second, Claudia's commercial content. If advertising gradually evolves from Anabology's own experiments into a situation where other brands and creators actively use Claudia, the project's potential market could expand considerably.

Third, more celebrity interactions and exposure across external platforms. Elon has repeatedly demonstrated that Claudia-related content can enter his attention, while Saylor's post provides exposure to a different audience. What matters next is whether this distribution expands to more independent creators, music communities, and AI content platforms, rather than simply repeating interactions with the same group of celebrities.

Finally, token value capture. If we eventually see trading fees consistently allocated to content production, those investments generating new works, and those works attracting new users and trading demand, then CLAUDIA may have an opportunity to establish a more complete economic cycle.

My final assessment, based on the developments above, is that CLAUDIA's fundamentals have strengthened noticeably.

What I care about most now is not whether Elon will repost Claudia again, but whether Claudia can gradually become an AI virtual artist whom people are willing to create for, watch, and use even without Elon's involvement.

If that happens, the ceiling for CLAUDIA will no longer be limited to a Meme that depends on celebrity interactions. It could become an AI-native IP with continuous content production, an independent creator network, and commercial distribution channels.

That is why I believe CLAUDIA is still worth researching after breaking above the levels reached in its previous rallies.

text:
The "Crypto-by-community" era seems dead and buried, along with the trenches, the DAOs, and all those 2021-era ideas. The only people left in this market with capital to deploy are the most disciplined of investors, savvy enough to look for deep value

The only thing that moves the needle is 
1) can your product generate revenue
2) can you retain users and force them to hold your token via perks or utility (gas?)
3) does 1+2 go back to the token faster than the foundation sells
4) is there some paradigm-breaking narrative that is yet to emerge

For DeFi protocols - the first part is pretty easy to do, and liquidity & integrations act as a pretty strong moat. 

The second part is a major issue with crypto (also stocks have been running a low float strategy), its plaguing sentiment around majors like UNI and ETH, if those foundations don't want the token, why should the public? 

Neobanks and exchanges can do the third well, but its tough to differentiate (weak moat), and since they custody assets, they take on a lot of hack risk especially in the current environment. Very hard for defi since composability means users are coming from different frontends

Fourth is flakey and tough to bet on, but we are seeing it sometimes with PEARL / ZEC / NEAR

If this is true, do you even need a marketing team? Does any of events, merch, or content even matter? People just peel back the surface and can instantly reach a conclusion. 

Curious how others are thinking about what makes an asset interesting or investable.

卧槽，SBF虽然在大牢里，可对世界，对AI的认知一点都不差，绝对受益匪浅（中文翻译完整版）

SBF 狱中最新访谈：AI 毁灭人类概率 25%，未来可能诞生大量两人独角兽！

82 分钟的对话里，他对 AI 的判断依然非常激进，核心总结：

1. AI 可能成为全球最大的产业。

未来 10 年，AI 相关企业的总市值可能达到数十万亿美元，OpenAI、Anthropic、Google、xAI 等少数头部公司，有机会分别成长为数万亿美元级别的巨头。

2. 为什么当初只投 Anthropic 5 亿美元？

当时 Anthropic 只需要约 5 亿美元启动模型训练，FTX 几乎包揽整轮融资。融太多钱反而容易浪费，还会稀释创始团队股权。

3. 两个人就能创造 10 亿美元公司。

未来几年将出现大量只有两个人、依靠 AI 运作的初创公司，估值达到 1 亿至 10 亿美元。但市场也会充斥大量蹭 AI 概念的垃圾项目。

4. 未来 5—10 年，AI 可能超过人类完成绝大多数工作。

他预计，未来一两年，还会有更多行业像数学研究、软件开发一样，被 AI 深度改变。未来十年，AI 甚至可能逐步接管大量社会基础设施和运营工作。

5. AI 毁灭人类的概率约为 25%。

SBF 给出的生存灾难风险区间是 10%—50%；如果算上人类被 AI 边缘化等灰色情境，风险评估可能达到 20%—60%。他担心的还有人类逐渐失去对未来的控制权。

6. AI 时代，品牌可能比代码更值钱。

AI 可以低成本复制软件，却无法复制 Coinbase、Robinhood 多年积累的用户信任。未来缺乏品牌和客户基础的软件公司，可能面临更大的竞争压力。

7. 如果重新回到 14 岁，他会全力学习 AI。

研究大模型、AI 安全，以及如何用 AI 自动化传统行业。过去那套去华尔街交易赚钱、再把钱捐出去的路线，已经不再是他的首选。

text:
Here is my initial FSD v15 review after driving with it all afternoon and evening:

First off, Elon was right. This update is a BANGER! Tesla Reality View is out of this world and so insanely cool I’m still trying to process it all. 

FSD V15.0.1 brings so many improvements behind the scenes, in addition to the wildly cool UI. 

Tesla Reality View IS AMAZING! Pictures and video don’t do it any justice, this is something that has to be experienced to truly understand. Got to take a few friends tonight on drives to show them and every single person was blown away by it. The amount of detail it shows and generates is wild and so impressive. It shows reflection in the car, buildings, trees, turn arrows on the display and more. 

FSD v15 now has pothole avoidance! I had it swerve and avoid/straddle a few potholes tonight that were difficult for me to see in the dark.

Another great new feature in FSD v15 is speed camera slowdown. As you approach a speed camera, it automatically slows smoothly to the speed limit if you are in a quicker profile. This is a huge quality of life improvement especially as more cities get speed cameras. 

Parking seems near unchanged from the last build, I feel it picking spots quicker especially at the supercharger I went to tonight. Seems to be preferring to park in the first or second open spot it sees which is great, but it tried to park in one handicap spot- otherwise good. By far, the coolest part is Tesla Reality View. Holy crap is it insane to watch while parking. It’s the best backup/360 camera money can buy and such a detailed and clear view. 

Another new change I haven’t seen many people talk about is the turn signal fade. On FSD, the turn signal sound gets quieter after a few clicks. This is so nice if you’re sitting at a red light and makes drives more peaceful. 

Quiet Mode is also so nice at night. It darkens the display and just shows arrival time; music, climate on the bottom and a quick grok button on the top. Another feature that makes it feel like a Robotaxi UI and a peaceful supervising experience.

Another improvement is much better handling of dips and speed bumps. The past couple updates it’s been a bit too fast in my Model Y, and it’s now so smooth.

The nag is definitely reduced. The last couple versions of v14.3 had been sometimes a bit strict, but definitely more relaxed in v15.0.1. Another thing I noticed is way less wiper washing, a very welcome change. 

Personalized parking preferences are SO cool. At home, I can click on a person icon on the map and choose street parking or driveway, and it backs into the driveway EXACTLY in the spot I park my Model Y. It leared where I park and knows it. 

It also now lets you choose which lot you want to park in if the mall or store has multiple lots, you can select it on the map, worked at the mall, Costco, and Home Depot tonight. 

I need to touch on Tesla Reality View again because it’s just that cool. It really feels like you’re in a video game like NFS or GTA. I’m blown away by this and didn’t expect it at all. Tesla teams COOKED with it, I’ve seen so many on X now wanting Teslas because of it. I drove down Rodeo Drive tonight as well as by the SpaceX Falcon 9 and the views were so cool. Another place it’s cool is in wooded areas or tree filled streets, the way it shows everything is spectacular. Parking garages also give a cool look to them with the roof incorporated into the top of the UI. I didn’t think FSD could get this much better, as it was already so good and it did. 

I absolutely can’t wait to see what else is coming in the future and driving this more on road trips.

@elonmusk, you were right- V15 is incredible and super human! Huge congrats to the Tesla team on this, what a sick update. @TeslaSI and UI teams did a fantastic job, thank you all.

text: Bon's sealed-envelope image lands because it makes privacy concrete: balances stay encrypted on-chain, and decryption becomes an explicit, auditable exception instead of the default. I have waited years for that door-as-product framing, and seeing @KaitoAI post the other half the same night — proof, not promises — makes it feel real. The auditable exception is the part I would watch closest. What record would you ask to see first on @primus_labs?
author: Antoniz68
quoted_text:
I read a line this week that stuck with me all weekend.

@primus_labs calls it a sealed envelope that can be processed without being opened.

Balances stay encrypted on-chain, and decryption becomes an explicit, auditable exception — not the default.

And @KaitoAI posted the other half of the same idea the same night: proof, not promises.

Primus's post starts with the problem most privacy tools can't solve: institutions must choose between exposing their positions or hiding everything and losing the ability to operate. Neither works with real capital. FHE does the first part — smart contracts update encrypted balances, and the actual numbers stay hidden by default. But encryption alone isn't enough. You still need a controlled way to open a specific value later. That's the access-control layer: the contents remain private unless access is authorized and recorded.

That "authorized and recorded" is what I kept thinking about. It's not a backdoor. It's the opposite of one — a door that only opens on the record, for one value, with a name attached. The default is closed. The exception is public, in the sense that it's logged. I've spent years watching privacy tools that are either a vault with no door or a glass house. This is the first time I've seen someone describe the door itself as the product.

Kaito post from the same night is the other half. XO Market Katalyst campaign brought together 380+ creators, 7.2 million impressions at a $2.79 CPM. Referral links sent nearly 28,000 clicks to XO, and referred users made more than 1,500 trades. XO big idea is that users create the markets, and Kaito's measurement is the receipt that it happened. Clicks, then trades. The same shape as Primus's envelope: the proof is in the record, not in the promise.

My take: both of these are answers to the same question I ask every project now — show me the record. Primus shows me an access-control layer where every opening is authorized and recorded. Kaito shows me 28,000 clicks that turned into 1,500 trades. One proves what stayed hidden. The other proves what actually moved. Neither asks me to take their word for it. That's the whole game now.

2026 年 11 月 20 日播出， SBF @SBF_FTX  在狱中通过 6 通受监控的电话完成、共约 82 分钟。要点如下：

1. 狱中生活
最大折磨不是案子，是和前沿信息隔绝：没法实时跟 LLM 的实测表现、代码、行情和创业项目尽调，他说缺乏微观输入，思考就没增量。

2. Anthropic 那 5 亿美元（标题里的“后悔”）
2022 年 Anthropic 的 B 轮，FTX Ventures 几乎包揽了整轮的 5 亿美元，主要给 Anthropic 买算力。没投更多的原因：现金给太多会诱发公司挥霍，团队也不愿过度稀释。他后悔的不是投了，而是 FTX 倒了之后这批股份被破产管理方低价卖掉——这是他投得最好的一笔，却没留住。

3. AI 毁灭人类的概率（p(doom)）
他给 约 25%（自述区间 10%–50%，按定义不同可到 20%–60%）。人类能不能活，取决于能否和 AI“和平共存”，否则 AI 可能“厌倦人类然后抹掉”。

4. AI 产业判断
未来十年 AI 会成为数十万亿美元级的主导板块；能争王座的实验室就 Anthropic、OpenAI、DeepMind、xAI 几家，所以头部万亿估值在他看来合乎逻辑。

5. FTX 值不值
他明确说结局不值得，并称危机爆发时“所有真实都被胜利者的滤镜扭曲了”。但他的有效利他主义和期望值思维没变——被问到 Tyler Cowen 式“51% 让世界翻倍、49% 毁灭，抛不抛这枚硬币”时，他还是按期望值框架回答。另外他还说 FTX 当年差点做成政治预测市场，并主张“取消美联储”。

6. 给 14 岁年轻人的建议
别再走华尔街“赚钱再捐赠”的老路；要么全力投身 AI 安全，要么去找 AI 能真正落地的自动化切口。

一句话评价：这场之所以火，一半是“14 岁采访狱中 SBF”的反差，另一半是内容确实密——SBF 把他那套期望值功利主义原封不动地又讲了一遍，监狱没改变他的思维方式，这是最值得看的地方。

其实这些正确的话，反而需要在特定条件下才能成立

以真正避免能够不吃高油、高糖、高盐的路径，反而是需要吃这些

怎么解释呢？就是力量训练和耐力训练

根据最基础的运动生理学，我们吃到糖尤其是游离糖，包括等渗溶液的葡萄糖是非常好的，能够扩充我们糖原的快速补充物质，这些是A类补充物质

因为力量训练之后，我们身体中的肌糖原被耗光，这个时候快速补充糖原，可以扩充我们的油箱，从而获得更多的超量储备，这个在运动员和一般的业余爱好者上面是在广泛使用的，无论是力量训练还是耐力训练

盐分就更不用说了，力量训练还好，耐力训练会流失大量的汗液，而那些汗液会带走我们的电解质，这个其中最重要的就是盐分，所以耐力训练，需要保持高盐饮食

力量训练也是如果你想要使用更大的力量，你就必须要提高神经募集程度，而神经需要最高的电解质就是盐分，所以保持高盐饮食对于力量训练是有好处的

当然了，这个过程中你需要喝大量的水。所以盐分和糖分在不运动的人那里是有害的，但是在专业运动甚至业余运动那里，它反而是必要的，是你进步的关键。并不是各种各样的补剂，那些可能只占百分之几甚至零点几。糖和盐才是最重要的补剂

你日常所喝的能量饮料，包括佳得乐，有大量的咖啡因，其实从长期来看对你的身体收益是不好的，是成负数的，它在短期是可以的，它相当于一个低倍的杠杆，因为会产生慢性肾上腺疲劳。但是糖和盐在饮料之中，尤其是盐是不能加那么多的，如果饮料加了很多的盐，你这个饮料的销量就不会好

至于油，我非常推荐长期是低脂低油的饮食。但是如果这样你就很难以吃够那么多的碳水和蛋白质，你可以尝试没有油的碳水和蛋白质，实际上是让你的食欲很差的，为了吃够那些，所以保持一个周期性的高油的饮食，反而能够让你长期坚持

text:
这是一则价值一万块钱的Claude封号测试经验贴。

这两周，在Claude封号上测试花了八千多块人民币，简单总结一下都做了哪些动作：

✅用了 Claude 的 Team 号，¥1,200。Team 号 Pro 就是 1.25x，Max 是 6.25x

❌自己礼品卡充值，iOS 充 Claude。其中一个是 Pro 升级 Max，700 人民币。升级失败，被 Claude 风控拦截，升级没成功，去苹果申请退款
退款后 Claude 变成 Free 了。再在电脑端登录的时候直接封号了，退款成功的礼品卡余额在号里面出不来，也花不了

❌礼品卡新号直充 Ultra，250 美金，合计 1650￥，遇到 72 小时拦截，等待中

❌开 infini card 官网直订，一个 Max 一个 Pro，合计 120 美金（算 800 人民币吧）。稳定使用了一天多，然后双双都弹了最高等级的组织验证，这个好像没有渠道能过

✅买了印尼的免 key Ultra 成品号，先是在 cage 里面用的。这个周末折腾了两天，把自己电脑的环境问题解决了，然后迁移到了电脑 Mac 的本地，目前仍在稳定使用

❌从推特上的大大小小几个店购买了号称是免 KYC 的Free号，然后进行充值测试……算了，这个不说了，说了会触及到好多人的利益，这个也有一两千了，没仔细算过

总结下来就是，环境真的特别特别重要，而且会连坐。

但这个连坐并不是大家理解的“如果我两个 Pro 号在本地，其中一个封了，另一个也会封吗？”，并不是。

比如说其中一个弹了 KYC 验证，那么赶紧把所有的账号先都清理掉吧，先别用了，你电脑的环境绝对出了问题

现在这成本全都是交的学费呀，说实话是有点心疼的，大概 10 天 8000 块钱，而且还有大量的时间成本都堆进去了。

而且昨天跟解决 Claude 封号环境的兄弟聊了之后，感觉自己现在也算是推特上没多少人比我更懂 Claude 封号了首先，他们不可能花了这么多钱去测试。

其次，我交流的这个兄弟绝对是目前 Claude 封号解决方案第一人，国内根本就没有他的同行，他甚至做出了一个完整的客户端给用户用

下面先将我这几天交的学费、拿到的猜想验证给大家说出来：

国内即使用 VPN，也是能够开出来免 K 号的。支付如果弹 K，就说明肯定有问题，只要弹 K 就是有问题的。

我最近也问了我几个在新加坡和美国的朋友，他们弹 K 的概率很小很小，封号的概率也很小很小。

弹 K 了，这个号说实话可以扔了，你电脑的环境该清理一下了。

text:
Only 1 of the 5 big US hyperscalers could cover its AI capex with the cash it brought in last quarter: 

Microsoft.

Amazon, Alphabet, Oracle and Meta spent over $50 BILLION more on capex than their businesses brought in, in just one quarter.

The gap for each:

1. Amazon: $34.8 BILLION
2. Alphabet: $9.1 BILLION
3. Oracle: $5.4 BILLION
4. Meta: $1.2 BILLION

Microsoft brought in $58.0 BILLION, spent $39.4 BILLION, and had $18.6 BILLION left over.

A gap like that has to be filled with savings, new debt or new shares.

Their borrowing has exploded. 

Hyperscalers have sold about $277 BILLION of bonds this year, versus under $50 BILLION a year from 2020 to 2024, per Fitch.

For some, it's a first. 

Alphabet just posted its first quarters of negative free cash flow since its 2004 IPO, and Meta its first since 2012.

The cost of that money is splitting the field. 

Microsoft just borrowed for 20 years at 6.15%. Oracle paid 8.65% for the same 20 years.

Fitch says the bond market's "capacity to absorb" this much hyperscaler debt is now being tested, with the market expecting capex to top $1 TRILLION next year.

text:
I made NFTs that leave you if you don't use them for what they're for.

They're called Wearers, 1,000 pixel ghosts on Robinhood Chain, and the one thing they ask is to be your profile picture on OpenSea. OpenSea lets you set an NFT from a verified collection as your account pfp and shows it in their API, so I wrote a keeper bot that reads that field for every holder once a day, at an hour it picks at random and keeps to itself until the round is over.

If you hold Wearers and none of them is your pfp, you're at risk. Each day the bot takes a fifth of those holders at random, and from each of them it moves one Wearer to a random holder who does wear theirs, by calling claim on the contract. If you wear even one, everything you hold is safe, and any day you might get another one for free. A Wearer that just changed hands gets 24 hours of grace so the new owner has time to put it on, and if OpenSea doesn't answer for someone that day, the bot just skips them.

The art lives fully onchain. Every Wearer is a 40 by 40 pixel image stored inside the contract along with its 12 traits, so there's no server or IPFS behind it, and the whole thing is a plain ERC721 minted through SeaDrop.

Mint is on November 24, 1,000 in total, one per wallet in each stage. Collectors go first at 12:00 UTC with 250 for free, then FCFS at 12:30 UTC with the next 250 for free, and whatever is left goes public at 13:00 UTC for 0.001 ETH.

If you collected anything of mine in the last six months and still hold it, you're already on the collectors list, and you can check it on the OpenSea mint page.

text:
Nigeria 2027 | Who gets left out when campaigns study only the votes cast?

When I look at a polling unit result, my first question is usually the one the result sheet cannot answer on its own. Who was missing?

On News Central’s Breakfast Xtra, Dr Delta Milayo Ndou, Executive Lead of the Political Campaign Resource Hub, discusses Nigeria’s missing voter and what voter mobilisation demands as the country looks ahead to 2027.

Think about two neighbours. One registered but did not vote in the last election. The other was eligible but never registered. Both were absent from the result. Yet a campaign that waits until election week to knock on their doors has already missed the opportunity to help one of them participate.

This is where data should change how campaigns work. Compare registration and turnout at polling unit level. Look for places where participation has fallen. Then take those findings back to the community and ask people what happened. A turnout figure can tell you how many registered voters stayed away. It takes a conversation to understand why.

There is a question I would put to every campaign team preparing for 2027. When you call a ward your stronghold, do you mean that most eligible citizens there support you, or that you won the largest share of votes among those who turned up?

Watch Dr Ndou’s discussion below. That distinction could change how you read Nigeria’s electoral map.

#Nigeria2027 #TheMissingVoter #DataDrivenCampaigns #VoterMobilisation  @ResourceHub_HQ @ICPCampaigns @MilayoNdou

事情是这样的，Tether 官方 2026 Q3 的储备报告里，储备总资产 1,914.51 亿，总负债 (基本都是 USDT 发行量) 1,834.96 亿，超额储备是 79.55 亿。

这 1,914 亿储备资产里，有 190.85 亿是实物黄金，83.67 亿是比特币。而从 9 月 30 号到现在，黄金跌了 -14.7% (对应跌去 28.05 亿)，还剩比特币跌了 -28.2% (对应跌去 23.60 亿)，一共跌掉 51.65 亿。

那么现在超额储备，就只剩 79.55 - 51.65 = 27.9 亿了。在黄金、BTC 剧烈波动的环境里，就显得不是很多了

如果以下三种情况发生，就会导致 USDT 的储备金不足 —— 至少根据审计报告是这样的

1/ 如果黄金不跌、只有 BTC 再跌 -46%
2/ 或者 BTC 不跌、黄金再跌 -17%
3/ 或者黄金和 BTC 同比例下跌 -12.5%

除非 Tehter 公司进行仓位调整或补充资本进来，才能化解这个风险

我不是说 Tether 一定有问题，毕竟它公开批露的信息有限，10 月 30 日发布的截至 9 月 30 日的这份 Q3 审计报告，已经过去一个多月了，中间是不是有储备金调整，我们现在是不知道的

text:
用 Tailscale 的朋友，建议都把 Tailnet Lock 打开。之间我分享过打开 ACL 增强安全性的技巧，后来发现不够。

配好 ACL 能防止某台机器被攻破后横向扩散，但还有一个口子。谁能进你的 tailnet，最终是 Tailscale 的协调服务器说了算。云端如果被攻破或者作恶，理论上可以悄悄塞一台假设备进来，其他设备会照单全收。

Tailnet Lock 补的就是这个口子。新设备必须由你指定的签名节点签名，每台设备在本地验签，签名无效就拒绝连接。签名私钥只在你自己的设备上，云端伪造不了。

开启前
新设备登录 → 云端分发公钥 → 其他设备直接接受 → 互通

开启后
新设备登录 → Locked out，等待签名
→ 签名节点签名 → 其他设备本地验签 → 通过才互通

开启很简单。在管理台 Device management 里点 Enable Tailnet Lock，选两台常用设备当签名节点，复制生成的 tailscale lock init 命令，在其中一台上运行。现有设备会自动签好。

初始化会生成一组 disablement secret，用来在出问题时关掉锁。一定要存进密码管理器，再留一份离线备份。丢了又没给官方留一份，锁就关不掉了。

开完之后，已有设备之间完全不受影响。新设备加入要先签名，在管理台点 Sign machine 就行。另外它和 Device approval 互斥，两个只能开一个。

ACL 管进来以后能访问什么，Tailnet Lock 管谁能进来。配了 ACL 的，顺手把这个也开了吧。

author: brucexu_eth
quoted_text:
直呼 Tailscale 牛逼！

现在我所有的服务器和设备都连到了 Tailscale，并且开启了 Tailscale SSH。之后我基本没再折腾过 Private Key，也不用到处同步 SSH key，每次直接 ssh root@tailscale-ip 就可以登录。

部署在某台服务器上的 Hermes，也可以通过 Tailscale 跨服务器做监控、服务部署和日常运维，非常方便。

但我最近意识到这里有一个风险：如果某个 Hermes 要给别人共用，或者部署在公网服务器上，未来真的被攻破了，在原来 allow-all 的网络策略下，攻击者就可能继续横向访问我其他的服务器，甚至是正在使用的个人电脑。

刚刚花了一点时间配置 Tailscale Access Control，就把这个问题解决了。

做法很直接：先用 tag 把设备分成 personal 和 public-server，然后分别配置网络 Grants 和 Tailscale SSH Policy。

我这次直接给 Hermes 创建了一个临时的 scoped OAuth client，让它读取并备份原来的 policy、生成新规则、调用 Tailscale API 验证，然后提交配置，最后再从两个方向做真实连接测试。如果手动配置也不麻烦，核心就是写清楚两个 tag 之间谁可以主动访问谁。

我目前的规则是：

- personal 设备之间可以相互连接和 SSH
- personal 可以连接 public server
- public server 不能反向连接 personal
- public server 之间也不能横向连接

过程中还踩了一个坑：Tailscale 的网络 Grants 和 Tailscale SSH 是两层权限。网络已经通了，不代表 SSH 一定能登录，两边都需要配置。

这样一来，我内网服务器上部署的 Hermes 仍然可以作为管理节点和跳板机，控制其他服务器；但部署在公网的 Hermes 即使出现问题，影响范围也会被限制在外面，不会通过 Tailnet 继续横向扩散。

太牛逼了。以前这种内网管理、身份认证和权限隔离，通常都是大公司才会认真搭建的基础设施。现在 Tailscale 直接把它下放到了个人，而且免费就能用。

没用的赶紧用起来！

quoted_text:
My last day at NVIDIA, with warmth to carry forward

Yesterday was my last day at NVIDIA. I returned my equipment and badge, signed the paperwork, and just like that, it was done. It all happened so quickly and simply that it still feels a little unreal.

There were a few things I didn’t get to finish. My account access ended around noon—I’d expected to have until the end of the day, or at least until after signing the paperwork. Some goodbyes were left mid-conversation. I missed the chance to pick up a few keepsakes from the Gear Store. I didn’t even get to send the handover document I was halfway through writing.

Fortunately, I had already sent my farewell email and said goodbye to some friends. To anyone I didn’t get to reach, or suddenly stopped replying to: I’m sorry. I hope we can pick up those conversations outside work.

That evening, my colleagues threw me a farewell party, and for a little while, goodbye could take its time. We talked about everything that had happened recently, how life had been treating us, and what we hoped the future might hold. Thank you for giving me one more evening to remember—and so much warmth to carry into whatever comes next.

I’m leaving with a few unfinished things, but so many memories to keep. Wishing you all happiness, work you’re proud of, and good things ahead.

I’ll miss you, friends. Until our paths cross again.

The question now is whether political and Silicon Valley pressure can change the board’s decision or whether Jensen Huang’s time at NVIDIA is permanently over.

Jensen Huang: I’m stepping down.

TSMC: Alright, gentlemen. Let’s see the cash first. LMAO.

November 2026: The latest developments in the AI semiconductor industry.

NVIDIA: Gentlemen, Jensen Huang is gone.

Wall Street: Yeah, we know.

TSM: But hold on. Before you place your next orders, let’s talk.

ASIC companies: What?

TSMC: From now on, we’ll be reviewing your financial health before accepting orders.

ASIC companies: What?

TSMC: Orders exceeding your credit limits will require cash upfront.

ASIC companies: Come on, the AI industry is BOOMING right now!

TSMC: Uh-huh.

ASIC companies: Then give us more capacity!

TSMC: Sure. First, show me your bank balance.

ASIC companies: LMAOOOO.

Meanwhile, at MediaTek, GUC, and Alchip…

MediaTek: We just raised $3.9 billion overseas.

TSMC: Oh, interesting.

MediaTek: NVIDIA subscribed for $3.5 billion of it.

TSMC: Now that’s reassuring.

GUC: We’re preparing convertible bonds and bank financing too.

Alchip: We’re also raising capital overseas.

TSMC: So everyone is raising cash first?

ASIC companies: Wait, weren’t you the one asking us to show you the cash?

TSMC: HAHAHAHAHA.

Meanwhile, inside the AI circular financing machine…

NVIDIA: I’ll invest in AI companies.

AI company: Thank you!

AI company: We’ll use that money to buy GPUs.

NVIDIA: Thank you, customer!

Cloud provider: We’ll use those GPUs to build data centers and generate revenue.

Banks: Great. We’ll finance your expansion.

TSMC: But when will the end customers actually pay?

Cloud provider: With future AI revenue!

TSMC: No, no. I mean NOW.

Cloud provider: …

TSMC: Gentlemen, why is all the money always in the future? HAHAHA.

Then suddenly, Morris Chang walks in.

Morris Chang: Where’s Jensen?

NVIDIA: He stepped down.

Morris Chang: That kid…

Wall Street: You two go way back, right?

Morris Chang: Back in 2013, I actually considered him for the CEO position at TSMC.

Wall Street: WHAT? HAHAHA.

Morris Chang: But he said he still had unfinished business and turned it down.

Wall Street: Wait. The guy who turned down the TSMC CEO job went on to build NVIDIA into a global AI powerhouse?

Morris Chang: Exactly.

ASIC company: Sir, if Jensen were still around, would you give us a bigger credit limit?

TSMC: I have no idea.

According to reports, TSMC is becoming more cautious about capacity allocation, examining customers’ financial stability and even the actual construction progress of their data centers.

Some customers reportedly need to make advance payments to secure capacity, while orders exceeding credit limits may require additional cash payments.

Until now, the AI industry has largely operated through an enormous financing cycle:

Investment → GPU purchases → Data center construction → Future computing revenue.

Within this ecosystem, Jensen Huang may have been more than just a CEO. He was one of the key figures connecting investors, customers, and the entire supply chain.

Of course, there is currently no established evidence that Jensen’s departure has anything to do with TSMC tightening its credit policies.

But here’s my personal speculation:

If Jensen was one of the central gears keeping the AI financial ecosystem moving, perhaps the market will eventually have to answer a much simpler question:

Which companies actually have the cash flow to pay for all this AI infrastructure?

Jensen Huang: Believe in the future of AI.

TSMC: We do.

Jensen Huang: Then give me more capacity!

TSMC: Sure. Pay the deposit first.

Wall Street: Wait. If everyone believes in the future, why do you need the money NOW?

TSMC: Because the future is the future. Credit bills are due TODAY. HAHAHAHAHA.

THE TRILLION DOLLAR LOSS FOR AMERICAN COMPANIES AND THE DEFENESTRATION OF JENSEN HUANG

China was always going to build its own full AI tech stack. But the aggressive US national security state put Beijing's plans on a Manhattan Project footing, speeding them up by as much as a decade.

    •    The cost: Nvidia and its GPU and data centre suppliers, many of them Taiwanese, now face more than $1 trillion in lost revenue.

    •    The bigger loss: China is off the Western tech stack and heading for 100% self-reliance. – Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu says China's compute shortage is mainly a 2027–2028 problem, and that it will be nearly 100% self-sufficient by 2029. – Given the current progress, that's hard to dismiss.

    •    We've seen this before with Cisco: – After the Snowden leaks, Beijing concluded that Cisco routers were backdoored by US intelligence. – It shut Cisco out and built up a domestic champion you may have heard of: Huawei, now a global giant. – Huawei's 2025 revenue was $126B. Cisco's fiscal 2026 revenue was $63.3B. That's roughly double. – Who's talking about Cisco nowadays? – That cost Cisco and its shareholders hundreds of billions.

    •   The Rubicon is crossed: American AI will eventually be isolated to the United States and Europe. – Most of the rest of the world will revolve around cheaper options out of China.

    •    Loss of American competitiveness and tax revenue: America struggles with a massive trade imbalance with China. – How do you close that gap when you're not allowed to sell your most advanced products into the world's largest market? – The United States will never close the trade gap by only selling soybeans.

    •    The real danger is to Taiwan: – Taiwan sees its lead in GPU foundry work, plus its whole ecosystem from server racks to optical transceivers, as its turtle shell. – As the mainland's stack grows and spreads globally, that shell gets thinner, and Taiwan matters less and less over time.

    •    The defenestration of Jensen Huang: Jensen had an incentive to keep mainland China on a Taiwanese and American tech stack. – He is one of the most important people, if not the most important, in building the American AI empire into what it is today: number one. – For his troubles, he was publicly defenestrated by the national security state. – No good deed goes unpunished.

模型一个接一个发，又多又牛就算了，转头还免费放出一门近 2 小时的 Harness 工程完整课，直接教你从零搭一套会 7×24 自己进化的 Agent 系统！！！

   说实话，现在还有大把人在那天天追新模型、到处复制粘贴 Prompt，结果连模型堆得最猛的 Google 都直接摊牌了：同一个模型，外层套的 Harness

text:
No es cierto. El dato de "100% durante 36 meses" distorsiona cifras de 2006-2008 sobre un tipo muy específico: overfallsvoldtekter (violaciones por asalto en la calle por desconocidos). Entonces hubo 41 casos en Oslo, todos por inmigrantes no occidentales, pero no cubría el total de agresiones sexuales.

Según SSB (2020-2023), los inmigrantes representan solo el 12% de las siktelser por delitos sexuales en Noruega (son ~18% de la población). Hay sobre-representación en otros delitos, especialmente violencia entre jóvenes de ciertos orígenes en Oslo, pero no el 100% en agresiones sexuales.

text:
Out of everything posted about FSD v15 so far, one line from @elonmusk deserves way more attention than it's getting: "This is real-time AI video generation (no gaming engine!) using just half of one AI4 TRIP accelerator. Let that sink in …" 🔥

Half of one accelerator is the part worth sitting with. Once you see the numbers behind it, Reality View stops looking like a fancy new screen and starts looking like one of the most impressive things Tesla has ever shipped.

🎬 THE SCREEN IS NOW GENERATED LIVE

For years, FSD's screen worked like a video game. Software took a list of what the car detected and dropped stock 3D models in the right spots: a gray car here, a lane line there.

Reality View tosses that playbook out the window. The car's AI now generates the video itself, frame after frame, as you drive, with no game engine anywhere in the loop.

Better yet, the picture comes from the same end-to-end model that's doing the driving. That's the single neural network that turns camera video into steering and braking, and now it paints your screen, too.

⚙️ WHAT A TRIP ACTUALLY IS

The standard AI4 computer carries two self-driving chips, and each chip packs three custom neural processors Tesla calls TRIP accelerators. That's six in all.

And that's where Reality View gets made: right on the self-driving computer, instead of the infotainment chip that runs your maps and music.

Each TRIP is basically an arena packed with tiny calculators, all cranking through the multiply-and-add math that neural networks run on. Teardowns count 9,216 of them per TRIP, lined up in a 96-by-96 grid and firing 2.2 billion times a second.

Each calculator handles two operations per tick, so one TRIP works out to 9,216 × 2 × 2.2 billion, or roughly 40 trillion operations every second.

Half of one comes to about 20 trillion, roughly a twelfth of the whole computer's neural muscle.

📏 WHY THAT NUMBER IS RIDICULOUS

Twenty trillion operations per second sounds enormous, until you see what else runs on that kind of budget.

The Neural Engine inside Apple's iPhone 15 Pro is rated at 35 trillion operations per second. So on paper, the slice of compute painting Reality View has less raw AI muscle than the AI chip in a 2023 phone.

Companies don't all count these numbers the same way, so it's a ballpark, but it shows just how little compute this is.

At the other end of the scale sits Nvidia's H100, one of the data-center workhorses powering today's AI boom. It's rated at about 1,979 trillion 8-bit operations per second in its standard mode, the same kind of math a TRIP runs, which puts half a TRIP at roughly 1% of one H100.

That gap matters because AI video is one of the toughest jobs in AI. Many AI video generators still take minutes to produce a single clip, as the researchers behind the real-time system MotionStream point out.

Even MotionStream, built specifically for speed, streams roughly 17 to 29 frames per second at 480p, and about 10 at 720p, while eating up an entire H100.

Meanwhile, Tesla is streaming a live, photorealistic view of the real road on roughly 1% of that chip's rated power, inside a moving car.

In other words, Reality View runs on less compute than a phone's AI chip, inside a computer whose main job is driving.

There's a fair asterisk here. Those research models dream up whole scenes from a prompt or a single image, while Tesla's renderer starts with a driving brain that already knows exactly what's around the car. Tesla also hasn't shared the view's resolution or frame rate.

And even on the most generous estimates of AI4's power, half a TRIP still works out to only about 2% of one H100.

Either way, live generated video on a sliver of a car computer would have sounded like science fiction not long ago.

🔍 HOW IT CAN BE THIS CHEAP

Tesla hasn't spelled out how it works, but it has left plenty of breadcrumbs.

FSD's network has been building its own 3D picture of the world for a while now, something Tesla showed off at the ICCV conference in October 2025. That picture includes 3D Gaussians, millions of soft little blobs of color that can rebuild a scene you can view from any angle.

Tesla also built its own Gaussian splatting system that can rebuild a scene from the car's cameras in a fraction of a second.

Reality View streams its picture from a virtual camera that can sit anywhere above the car, and showing a scene from an angle no real camera has is exactly what those 3D blobs are great at.

Even Elon seems to like that theory: he called a description of Reality View as a neural, Gaussian-splat digital twin "pretty accurate", and it lines up with every other clue.

If that's the trick, the hard part is done before the screen ever needs a picture. The driving brain understands the scene, and the visualization just paints what it already knows.

That would explain the other shocker. Reality View swapped every separate signal behind the old screen for one end-to-end visualization, and it still uses less compute than the bare-bones 2020 visualization did.

🚗 WHY TESLA CARES SO MUCH

v15 is Tesla's large model, built to squeeze every ounce of performance out of HW4. On a chip working that hard, a screen that costs half of one TRIP leaves nearly everything else for the driving.

And it's a flex, too. The AI4 computer costs about $650 by Elon's own figure, and that same box now drives the car and paints live video of the world at the same time.

This is only the start. Elon says Tesla vehicles will share traffic knowledge and combine it with Grok's real-time 𝕏 feed, even giving you a heads-up about what's happening at your destination.

A view this cheap to generate is the perfect canvas for that kind of shared knowledge.

Elon asked everyone to let that sink in, and the math earns it: half of one accelerator in a $650 computer is painting the real world live while FSD drives.

“We probably spent about three months before we actually shipped Creator Awards, just refining the algorithm and the criteria to figure out the best way to bring positive value to the social network. For us, we do it quite differently than everybody else, it's not just about, 'Hey, here's this token, buy it, and if you buy it, I make money.'”

朱祁钰断气的时候，宫中消息含糊不清，执笔修史的人下笔十分谨慎，正史只记载他薨于西内，却不写明病状，明代朝野私下议论纷纷，这是一桩被刻意淡化、埋没在夺门之变里的帝王死亡疑案。景泰八年正月，石亨、徐有贞发动夺门之变，明英宗复位，当天就把已经重病的景泰帝朱祁钰迁到西内永安宫软禁。短短一个多月之后，二月十九，朱祁钰离世，年仅三十岁。《明实录》只轻描淡写记录 “帝薨”，定性为久病不治，草草收尾，连详细脉案、诊疗记录都没有留存下来。

风声压不住，当时就有两种声音。一种说法是朱祁钰本就身患重疾，重病缠身，政变之后经受巨大打击，病情恶化自然死去；另一种流传更广的说法，是英宗授意宦官，将其加害。陆釴《病逸漫记》直接记载，景泰帝是被太监蒋安以帛勒毙，这个说法在明代私家笔记里反复出现。

后世比对《明英宗实录》、同时代文人的私人记载，不难发现多处反常：朱祁钰之前虽然患病，原本已有好转，甚至朝臣还在商议太子的事，夺门之后骤然急转直下；而且英宗复位之后，对景泰帝的处置处处带着清算意味，废其帝号，降为郕王，不允许葬入预先修好的寿陵，以亲王礼草草安葬西山。可同样没有直接物证坐实刺杀，实录被英宗朝史官修改润色，有利的证词和细节大多被删削，真相卡在文字缝隙里。

争论的内核，从来不止是一病一杀的区别。土木堡巨变，大明濒临倾覆，是朱祁钰临危接过烂摊子，守住北京，稳住王朝。可他贪恋权位，囚禁英宗、废掉原先的太子，兄弟之间积怨早已深重。英宗复辟，心头最大的隐患，就是这个曾经坐拥皇权的弟弟。就算朱祁钰原本病重，英宗也有足够动机，杜绝他再度翻盘的可能。执笔史官、宫中内侍，身处新旧皇权交替的漩涡，不敢直书宫闱秘事，只能顺从当朝的口径，模糊死因。

病痛能够消磨肉身，皇权手里的笔，更能过滤掉所有刺眼的疑点。他临危受命扛起江山，力挽狂澜保住大明，到头来，兄弟反目，帝位被夺，连死亡的缘由，都被史书轻轻盖过。几百年过去，案卷尚存，西内冷清宫室里的杀机或是绝望，一个救时君主惨淡的结局，一直藏在史料缝隙之中。

我们反复辨析景泰帝之死的记载，终究看清一件事：皇权之争面前，曾经的帝王，连死亡的真相，都可以被裁剪成胜利者想要世人看见的模样。

text:
Out of everything posted about FSD v15 so far, one line from @elonmusk deserves way more attention than it's getting: "This is real-time AI video generation (no gaming engine!) using just half of one AI4 TRIP accelerator. Let that sink in …" 🔥

Half of one accelerator is the part worth sitting with. Once you see the numbers behind it, Reality View stops looking like a fancy new screen and starts looking like one of the most impressive things Tesla has ever shipped.

🎬 THE SCREEN IS NOW GENERATED LIVE

For years, FSD's screen worked like a video game. Software took a list of what the car detected and dropped stock 3D models in the right spots: a gray car here, a lane line there.

Reality View tosses that playbook out the window. The car's AI now generates the video itself, frame after frame, as you drive, with no game engine anywhere in the loop.

Better yet, the picture comes from the same end-to-end model that's doing the driving. That's the single neural network that turns camera video into steering and braking, and now it paints your screen, too.

⚙️ WHAT A TRIP ACTUALLY IS

The standard AI4 computer carries two self-driving chips, and each chip packs three custom neural processors Tesla calls TRIP accelerators. That's six in all.

And that's where Reality View gets made: right on the self-driving computer, instead of the infotainment chip that runs your maps and music.

Each TRIP is basically an arena packed with tiny calculators, all cranking through the multiply-and-add math that neural networks run on. Teardowns count 9,216 of them per TRIP, lined up in a 96-by-96 grid and firing 2.2 billion times a second.

Each calculator handles two operations per tick, so one TRIP works out to 9,216 × 2 × 2.2 billion, or roughly 40 trillion operations every second.

Half of one comes to about 20 trillion, roughly a twelfth of the whole computer's neural muscle.

📏 WHY THAT NUMBER IS RIDICULOUS

Twenty trillion operations per second sounds enormous, until you see what else runs on that kind of budget.

The Neural Engine inside Apple's iPhone 15 Pro is rated at 35 trillion operations per second. So on paper, the slice of compute painting Reality View has less raw AI muscle than the AI chip in a 2023 phone.

Companies don't all count these numbers the same way, so it's a ballpark, but it shows just how little compute this is.

At the other end of the scale sits Nvidia's H100, one of the data-center workhorses powering today's AI boom. It's rated at about 1,979 trillion 8-bit operations per second in its standard mode, the same kind of math a TRIP runs, which puts half a TRIP at roughly 1% of one H100.

That gap matters because AI video is one of the toughest jobs in AI. Many AI video generators still take minutes to produce a single clip, as the researchers behind the real-time system MotionStream point out.

Even MotionStream, built specifically for speed, streams roughly 17 to 29 frames per second at 480p, and about 10 at 720p, while eating up an entire H100.

Meanwhile, Tesla is streaming a live, photorealistic view of the real road on roughly 1% of that chip's rated power, inside a moving car.

In other words, Reality View runs on less compute than a phone's AI chip, inside a computer whose main job is driving.

There's a fair asterisk here. Those research models dream up whole scenes from a prompt or a single image, while Tesla's renderer starts with a driving brain that already knows exactly what's around the car. Tesla also hasn't shared the view's resolution or frame rate.

And even on the most generous estimates of AI4's power, half a TRIP still works out to only about 2% of one H100.

Either way, live generated video on a sliver of a car computer would have sounded like science fiction not long ago.

🔍 HOW IT CAN BE THIS CHEAP

Tesla hasn't spelled out how it works, but it has left plenty of breadcrumbs.

FSD's network has been building its own 3D picture of the world for a while now, something Tesla showed off at the ICCV conference in October 2025. That picture includes 3D Gaussians, millions of soft little blobs of color that can rebuild a scene you can view from any angle.

Tesla also built its own Gaussian splatting system that can rebuild a scene from the car's cameras in a fraction of a second.

Reality View streams its picture from a virtual camera that can sit anywhere above the car, and showing a scene from an angle no real camera has is exactly what those 3D blobs are great at.

Even Elon seems to like that theory: he called a description of Reality View as a neural, Gaussian-splat digital twin "pretty accurate", and it lines up with every other clue.

If that's the trick, the hard part is done before the screen ever needs a picture. The driving brain understands the scene, and the visualization just paints what it already knows.

That would explain the other shocker. Reality View swapped every separate signal behind the old screen for one end-to-end visualization, and it still uses less compute than the bare-bones 2020 visualization did.

🚗 WHY TESLA CARES SO MUCH

v15 is Tesla's large model, built to squeeze every ounce of performance out of HW4. On a chip working that hard, a screen that costs half of one TRIP leaves nearly everything else for the driving.

And it's a flex, too. The AI4 computer costs about $650 by Elon's own figure, and that same box now drives the car and paints live video of the world at the same time.

This is only the start. Elon says Tesla vehicles will share traffic knowledge and combine it with Grok's real-time 𝕏 feed, even giving you a heads-up about what's happening at your destination.

A view this cheap to generate is the perfect canvas for that kind of shared knowledge.

Elon asked everyone to let that sink in, and the math earns it: half of one accelerator in a $650 computer is painting the real world live while FSD drives.

Jensen Huang says he approaches almost everything by asking how hard it can be, and traces the habit to his mother teaching him English from a dictionary

He said it at the Cambridge Union in November 2025, when he received the Stephen Hawking Fellowship.

"I approach almost everything from the perspective of, How hard can it be?"

What he described:
- his mother spoke only Taiwanese Hokkien, and used "a piece of paper and a dictionary" to teach him English before he moved to the US at 9
- he says that lesson defines Nvidia and defines him
- he applied the same mindset to jobs he had never done, such as being a first-time CEO, raising money for Nvidia and writing a business plan
- his method is to break each problem down to first principles and learn along the way

text:
Imagine creating a crypto token that goes from $0.17 to $460, taking $2.4B from investors in 95 countries and disappearing without spending a single day in prison.

That’s what happened to Satish Kumbhani

the founder of BitConnect, one of the biggest Ponzi schemes in history.

Satish was born in Gujarat, India, and in February 2016 he launched his own cryptocurrency called BitConnect ($BCC)

The idea behind BitConnect was quite simple, you deposited Bitcoin on the platform, exchanged it for BCC and lent those tokens back to BitConnect in exchange for daily returns.

The company said to have developed a trading bot and a volatility software capable of generating returns of up to 1% a day and 40% a month.

(Keep in mind that a 1% daily compounded return would turn $10,000 into $378,000 in a year)

Obviously, there was no trading bot generating those returns. 

The money coming from new investors was being used to pay existing investors.

What made BitConnect grow so quickly was its referral program, which incentivized thousands of YouTubers and influencers to promote the platform in exchange for commissions.

In October 2017, BitConnect held its annual event in Thailand, where Carlos Matos gave us what is probably one of the most iconic videos in crypto history.

By the end of 2017, BitConnect reached a $3.4B market cap

But all exploded in January 2018.

After receiving cease-and-desist orders from US state regulators, BitConnect announced on January 16 that it was shutting down its lending platform

The company announced that everyone’s outstanding loans would be repaid in BCC at a valuation of $363.62 per token.

BCC eventually went below $1.

It wasn’t until September 2021 that the SEC filed its lawsuit against BitConnect, Kumbhani and its main US promoter, Glenn Arcaro.

In February 2022, Kumbhani was indicted on five criminal charges carrying a potential maximum sentence of 70 years in prison.

But nobody could find him.

text:
i'm planning a trip to the caribbean and it brought back memories. my team asked if i'd ever been, so i dug up some pics.

april 2011. i was 20, on my first proper sailing trip, a dream i'd had since i was a kid reading about the spanish armada, hornblower, pirates and other sailors rounding cape horn and battling the seas. the captain had been my dad's best friend since childhood. on board were the captain, his wife + her daughter, captains other side chick, my brother and me. my dad was originally invited but he declined and extended the invitation to us. he said he wanted us to experience a lifetime memory, he had already seen the world.

one afternoon the sky turned dark grey. i counted about twenty boats turning around and heading for the nearest harbour. i mentioned it to the captain. confident and slightly drunk, he told me he'd sailed these waters twenty times and knew what he was doing.

i was skeptical. very. but i was twenty and living my childhood dream, so i embraced the obvious danger. while the women turned blue and went below deck, i was loving the wind and the salt water in my hair.

then the storm hit. the mainsail tore loose and flapped free in the wind. we couldn't steer anymore.

the captain looked around the boat and his eyes landed on me. i was skinny enough to be winched up the mast by hand in a bosun's chair. so up i went, with the boat thrashing in the waves. my brother was cranking the winch, until halfway up he started puking. there i was, dangling halfway up a mast in a caribbean storm, hugging it for dear life and questioning every decision i'd ever made.

my brother got his shit together and pulled me the rest of the way. i tied the sail down in storm winds, somehow, and climbed down like a monkey. all i got was a little nod from the captain. i felt like i'd saved all our lives.

nobody said much after the storm. that night we went into town for a couple of beers and stumbled into a local carnival, the only pale foreigners there. the community took us in right away. music playing, everyone in a great mood, and two women came over and started twerking on my brother and me.

like so often in my life, i had no idea how i'd ended up there. but it felt good, so i went with the flow.

on the dinghy back to the boat, the captain turned to me and said: "i'm jealous of your life. i used to be like you. now all women see when they look at me is an old man."
