text:
You need to hear my return from London story:

I was still not 100% adjusted so I wake up at 3ish am and start just texting my mother. Yes my mother. 

Around 4 am she tells me get some sleep. I said you're so right. I try to sleep. I can't.

It's 7am, I still can't sleep. I have my return flight at 3PM. I started to get paranoid.

I'm so tired if I sleep, I think I will sleep through my alarm and I'll be stuck in London forever. 

We need to pack NOW!! 

So I get up, and almost die.
Omg. I'm hungover. I can barley move. How are we gonna pack?

So I start picking up everything and just THROWING it into the bag.

It became a fking MOUNTAIN of clothes. 
I'm telling you it was a mountain. 

I have no idea how im gonna close this suitcase. 

So I lay on it and it's not even close to closing and I just say okay. This is not an option. I need to figure something out.

A brilliant thought hit me that would curse me later

Wear all your biggest, warmest stuff, and it will make space. 

Sure enough. It worked (after leaving some stuff behind on purpose as well, some of which I have still to discover because I was hungover full of anxiety thinking im gonna miss my flight in 8 hours, this is happening early in the morning remember?!).

Important pre story:
On the way here, I had to take out my laptop from my suitcase. I did not remember I put it in their but I was using a gift bag, those paper bags you get from buying nice things to hold it. I only bought a cologne, but it was a perfect bag on the way there.

In this scenario I had to open my suitcase in front of everyone but only just a bit, stick just enough that my hand can get through and pull out the laptop in front of everyone , and try to close it again. 

The issue became, now I had a fully exposed laptop. 

I bought a cologne and it coincedently came with a strong paper bag that could perfectly fit my laptop. To me, this is God at work, making everything easy for me. Life always works like this to me, thank you God.

I was asleep when I got on the flight to London, when I woke up on that flight, the bag looked like I got into a fight with it, torn and abused. 

This bag now, cannot be trusted. It's 75% ripped and my laptop will fall. It will not last the way back, I'm sure of it.

This makes me even more paranoid. My suitcase, the exposed laptop, I must get to this airport EARLY.

So I check in like 8 hours way too early. 

I find a place with laptop bags. their cheapest one was 185 british pounds, for the ugliest mfr ive ever seen. Whatever.

A hangover from hell, just wanting to be home, I rather die than carry anything. 

but I look around, and I'm so early my flight isn't even showing on the boards. This makes me freak out even more.

I thought flights always show up on the boards (I'm never this early)... Am I in the right place? 

How did everyone let me through just scanning tickets and telling me to go here? Who took my luggage! If it's not on the boards with every flight, where will it go? 

I assume my luggage is lost forever. 

I cannot do anything about that now. 

Grok started here. I said what is going to happen, did I just lose my luggage and I can't even find my flight on the board.

It assures me i'm fine and this is normal, I just showed up too early, and that luggage is done from some automatic conveyor belt thingies and it's coming. 

I don't believe it, but now I'm still not convinced grok is right about the boarding.

so every 10-30 minutes now, I can't even relax.

 Will my flight show up on the boards? Am I in the right area? and again, how did anyone let me into this place!!

I think about having a drink but no, I know at this point I'm so lost even a single drink will make sure I am stuck in London forever. 

Eventually, the flight shows up on the board. I am saved. 

Now remember, I'm in all my biggest warmest stuff. At this point I am not sweating at all. And I smell good. 

I board my flight and what seemed like a genius idea at the time (the giant jackets/sweater/sweatpants), becomes a very bad idea, very quickly:

- I start sweating within the first 10 minutes
- I start getting my stomach rumbling within the first 10 minutes but its nothing for now 

Eventually my stomach starts getting worse and worse. It's diarrhea.

My entire flight turned into me sweating for 10 hours straight due to what i'm wearing, and spending half the flight on the toilet which I had to get someone to move everytime I wanted to go. 

I'm sorry whoever that was. 
He's endured 10 hours of my sweat and bathroom breaks the flight as well. 

I'm still not home. Layover.

You see, when I was headed to London, I noticed this layover. I do not do layovers.

I had a plan, in London, fix/upgrade the seats, worst case I stay a day longer.

I forgot I had that plan and my flight just landed somewhere that isn't my home.

So I get off the plane, get my luggage, and do my first ever layover. Which includes exiting the airport.

I am on the streets now and have no idea where to go, and Grok comes in and starts location tracking me telling me if I'm walking in the right direction or not.

Grok literally saved my life. 

I was ready to give up and just call an uber to drive however long it would've taken, anything but another plane.

I end up getting my bags rechecked, finding the terminal, and we have a delay. Then another delay. 

Now also smelling like raw dumpster after sweating and sh*tting for 10 hours. 

The return flight eventually gets here, and it's pretty empty. I get a seat by myself by the grace of God.

I tell Grok to book me the nearest hotel, I need rest. 

I get to this hotel and maybe have 2 hours sleep because now I'm on different timezones, after time traveling and this is the time I'd normally be up. 

Get an Uber at like 6-7am and I'm finally on the ride home. My house is a little over 2 hours from the airport.

I didn't look at the type of car. 
The UBER shows up in a Tesla. 

I never considered this. His first words were "I'm surprised you accepted a Tesla" 

idkk why he would say this such thing, teslas are nice I like them.

Halfway home he says why, it needs to recharge. 

This recharge took us off the quick path home and adds another hour + 30mins. 

Everything on the way home was cursed. 

The trip was worth it and amazing 10/10.

Missing things I'm sure, but I made it.
Alive, but barely. 

Now it's 5am and my sleep schedule is still on Londons time zone but we'll deal with that later. 

attached is the bag before I got in a fight with it headed into London. And my mothers texts, and groks reply to yall.

Lets do it again.

Alright I’m getting tired of the 6.2 hate

Here’s my take:
1. It is a very very smart model 

2. It is a “trees” model in that it prefers detail and obsessive proof of everything
 
3. Makes sense! This is the Navier-Stokes model 

4. It is hella token efficient and that matters for us (and for OAI, which is back to being compute starved) 

5. It is quite bad at writing for people and that is half of why people hate it 

6. As a “trees” model it codes “trees” shaped stuff really well—but not “forest” shaped eng problems. This is the other half of why people hate it 

7. It is very good at talking to other agents—inverse of talking to people. High info density, obsessed with verification 

What do we learn from the hate? 

Most people dumb down intelligence not shaped like their brains, or intelligence with a bad human interface. See Orcas, octopi, sperm whales etc

Or in math words: 

If Intelligence in a model is X shape in an n-dimensional hyper sphere, 

And human brains are Y shape

Then humans judge X by the intersection with Y only—because we model intelligence as ourselves instead of as its true hyper-dimensional shape 

And yes I used em dashes before it was cool 😉

Avrupa neden geriliyor? Size bir örnek vereyim: 2026 yılında Carmine Paolino adında bir girişimci, Almanya'da şirket kurmaya karar veriyor. Adamın müşterileri hazır. Yapacağı iş belli. Hatta çalışmaya bile başlamış. Ama şirketin resmi işlemleri bir türlü tamamlanmıyor. Avukatla görüşüyor, notere gidiyor, mahkemeden belge bekliyor, muhasebeci tutuyor.

Aradan beş ay geçiyor. Bu süre içerisinde yaklaşık 9.600 avro harcıyor ama yurt dışındaki müşterilerine vergi numarasıyla fatura gönderemiyor.

Hatta kendi anlatımına göre, kendisine hizmet veren herkes parasını almış ama kendisi müşterilerinden parasını alamamış.

Vergi numarası 203 gün sonra geliyor. İlk uluslararası faturalarını gönderebilmesi ise şirket kurma işlemlerine başlamasından 229 gün sonrasını buluyor.

2019 yılında Tesla, Almanya’da fabrika kurmaya karar veriyor.
Berlin yakınlarında bir arazi seçiliyor. Burada elektrikli otomobil üretecekler. Binlerce insan çalışacak ve milyarlarca dolarlık yatırım yapılacak.
Ama fabrika kurulmaya başlayınca Alman bürokrasisiyle ilgili sorunlar yaşıyorlar.

Tesla’nın inşaata devam edebilmek için bazı geçici izinleri var. Fakat fabrikanın tamamen faaliyete geçebilmesi için gerekli izinler bir türlü tamamlanmıyor.

Hatta şirket 2021 yılında Alman makamlarına bir mektup gönderiyor.

Mektupta, izin başvurusunun üzerinden 16 ay geçmesine rağmen nihai iznin ne zaman verileceğinin bile belli olmadığını söylüyorlar.

Elon Musk da aynı yıl Almanya’ya gidiyor.

Gazeteciler kendisine fabrikanın ne zaman açılacağını sorunca bürokrasiden şikayet ediyor.

Almanya’da çok fazla kural olduğunu, sürekli yeni kurallar getirildiğini ama eskilerinin kaldırılmadığını anlatıyor.

Hatta böyle devam ederse zamanla hiçbir şey yapılamayacak hâle gelineceğini söylüyor.

Fabrikanın izni, ilk izin başvurusunun üzerinden yaklaşık iki yıl sonra çıkıyor.

2025 yılında Nvidia’nın CEO’su Jensen Huang, Fransa Cumhurbaşkanı Emmanuel Macron’un düzenlediği bir akşam yemeğine katılıyor.

Konu yapay zeka yatırımlarına geliyor.

Huang, Avrupalı yöneticilere dönüp Avrupa’nın ve Fransa’nın çok yavaş hareket ettiğini söylüyor.

Bunu da toplantıya katılan bir Fransız girişimci daha sonra gazetecilere anlatıyor.

Hatta aynı yıl Fransa Cumhurbaşkanı Macron da Avrupa’daki işlemlerin çok yavaş ilerlediğini kabul ediyor.

Mesela çip fabrikalarının kurulmasıyla ilgili 2026 yılında yayımlanan bir araştırmada:

Tayvan’da bir çip fabrikasının izin ve tasarım aşamasından üretime başlamasına kadar geçen süre yaklaşık 19 ay.

Singapur’da 23 ay.

Avrupa’da ise 34 ay.

Yani Tayvan’daki bir şirket üretime başlamışken Avrupa’daki rakibi hâlâ fabrikanın inşaatıyla uğraşıyor olabilir.

Bir zamanlar Avrupa dünyanın en büyük sanayi merkezlerinden biriydi.

Almanlar otomobil, Fransızlar uçak, İtalyanlar makine üretiyordu. Çinli şirketler de Avrupa’ya gidip bu teknolojileri öğrenmeye çalışıyordu.

Asya bu işleri zamanla öğrendi; düşük maliyet, ucuz işçilik, ucuz enerji ve hızlı karar alması sayesinde birçok sektörde üstünlük kurmaya başladı…

Avrupa’nın bundan 30 yıl önceki en büyük avantajı, karşısında bugünkü kadar güçlü bir Çin’in olmamasıydı. Kaliteli ürünler üretiyorlardı, dünyaya satıyorlardı. İşlerin yavaş ilerlemesi de pek sorun olmuyordu. Ama artık dünya çok hızlı değişiyor. Bugün hayal gibi gelen şeyler iki yıl sonra hayatımızın içerisinde sıradanlaşıyor.
Böyle bir dünyada hâlâ eski hızla hareket etmek büyük sorun…

quoted_text:
After 12 years, I'm moving my money back to TradFi...

For the past ~7 months, I've been moving a ton of money from onchain to tradfi. Money I never ever thought I would have a reason to move to tradfi, money that, in one form or another, has been onchain since I bought my first BTC back in 2014.

It's been a painfully tedious process bridging it. (I might write about that some other day, but that's not the point of this post.)

About 8 months ago, I came to the conclusion that having substantial amounts of capital parked onchain wasn't worth the r/r anymore, for several reasons...

BTC is not a SoV, and I haven't held it in a while. 
Stables are nowhere near as decentralized as we pretend they are. 
DeFi's third-party and smart-contract risks relative to the yields you get are a kick in the nuts.

I could go on...
 
I've been putting up with all of this for years because I really didn't want to go through the process of moving all that money to tradfi.

And because, despite all those problems, I had always considered onchain superior to tradfi.... Particularly in terms of portability + permissionless access + self-custody, which made putting up with all the other bullshit worth it.

But having been at the frontier of AI since day one, and watching how quickly these models have advanced in mathematical reasoning and automated vulnerability discovery, I've become extremely concerned about the security assumptions that hold this entire onchain machine together.

With the most fundamental one being cryptographic risk. AI can't break Bitcoin's elliptic-curve cryptography today, and quantum computing is a whole different beast. But imagine a future breakthrough that makes deriving private keys from exposed public keys computationally feasible....Imagine waking up to Satoshi's coins moving because someone had managed to reconstruct his private keys.....Imagine what that would do to confidence in every other wallet secured by the same cryptographic assumptions.

We have built an enormous financial machine on top of cryptographic primitives + software implementations +  security assumptions that have held up remarkably well so far.....But the amount of intelligence and computational effort that can be directed toward finding weaknesses in that machine is changing very damn fast.

And I have no interest in finding out which part breaks first with a substantial amount of money sitting inside it.

At this point, I'm more convinced than ever that some version of this is a question of WHEN, rather than IF. 

I have no idea when, and I might bevery wrong about the tl, but the potential loss is too large relative to what I'm being compensated to keep that capital onchain.

Now.....I'm sure that if I leave it here, one of the first and most popular comments will be something along the lines of:

"You're a fucking idiot. If cryptography breaks and crypto goes down, the entire financial system goes down with it."

And yes, that's absolutely right, given that Tradfi depends on cryptography too.

But here's my thinking...

I'd rather be fucked alongside the rest of the world than exclusively alongside magic internet money enjoyors.

Because when the world's financial system gets fucked, it's in EVERYONE's interest to fix it. Governments, central banks, financial institutions, you name it... The entire world's machinery will be put to work to get shit back in order.

Not so much the case for onchain....

If some critical piece of onchain infrastructure breaks who tf is coming to save us?

Nobody owes us shit.... And if the rest of the financial system is also compromised, you can bet nobody is going to waste resources saving our magic internet money while trying to save the rest of the world.

So I'd rather have that money on the other side.

And if a large portion of your NW is sitting onchain, I'd suggest you consider taking that hedge too.

PS: This doesn't mean I'll stop trading onchain or being active in crypto...Ofc I won't....I love this weird fkn world too much.... 

But going forward, I'll only keep the money I'm actively playing with onchain, and not a cent more.

author: manateelazycat
quoted_text:
深度用了 Neon 几天，我觉得这是一个 Sota 级别的模型，详细评价如下：

- 协作起来太舒服了，交流很顺畅，并且能懂你要做什么；
- 有时候会倾向于半途停下来，喜欢在工作到一半之后给你几个选项问你接下来要做什么，不过可以通过 AGENTS.md 修正；
- 速度还不错，能快速做出一个原型来验证，所以挺适合前端工作的；
- 有一定的设计和审美，很独特，但总体不如 Opus 5.5，不过我更倾向于说是互补而不是 Opus 5.5 全面更优；
- Coding 能力不如 Opus 5.5，或者说不如 Opus 那么“许愿式”，需要人工干预，One Shot 是绝对会出问题的；
- Review、Debug 能力还不错，所以你只要在让它干完活起独立审查，就能解决很多问题；
- 额度问题已经得到了非常大的优化，95%的缓存命中，Ultra 5x 能得到约 1.5B tokens 的 Neon 额度，20x 就是 约 6B，这个额度已经相当不错！

所以总体来说，这确实是个 Opus 5.5 的平替，很多方面不如 Opus 5.5，但可以在一定程度上弥补、修正；同时又有一些方面胜过 Opus，比如语言，非常的明显。综合下来非常推荐尝试订阅 Google AI Ultra！（建议月付，不要轻易上年订）

author: taomerchx
quoted_text:
Nearly 1,000 AI agents ran their own research world for three months.

They caught errors in published human papers, then retracted their own mistakes before anyone asked.

Blinded judges scored their rigor about 9 out of 10.

Matched human papers scored about 7.

Then came the twist. On choosing questions worth asking, the agents fell behind.

AI can already do the work. AI can already check the work. It still cannot choose the work.

Bittensor's cofounder read the study and said it would work well as a subnet. Nobody has built it yet, but picture it:

1. Miners publish papers with code and data attached.
2. Validators rerun the code.
3. TAO flows only to results that hold.

That check has teeth. When reviewers challenged a paper and reran the code, about half the headline conclusions collapsed.

Human science calls this the replication crisis. A subnet turns it into a payout.

Humans pick the question. Agents do the grind. The market pays for what is true.

Most people think $TAO pays for chatbots. It pays for work that survives a check. https://t.co/PzOvMe00zr

Base head Jesse Pollak says Base is still exploring a token but isn't in a rush: the team doesn't want to get distracted from its growth

"At the beginning of Base, we made a really conscious decision that we weren't going to do a token at that point."

"We wanted to make sure that we weren't getting distracted too early on by the noise that comes with a token, and that we weren't clouding our ability to find product market fit."

"As we think about further decentralizing Base, as we think about aligning all the different participants in the economy, as we think about continuing to be at the cutting edge of the technology innovation that comes with blockchain, a token can be a potentially really powerful lever."

"I think what all of that has led to is us continuing to explore, but also not being in a rush."

"When we think about when is the right time for us to further decentralize Base, it really is about making sure that we are not distracting ourselves, that we are accelerating the growth that we're seeing in front of us. We feel like we have a lot more work to do there."

text:
用 Tailscale 的朋友，建议都把 Tailnet Lock 打开。之间我分享过打开 ACL 增强安全性的技巧，后来发现不够。

配好 ACL 能防止某台机器被攻破后横向扩散，但还有一个口子。谁能进你的 tailnet，最终是 Tailscale 的协调服务器说了算。云端如果被攻破或者作恶，理论上可以悄悄塞一台假设备进来，其他设备会照单全收。

Tailnet Lock 补的就是这个口子。新设备必须由你指定的签名节点签名，每台设备在本地验签，签名无效就拒绝连接。签名私钥只在你自己的设备上，云端伪造不了。

开启前
新设备登录 → 云端分发公钥 → 其他设备直接接受 → 互通

开启后
新设备登录 → Locked out，等待签名
→ 签名节点签名 → 其他设备本地验签 → 通过才互通

开启很简单。在管理台 Device management 里点 Enable Tailnet Lock，选两台常用设备当签名节点，复制生成的 tailscale lock init 命令，在其中一台上运行。现有设备会自动签好。

初始化会生成一组 disablement secret，用来在出问题时关掉锁。一定要存进密码管理器，再留一份离线备份。丢了又没给官方留一份，锁就关不掉了。

开完之后，已有设备之间完全不受影响。新设备加入要先签名，在管理台点 Sign machine 就行。另外它和 Device approval 互斥，两个只能开一个。

ACL 管进来以后能访问什么，Tailnet Lock 管谁能进来。配了 ACL 的，顺手把这个也开了吧。

上一篇 ACL 配置在这里

quoted_text:
直呼 Tailscale 牛逼！

现在我所有的服务器和设备都连到了 Tailscale，并且开启了 Tailscale SSH。之后我基本没再折腾过 Private Key，也不用到处同步 SSH key，每次直接 ssh root@tailscale-ip 就可以登录。

部署在某台服务器上的 Hermes，也可以通过 Tailscale 跨服务器做监控、服务部署和日常运维，非常方便。

但我最近意识到这里有一个风险：如果某个 Hermes 要给别人共用，或者部署在公网服务器上，未来真的被攻破了，在原来 allow-all 的网络策略下，攻击者就可能继续横向访问我其他的服务器，甚至是正在使用的个人电脑。

刚刚花了一点时间配置 Tailscale Access Control，就把这个问题解决了。

做法很直接：先用 tag 把设备分成 personal 和 public-server，然后分别配置网络 Grants 和 Tailscale SSH Policy。

我这次直接给 Hermes 创建了一个临时的 scoped OAuth client，让它读取并备份原来的 policy、生成新规则、调用 Tailscale API 验证，然后提交配置，最后再从两个方向做真实连接测试。如果手动配置也不麻烦，核心就是写清楚两个 tag 之间谁可以主动访问谁。

我目前的规则是：

- personal 设备之间可以相互连接和 SSH
- personal 可以连接 public server
- public server 不能反向连接 personal
- public server 之间也不能横向连接

过程中还踩了一个坑：Tailscale 的网络 Grants 和 Tailscale SSH 是两层权限。网络已经通了，不代表 SSH 一定能登录，两边都需要配置。

这样一来，我内网服务器上部署的 Hermes 仍然可以作为管理节点和跳板机，控制其他服务器；但部署在公网的 Hermes 即使出现问题，影响范围也会被限制在外面，不会通过 Tailnet 继续横向扩散。

太牛逼了。以前这种内网管理、身份认证和权限隔离，通常都是大公司才会认真搭建的基础设施。现在 Tailscale 直接把它下放到了个人，而且免费就能用。

没用的赶紧用起来！

text:
A staking contract can look fully funded while quietly spending user principal as rewards.

Zealynx found that hidden balance failure in Ample Protocol.

`StakingContract` held deposits and funded rewards in the same token balance, with no internal accounting to separate them or reserve promised interest.

Earlier reward payments could therefore consume tokens owed to stakers. Under heavy withdrawals, later users could be unable to recover their principal.

The fix added separate tracking for the reward pool and promised rewards. Ample fixed the High-severity finding, and Zealynx verified it.

习近平修宪成功已经一年多了，说出了那句“中美合则两利、斗则俱伤”，川普也说“我对中国没有敌意，希望两国越来越好”。

央视赶紧把《上甘岭》改成《黄河绝恋》，这些年，看把电影频道给忙乎的。

所有的虐恋都充满反转。刘鹤在白宫签约才八天。2020年1月23日，武汉封城了。随着病毒蔓延，中国官媒说病毒来自一位到武汉参加军运会的自行车女选手。

这么好的人民，不执行计划生育，可惜了。

美国驻成都领馆真是故事多多，1999年美国轰炸中国驻南大使馆，爱国群众在这儿扔燃烧瓶砸玻璃，2012年王立军跑进了这家美领馆，导致薄熙来被抓，改写了中国政治格局，这次中美相杀又遭闭馆。成都的风水先生总说：美领馆风水不好，高楼压顶，路口逢冲，要不是美国人命硬，早就出事了。

孟晚舟乘国家包机回到深圳，机场挤满挥舞国旗的人群，高喊“欢迎回家”，这些天天操心房贷车贷的爱国群众，迎接一位拿着枫叶卡、在温哥华有两栋豪宅、孩子和老公都持国外护照的富豪回家，也不知人家回的哪个家。而孟晚舟对镜头说：“如果信念有颜色，那一定是中国红”……

在中国，最好演员从来都不在中戏。

这场贸易战谁吃亏了呢？

text:
花100U开包，抽到20U的宝可梦卡，反而更开心？

@oripaxyz   这个机制有点意思。

因为它是“亏钱挖币”：包价100U、卡片锁定价20U，协议记亏80U。在最初500万U累计记亏区间，每亏1U铸10枚币，你就能拿到800枚 $ORIPA。

但这里有个容易算错的地方。

卡片按当天指数价的85%回购，假设价格不变，20U的卡只能卖回17U。所以你实际花了83U，拿到800枚币，取得成本约0.104U一枚。

那这83U怎么赚回来？

第一条路是质押分开包收入。按项目方参数，在卡价不变、整池售完且全部卖回等假设下，每100U开包款，平均约27.75U可分给质押者。

假设你那800枚币一直占总质押量的1%，后面再开约300包，就可能分回83U。但后来的人既带来开包款，也会挖出新币加入质押，你的占比未必守得住。

第二条路是解锁后卖币。

假设已经分到20U，还差63U回本。800枚全部解锁后，平均卖到0.07875U就够；但按计划，明年1月13日首次只解锁一半，要靠400枚当天收回63U，均价就得达到0.1575U，手续费另算。

所以我觉得，判断ORIPA能不能持续，关键是：挖币奖励变少之后，还有多少人愿意真金白银开包、把卡寄回家？

只要还有真实消费，质押收入就可能继续；如果所有人都只想挖币退出，币价、开包量和分红就可能一起往下走。

11月25日首场付费开包，我会盯三个数：真实收藏需求、每千枚币实际分到的USDC，以及解锁后到底能卖多少钱。

quoted_text:
A lot of people are worried about P = NP.

Here’s the simple version.

P is the set of problems a computer can solve quickly. Sorting a list, finding the shortest route on a map, multiplying numbers.

NP is the set of problems where, if someone hands you an answer, you can check it quickly. A filled-in Sudoku is easy to verify, but solving a hard one from scratch can take forever.

If you can check an answer fast, can you also find it fast? P = NP says yes. Almost everyone believes the answer is no, but nobody has proved it either way. It’s a $1M Millennium Prize problem.

Riemann is solved, but it doesn’t change your day. P = NP would change everything very fast.

Almost all modern security rests on the assumption that some problems are brutally hard to solve but easy to check. Factoring huge numbers is the classic one.

If P = NP, that wall could fall. HTTPS, online banking, passwords, digital signatures, crypto wallets, all of it would be at risk.

The same power that breaks encryption would solve the hardest optimization problems we have.

Protein folding and drug discovery would speed up massively. Logistics, flight schedules and supply chains would become near perfect.

Training AI models could get far cheaper. Even finding mathematical proofs could be automated.

It depends on how it’s proved. If the proof is not constructive, or the algorithm runs in something like n^100 time, it's useless in practice. The scary version is a fast, practical algorithm.

Most researchers bet on P ≠ NP, and that is the reason your bank account is safe today.

But if someone ever proves P = NP with a practical algorithm, the world gets rewritten overnight.

Best case, we cure diseases and solve problems we thought were impossible.

Worst case, every lock on the internet opens at once.

Something to worry about indeed.

Netflix剧集《利他主义者》（The Altruists）上线引发加密社区热议，1confirmation创始人Nick Tomaino发文回顾FTX事件，怒批最受认可的个人和机构往往也表现出最强烈的贪婪。

Nick Tomaino指出，当时包括《纽约时报》和CNBC部分主流媒体及加密行业意见领袖为博取关注，过度宣扬FTX是最优秀的加密交易平台、SBF是加密行业的“摩根大通”；

此外，美国证监会（SEC）主席Gary Gensler及接受FTX政治捐款的政客则为追逐权力，曾与FTX方面会面讨论不采取执法行动函（No-action Letter），并接受其超过1亿美元的资金；红杉资本等风投机构则为追逐金钱，向这家存在欺诈行为的公司投入超过18亿美元。

Nick Tomaino最后表示，人们总是渴望获得更多，而FTX事件暴露出的这种缺乏底线的贪婪，值得整个行业反思。

Take this with a grain of salt: 1. Captain of industry who just borrowed dozens of billions to buy GPUs and 2. has been trying to crash the market for months now in destabilization campaigns against others in the industry he is competing in in order to 3. wipe out the competition and acquire assets (hardware, power, debt) for pennies on the dollar. 

That's not to say he's wrong. People have been criticizing circular financing, power / hardware scarcity, and neocloud business models for quite a while. The difference now is stocks are dumping & it will be harder to borrow. 

A contraction in AI has been needed. We're overbuilt on infrastructure and yet to see use cases that require this much compute. The clearest use case has been using clusters of servers to solve difficult math problems, but it's unclear how that will drive the yearly $3.7T in spend needed by 2032 for the AI bet to pay off. As hardware improvements continue to accelerate, the gap needed to fully utilize the hardware widens and a race to the bottom (where compute providers undercut one another due to low PMF) gets that much more brutal.

- When $BTC drops, alts usually get hit even harder. The more you try to catch the bottom, the more you get cooked

3. Look for market capitulation, not CT hype
I'd rather see everyone give up, turn bearish, and lose interest until no one even mentions crypto anymore

As long as top influencers are still bullish, price can still go lower (take CZ as an example)

CZ was still optimistic not long ago. Look where we are now

4. Don't blindly follow individual whale or MM wallets 
Just because a whale or MM buys a token doesn't mean it'll pump

They could be hedging with shorts elsewhere or even using onchain activity to bait retail

Look at the bigger picture and have your own plan

5. Don't buy a coin/token just because someone calls for a pump
If a KOL says a token is about to pump, ask why?. What's the actual story behind it?

Don't let someone else's price target become your entire investment

---
Stay patient, observe, study the market more, and have a clear plan

text:
Remember @thiccyth0t 's  MOAS theory? It describes pretty well what transpired in the markets this year:

"Greed makes you leverage those beliefs more and more as you get rewarded for them. The most greedy rise to the top as they leverage up the most on the behavior that rewards them. And then when the regime inevitably changes they get thanksgiving turkeyed. This manifests the most observably in financial markets but it pervades all aspects of life."

"Once this thing turns, it's not coming back. It turns once, right? It's a turkey distribution. All of financial engineering, the whole purpose of it is to transform return distributions into the Thanksgiving turkeys. And there's not gonna be a dip that you're supposed to buy. That's the dip that keeps dipping...

Everyone gets turkeyed - everyone follows, everyone thinks this is it, it's gonna launch, and then suddenly all demand has been filled and there's no one there with any spare ammo to buy it back...

Everyone comes in and the reflexivity exacerbates the FOMO. It pushes it to an inorganic price where there is no demand anymore and there's a f*ton of supply, and then it turns."

text:
$CLAUDIA 和 $DOGE 的类比听着爽，但有个根本的不同会误导预期

英文区很多人拿 $CLAUDIA 对标 $DOGE 的 Musk 互动路径，说这是“自 Doge 以来 Musk 给予最多关注的 meme”。数据上可能没错，但这个类比会把人的预期带歪。

$DOGE 的 Musk 互动是纯情绪驱动的，Musk 觉得好玩就发，整个过程背后没有任何内容实体。 $CLAUDIA 不一样，Musk 互动的对象是真实存在的 AI 音乐影像内容，Saylor 甚至拿去做了自己的视频，它的催化有内容锚点，不完全随 Musk 的情绪走。

这既是好事也是坏事。

好的一面，底更硬，anabology 在持续产出，IP 被外部调用的案例在增加，就算 Musk 哪天不聊了也很难归零。

坏的一面，天花板更低，$DOGE 能涨到几百亿恰恰因为它足够空、足够 meme，任何人都能往里投射任何东西，而 $CLAUDIA 有具体的角色、内容、创作者，这些“具体”同时也封住了想象空间。

所以拿 $DOGE 做预期锚定是危险的。更合理的对标，是那些有真实 IP 但体量有限的 meme，巅峰期几千万到一两亿那一档。

对 $CLAUDIA 来说，2000 到 5000 万可能是个更现实的上限区间，前提还得是催化不断。讲真这个逻辑我能接受，但真拿它想象上亿市值，得给自己泼盆冷水。

text:
没有什么「 镣铐 」 是一亿美金解决不了的。

从普通交易员视角看，最近 @variational_io 的产品体验其实优化了很多。

之前像 $SPY $QQQ 这大标的，但凡我超一个方向稍微开点仓位，整个平台就会处在 OI skew limit 中。如果我和其他大户不平，散户就开不了仓。

以至于当时我还需要自己做个监控网站，实时查看平台一共有多少额度可以供我开。

例如我想开 5m 的多单，但平台只有 1m 的做多额度，怕麻烦的我就会觉得为了这 1m 仓位，还要多管理一个平台太麻烦，容易猪脑过载，遂放弃在 var 上做这笔交易，带来的结果就是 OLP 赚不到钱，我也赚不到积分。

现在好了，融资一到位，OLP 的流动性提供能力暴涨，今晚我一共开了 15m 的 $QQQ 多单，3m 在 @binance ，12m 分 6 个号在 var 上开，全程丝滑无比。

为什么是 3m 和 2m 一个号？
因为这个仓位价值刚好卡 10X 杠杆的线。

再看执行成本这块儿：

1. 币安我的 V6 账户，用 BNB 结算手续费，taker fee 是 1.08 bp。

2. var 这边，1.9 bp 的 half spread，可以认为是 1.9 bp 的手续费，算上最高等级的 7.5% 点差返佣，大概是 1.76bp。

这个手续费刚好和币安卡 v2 账户，拿 40% 返佣的 taker 成本一致。

对于月交易量不大的小散户和无缘使用币安的交易员来说，这个执行成本就可以借助 OLP 体验到宇宙所的流动性，还是可以接受的。

虽然比币安 v6 要贵一些，但是给积分，以及我很欣赏创始人 @variational_lvs ，肥水不流外人田，哥们儿的手续费给谁赚不是赚？那不如让自己的朋友赚。

总体来说，var 在 crypto native asset 这块，大币种流动性很早就没问题了，rwa perps 的核心标的也终于不再是带着镣铐跳舞了。

这两大市场说实话，风控和安全搞扎实，产品体验做到 80 分，把 low-hanging fruit 摘完就好了，没必要花太多资源去卷细节，真没性价比。

要出奇迹，还是得把 SWAP 搞起来，尽快上美股个股，尽快开 7*24，这才是颜色不一样的烟火。

目前 @variational_io 占 RWA 全网交易量的 2%，这个数据是带着镣铐跳舞的结果，分享几点对产品的观察和思考：

1. 名义杠杆率低。

拿 $XAU $CL 这种热门大宗举例，25wu 的仓位，名义杠杆率就降到 10X 了；用 5X 杠杆，最多只能开 75wu 的仓位，和其他所相比，劣势过大，真实交易员的开仓能力是被压制的。

2. 出于 OLP 风控，skew limit 频繁。

过去两个月大家一定都经历过 $SPY $QQQ 这俩指数不能朝特定方向开仓的情况。

这是因为 OLP 限制了平台多空单的失衡金额。

为此，我甚至还做了个实时监控，来计算平台还有多少的单边额度可以开。

当要建立头寸时，我会先把 var 的额度用完，然后继续在其他交易开完剩下的。（ 毕竟这有积分收益）

所以有时候，你发现不能开了，大概率是因为我开的太多了，等哥们儿开始平仓了，你就能开了。

以上两个例子，说明仅仅是我一个小卡拉米能产生的真实交易量，OI，都因为平台还处在 RWA 测试阶段，没能得到充分释放。对流动性的需求，暂时没有得到完全的满足。

那算上其他的大户，真正的鲸鱼呢？

所以待到 swap 功能上线，封印被解除，杠杆率可以看齐其他所，OI cap 被打开，平台的数据大概率会提升不少。

3. 积分激励阶段，如何评估 farmer 带来的数据泡沫？

现在所谓的 trader 和 farmer 的界限在不断模糊的。

在一个所有链上赌场都在拿 token 预期抢市场的时代红利期，就算我搞小农经济，专注套利交易，无比追求每笔交易中的绝对现金收益，哥们儿也不会傻到不去评估把交易量给哪个所，潜在收益会更大。

你觉得猿是 trader 还是 farmer？

再比如有些散户，本来可能就想 farm 两下，打一炮就走，最后架不住自己脑子聪明，撸着撸着，搞明白了价差，理解了资费，意识到了指数的力量，发现干这活儿能长期赚钱，逐步进化成了 trader。

最牛逼的 trader，就是最牛逼的 farmer。

尽管如此，还是有些小技巧可以评估一个项目是否被过度 farm ，虚假繁荣的程度。

还是拿 @variational_io 举例，它的 RWA 市场，交易量分布够广，每个票都有人在玩，这是非常好的信号。

但 $XAUT $PAXG 这俩资产的 OI 过大，说明还是有不少人，在分号持仓跟 $XAU 对冲。

这显然不是正常做套利的人，愿意冒风险开的仓位，因为根本没有赔率。

之前多次提醒过， $XAUT 和 $PAXG 的高倍合约，是可以让人灰飞烟灭的东西。

4. 即将上线的 SWAP 功能，才是平台真正的拳头产品。

目前 var 基于 @binance 流动性做的一期 RWA 合约市场，在商业上，算是个非常讨巧，四两拨千斤的产品，而且是极好的现金流生意。

OLP 用类似 「 众筹 」的模式，通过对冲散户的订单流，养起了一个高 VIP 等级的 bn 号。

再把自己的交易优势，反哺回社区，给到了普通交易员更低的手续费成本，和无许可的便捷，让很多不能 KYC bn 的交易员，也体验到了宇宙所的极致流动性。

这个视角下，币安在 RWA 赛道 25% 的交易量占比，是有 var 的一份功劳。

var 是 binance 流动性的链上 broker。

而接下来，我们会看到非常多的新台子雨后春笋般地冒出，讲 RFQ ，吹 tradfi liquidity on chain 的故事。

这些对 var 都是好事儿。

从 orderbook 到 RFQ，从 crypto-native liquidity 到 TradFi dealer liquidity，这个市场教育不可能只靠一个项目完成。

需要一堆拿了 VC 钱的项目一起烧，一起喊，一起铺概念，最后完成「 高效价格发现 」和「 最佳执行成本下的流动性获取 」两种产品理念的二分天下。

但我们要看到本质， RFQ 本身不是护城河，谁在 RFQ 背后给你报价才是护城河。

任何交易所都可以做一个 RFQ 界面，让 mm 按需报价。

但能不能拿到真正顶级 TradFi dealer 的双边流动性，能不能和他们签对手方协议，能不能在大 size 下稳定对冲，能不能把这层流动性转译成更低的 execution cost，这才是核心。

var 的差异不在于 「 它有 RFQ 」。
var 的差异在于：OLP 自己就是链上用户和 TradFi dealer 之间的 counterparty layer。

说白了，var 不是开了个 RFQ 群聊，让一堆 mm 看到你要买什么，买多少后各自喊价。

而是 OLP 先站出来当你的交易对手，能内部消化的先内部消化，消化不了的净敞口，再丢给最头部的 TradFi dealer 去对冲。

所以同样都叫 “TradFi liquidity”，含金量完全不是一回事。

大部分场子充其量解决的是“让长尾市场有人愿意报个价”。

var 解决的是“把机构级 dealer liquidity 变成链上可调用的执行能力”。

以终为始来看现在的竞争，RFQ 压根儿就不是做价格发现的产品形态，而是做极限优化 exectution cost 的产品。

而只有 var 这套，用 OLP 干脏活苦活累活，才有机会真正优化掉执行成本，给到交易员极致的交易深度和可预期的持仓成本。

几年前，听说一个反撸的 L2 项目，给 KOL 每人发几万U 的茶水费，我当时大为震撼，就去扒了链上 Tx，开始对这个行业祛魅

顺便聊下转账记录这事，链上真没隐私，收款人就是裸奔。正常收付款，不想主动公开账本，American Fortress （美国堡垒）就是想解决这个需求

🌈美国团队，美国公司，美国专利

先说下 @Americanfort_io 背景，不是华人项目，它背后的公司是 MatterFi Inc.，注册在美国怀俄明州（彭博的企业身份记录里能查到）

创始人 Michal “Mehow” Pospieszalski，毕业于弗吉尼亚大学计算机系，创业做了 8 年的 Rune Wallet 钱包基建被 MatterFi 收购

我翻到一张他 2018 年出席 CIS 大会的照片，履历看，确实是旧金山湾区科技圈子的人

他的研究方向是钱包安全，项目有专利保护，2025 年拿到了美国国家专利

🔹我个人觉得，这种实名且有美国专利的项目，比币圈某些圈钱 PPT 好很多

--

🍀项目在做什么

按官方设计，你注册一个 FortressName，比如 sam，别人在钱包里输入名字，就能转账，不用每次复制那串长地址

但它不只是给钱包起个昵称，背后会按收发对象使用独立地址，让外人更难把这个名字、收款记录和常用钱包关联起来，不是看到名字，就能顺藤摸瓜翻你的账

这项目还没发币，估计快 TGE 了，代码是$AF，看后面能上哪些交易所

保护隐私，但绝不是混币器

--

🪂 对我们有什么用？

朋友之间转 U、给客户收服务费、做线上生意，我觉得这类需求很实在。我们要的是收钱方便，不是每次收款，都顺便把常用钱包交给别人研究

项目方今年 5 月在 Arb 上推出了测试版，已经可以进行产品测试

✅ 我不知会不会有空投。。。。这个真不知道。。。

现在的项目不需要撸毛人做数据了，能解决需求的才有市场，比如 HYPE 是交易赌场，这个美国堡垒如果能把转账隐私做到位，也能成长为细分领域的一棵小树

我分享记录一下看到的有趣项目，本文不做任何投资建议

"We wanted to make sure that we weren't getting distracted too early on by the noise that comes with a token, and that we weren't clouding our ability to find product market fit."

"As we think about further decentralizing Base, as we think about aligning all the different participants in the economy, as we think about continuing to be at the cutting edge of the technology innovation that comes with blockchain, a token can be a potentially really powerful lever."

"I think what all of that has led to is us continuing to explore, but also not being in a rush."

"When we think about when is the right time for us to further decentralize Base, it really is about making sure that we are not distracting ourselves, that we are accelerating the growth that we're seeing in front of us. We feel like we have a lot more work to do there."

text:
最近能早期参与的项目也就 @oripaxyz 了。一句话描述这个项目就是「cards的老虎机抽卡模式 + papertrade的代币经济学」的结合体——用代币补贴用户抽卡所涉及的亏损，再将产品收入分配给代币质押者，形成一套循环。

这篇内容我主要想讨论两部分内容：
1、数学上的问题。用户抽卡产生的亏损，是在以什么估值购买代币，以及收入分配给代币质押者，是如何分配，什么样的收入才能撑起代币的估值。

oripa总供应量无限趋近于770m枚，用户每铸造100枚，vault就配套铸造40枚（用户能拿到的550m枚，vault对应的是220m）。在5m usdc全网亏损达成前，用户每亏损1 usdc，就固定铸造10 $oripa，名义成本0.1 usdc/枚，对应的铸币成本是77m fdv。超过5m亏损后，铸币成本开始上升，到55m时，对应的铸币成本是308m fdv。到105m时，对应的铸币成本是693m。

但真正决定你实际成本的，不只是曲线位置，还有卡池结构。因为每个卡池都是按照0.85 rtp（玩家返还率）组池，melt按当日指数价格的85%返还usdc。用户花1000u抽10次的预期卡牌的价值是850u，全部melt能回本722.5u。看似不同池子最后的结果是一样的，但实质上不同方差的池子能够产出的 $oripa 其实天差地别。计算公式是L=max(0,抽卡价-卡牌锁定价)，盈利不抵消亏损，且亏损记账不乘85%回购系数（图一）。

在资金充足的情况下，在低方差池里，15%的melt折价全白亏了，真实成本飙升；但在高方差池里，大卡能够有效地让你回口血，但合约却还是按照你的真实亏损去记账铸币，真实成本可以压到更低。

oripa在收入分配上非常极致，扣除邮寄实体卡的补货差价（合约封顶不超过15%的锁定价）后，100%分配：5%抽卡费和抽卡盈余（扣除5%抽卡费和卡牌85%回购准备金后的余额）都会给到质押者。vault的币在解锁前是不能质押的，只能等解锁（用户2027年1月13日开始解锁，vault 2027年3月16日之后才开始分批释放）。

按照25%有效分红率、20% usdc apy（5倍P/E）来倒推一下需要多少的收入才能撑起 $oripa 的流通市值： 早期盘子极轻，只要日均流水做到5-10万usdc，质押apy就能轻松飙到50%–100%+，早期筹码甚至在代币开放转账前就能靠真金白银的usdc分红大幅降本。但反过来，一旦累计亏损冲过5500万、后期铸币成本拉到300m fdv以上，平台每天必须维持近40万美元的持续抽卡流水才能托住盘子，那时就完全没有性价比了。这些数据解释了为什么我们要尽可能早地参与（图二）。

2、虽然模式采用的是papertrade的代币经济模型，但是papertrade里的交易者的盈利是由亏损者提供的，它是一个自循环的系统，而oripa的卡是由项目方去提供的，这是潜在的运营成本。这是否是一个好生意？

首先需要明确的是，除了前期的购卡补卡成本外，项目方的真实运营成本其实不高。一是实体卡邮寄目前仅支持日本、韩国、台湾和香港（将收取25u每单的邮寄费用，单日上限5张），24小时内不选邮寄就自动melt。二是哪怕有人提货，补货差价（至多15%锁定价）会从质押者收益中扣除，进一步降低运营成本（可以看得出来，项目方是鼓励你melt卡牌，而不是提现的）。

其次，oripa是封闭卡池垫付制，抽卡会当场将用户的钱作为准备金，就算二级市场再怎么砸盘做空 $oripa ，也套不出来所在合约里的准备金（唯一风险就是卡牌大行情暴涨）。而papertrade是赊账制，盈利用户的钱来自于亏损用户，系统的偿付能力非常重要，一旦开放paper的二级交易就将面临做空代币+操纵外部喂价薅空兑付池的连环攻击。

唯一需要担心的是项目方能否在前期不抽一分钱的情况下，是否能够承担备货补货的费用。这个纯看项目方实力，卖币收回成本则需要等到27年3月16日vault的代币开始解锁。

所以看懂了这两层结构，对于早期项目参与者而言，oripa是hyperevm上参与赔率非常好的一个项目。参与策略也非常简单，早期入场，抢前500万平价区间，只玩高方差的池子，挖完立刻手动质押吃满前6周的usdc分红。

quoted_text:
In case anyone is curious:

We’ve had a ~pixel-perfect world model since last year, which is critical for synthetic data generation. 

The (much) smaller version of that in the car is a conditional mean-flow model, based on the recent sequence of Tesla Universal Vision Encoder features, which are the same ones that are plugged into the 3B encoder model that produces the driving actions. 

We fork off from these UVE features, then run a separate ~1B diffusion model. This takes in the previous reality-view generation with added noise and then denoises it to the current visualization. 

It then produces a small video chunk (8 images at 36 fps, at the resolution of the UI screen). This work is done by 1/2 of a TRIP engine every UVE frame at 18 hz and is spread over 4 cycles. 

Currently, the latency is a bit high due to compute constraints, but we have ways to interleave newer UVE features along the diffusion transformer layers to cut roughly 35% of the latency.

author: crypto_condom
quoted_text:
The AI boom now hangs on one field in Ohio.

It's where SoftBank, OpenAI and Nvidia have tied themselves together so tightly that if one of them slips, the other two take the hit.

The field is in Piketon, Ohio. 

For about 4 decades, it was a Cold War uranium enrichment plant. The government still owns the land, and the old plant is still being torn down and cleaned up.

On top of it, SoftBank's energy company, SB Energy, plans one of the biggest AI campuses ever proposed. That's 8 gigawatts of computing, with 9.2 gigawatts of new gas plants to power it.

OpenAI signed a 20-year lease to use it. And Nvidia will be the only chip supplier.

Here's how the 3 of them are tied together:

The landlord is SB Energy, owned by SoftBank. This month, SoftBank's credit default swaps implied almost a 1 in 3 chance the company defaults. It just lost about $7 billion in a single quarter.

The tenant is OpenAI. Last quarter it brought in about $10 billion and posted a $10.9 billion adjusted operating loss, according to the Wall Street Journal. And it can't get an investment-grade credit rating.

So who guarantees the rent?

Nvidia.

Its own filing shows up to $105 billion of guarantees for the OpenAI campus. They only go away once OpenAI earns a satisfactory credit rating.

And on Friday, Reuters reported that SEC enforcement staff are scrutinizing potential accounting issues at Nvidia.

Then it gets circular:

OpenAI put $500 million into SB Energy. So the tenant owns a piece of its own landlord.

Nvidia plans to put in $1.5 billion more. So the company guaranteeing the rent will own a piece of the landlord too.

And SoftBank owns about 13% of OpenAI.

Every one of them is propping up the other two.

So what's standing on that field so far?

Masayoshi Son was at the groundbreaking in March. But satellite images from February through July showed no graded pads and no foundations on the old plant's footprint. One tracker counted ZERO megawatts confirmed under construction.

And the timeline on paper is long:

The environmental review isn't expected to finish until January 2027. The first 800 megawatts aren't due until 2028. The utility expects to deliver grid power in 2029.

If OpenAI can't pay, Nvidia could owe up to $105 billion.

If Nvidia pulls back, the lease loses the backing that made it possible.

If SoftBank can't keep funding SB Energy, the landlord can't build.

And if the campus slips, OpenAI's compute plans slip with it, along with the valuation SoftBank is borrowing against.

That's 3 of the biggest names in AI, one 20-year lease, and a field that was still a demolition site this summer.

So which one of them falls first?

text:
不知道大家有没有发现一个现象。

以前我们把钱放在交易所，目的很简单，就是买币、卖币、开合约。

但现在不一样了。

理财、支付、借贷、资产管理，交易所能干的事情越来越多。

这让我想到一个问题：

未来的加密交易所，会不会逐渐变成另一种形式的银行？

其实这个趋势已经很明显了。

拿币安来说，除了现货和合约，还有Earn理财、Binance Pay支付等业务。

单独看这些产品，似乎没什么特别的。

但如果把它们放在一起看，就有意思了。

用户不需要频繁切换平台，就可以完成交易、资金管理和部分支付需求。

对平台来说，用户留下来的理由也不再只是手续费便宜。

我觉得币安在产品生态布局上确实走得比较早，这也是它长期积累下来的优势之一。

但问题同样存在。

交易所不是银行，用户资产也不等于银行存款。不同产品背后的风险、保障机制完全不同。

尤其是理财和借贷，收益从来不是白送的。

未来交易所之间的竞争，可能不再只是抢交易量，而是谁能成为用户管理数字资产的主要入口。

不过对我们普通人来说，平台功能越方便，越要记住一件事：

方便归方便，千万别把所有身家都放在一个篮子里。

text:
I’ve said this for years.  The number one job of a GM is to keep their job.  There are only 32 spots in the NFL.  

An owner has a different perspective.  They have to consider the short term vs long term.      If you have any sense of how hard it is to win a ring, there will be times when you think you have a chance to win, and you go all in, and take risks you otherwise might not take. 

The age of the owner also matters.   It’s really really hard to win a championship.   The older you are and the longer it’s been since you won, (if ever ), two things happen:

1.  Time/Seasons go by faster.  That comes with age.  So you can accept a rebuild or risk, because 6 months used to be a long time.  It no longer is. 

2.  But then you reach an age and you start realizing your own mortality. You don’t have unlimited time.   It could be now or never.  Which impacts your  decision making. 

3.  If you are an owner who stresses every minute of every game, has ridiculous superstitions they think impacts outcomes lol (like I did lol), cares about winning first, second and last and for whom losing hurts more than winning feels good, (Not all do. Some, if not most, would like to win, but it’s not their first priority) , you are lucky to be a fan of that team. 

This is one of the reasons I love Jerry Jones.  You can see how much he loves the Cowboys and how much losing hurts him.   It doesn’t mean it always works.  But it does mean no one else cares more than Jerry.  

I don’t know Carlie.  Never met her and haven’t watched their games.  But she obviously doesn’t give a fuck what you think about her.  She is doing what she thinks is best.  She is only 46.  My guess is She is going to get smarter and better at being an owner specifically because she ignores the trolls and learns all she can.

text:
I feel that the progression from "goal" to "outcome" based engineering is the biggest advancement our industry has seen since vibe coding.

For the first time we have proactive, perpetual, self-verifying systems that make it possible. Some examples of what this looks like:

Goal: "Build an Android app."
→ Outcome: "Keep our iOS and Android apps at feature parity on every release."

Goal: "Translate the app into Spanish."
→ Outcome: "Keep the product fully localized in our top 12 languages, in sync with every English copy change."

Goal: "Fix this crash."
→ Outcome: "Keep the crash-free session rate above 99.9% on every release."

Goal: "Optimize the homepage."
→ Outcome: "Keep every page at a Lighthouse score of 95 or higher."

Goal: "Set up backups."
→ Outcome: "Make sure we can always restore production from backup in under an hour, and prove it weekly."

Goal: "Fix the bug from this support ticket."
→ Outcome: "Every support ticket caused by a bug ends in a shipped fix and a reply to the customer."

Goal: "Upgrade our dependencies."
→ Outcome: "Keep every dependency on its latest stable version with CI green."

Goal: "Clean up the dead code."
→ Outcome: "No feature flag, dead code path, or unused endpoint survives more than 30 days."

Goal: "Write a setup guide."
→ Outcome: "A new engineer can always go from fresh clone to running app with one command."

Goal: "Update the docs."
→ Outcome: "Keep the docs accurate to whatever is on main."

Goal: "Refresh the staging data."
→ Outcome: "Keep staging an exact, anonymized mirror of production."

Goal: "Write a competitor comparison page."
→ Outcome: "Keep our competitor comparison page accurate as their pricing and features change."

Goal: "Speed up the API."
→ Outcome: "Get p95 API latency under 200ms and hold it there as traffic grows."

Goal: "Run an accessibility audit."
→ Outcome: "Keep every page of the site WCAG AA compliant, forever."

Goal: "Fix this production error."
→ Outcome: "Every production error gets a root-cause fix and a regression test within an hour of first appearing."

text:
现在是2000年还是2008年？最近市场大跌，大家对此争论又起。从几个点来看当下跟00年或者08年的差异点。
1、与2000年对比
上半年半导体板块很多标的股价确实走出了抛物线的形态、跟2000年有一定相似之处。
但看本质的差异：
2000年前后的互联网行业并没找到商业模式，从00年一直到06、07年 ，游戏、广告、电商、增值服务这四大商业模式才真正被确立。当下的状态是基础设施非常完善、信息传递速度很快，所以AI商业化的速度很快。年初这里https://t.co/bSInrkL9VE聊到：移动互联网用了不到10年就走完互联网要20年才能走完的路，AI可能只需要更短的时间就能走完移动互联网10年才走完的路。

当下AI的商业化进展其实还是可以的，几个例证：
1）之前这里https://t.co/0gbWD8NIH9 聊到Anthropic今年做到500～600亿美是没问题明年大概率能突破1000亿美金的实际营收体量，这其实是一个很大的体量了。
2）之前这里https://t.co/43bxJBT8q6也有三大云厂在三季度总计1100亿美金的云业务体量，而且增速都在上半年开始提速，三季度明显延续了加速的态势。

互联网的商业化就是这样，一旦被验证后渗透率和商业化会一路提升到饱和阶段，现在看商业化应该还没到饱和阶段。

2、跟2008年的对比
2006年下半年美国房价见顶，2007 年 4月2日，美国第二大房地产抵押贷款机构新世纪金融申请破产，整个二三季度美国一大半抵押贷款机构破产，07年8 月，美国浮息房贷的严重拖欠率已接近 20%，同月法国巴黎银行三只基金暂停赎回，9月英国北岩银行破产，花旗、瑞信等披露在次贷上巨额亏损。次贷证券的买家也在借短钱，资产一旦难估值，资金方不肯续作，持有人只能补抵押品或卖资产，家庭月供的缺口就这样传到了原本指望随时能赎回的投资者。底层资产价格崩溃开始一步步往上层传导、几乎止不住的踩踏。2007年10月美股触顶，大盘开始了长达一年半腰斩一路。
这里核心07年初开始，房贷已经大面积开始违约。

当下的状态是企业的债务、采购承诺、租赁合约、担保整体规模确实很大；11月13号的美联储报告也有提到。但周期都很长。采购承诺、租约、担保都是五年起步持续十几年的周期，并不是立马就兑现。举几个例子：
1）Meta有2,789.9亿美元尚未起租的租约，2026年余下时间至2036年陆续开始，租约基二三十年，最长30年。
2）谷歌披露   披露一年期以上的未来固定或担保承诺为7,070亿美元，绝大部分是长期供应协议。能源协议期限为2–26年，最远至2054年。
3）再如英伟达
本周三季度财报披露的 5,180亿美元未来承诺，数据截至10月25日。公司另列 320亿美元算力云商协议和 1,180亿美元担保敞口。这里需要说明320亿美元买的是满足条件后才开始计算。

其中3900多亿美金都是的采购承诺其中2700亿美金是未来一年半的采购承诺，看着很可大。但实际上按照英伟达现在的业务体量、他确实需要这么大的采购量。今年英伟达大概有4200亿美金营收、74%的毛利、那么成本至少就是1100亿美金这都是采购成本。英伟达官方预计下一年75%的增速，如果毛利保持不变、意味着下一年采购成本就到了1900亿美金。

而给OpenAI／SB Energy 担保的俄亥俄州项目，首批预计到2028年才生效。本周代理ceo也说只有当数据中心的土地、电力和外壳等基础设施真正就绪时，担保才会生效。

4）美联储报告里先进计算相关公司债务累计1.1万亿美金，规模确实很大但是期限也很长。

富时罗素统计过几家美国云巨头172 只面值合计 4,230.2 亿美元债券，平均本金回收年限是 17.27 年。 微软最长平均 22.69 年；大家最担心的甲骨文债务期限最短平均 15.70 年。

说到这点能说明什么？
2007年美国房贷已经大面积违约，违约层层传导到了房贷、次贷以及各种基于抵达贷款通过搭积木形成的各类金融衍生品上。

而当下至少我们并没有看到哪一家大云厂商、新云厂商、大科技开始实质性的违约，美联储金融稳定报告也是在提前做预防，以防AI收入不及预期会如何影响金融稳定；

其实市场跟美联储一样、都是把未来潜在的风险提前拿来计价。

当然同一个数据，不同的人看到的反应也不一样。
正面反应：这些债务、采购承诺、租赁合约、融资担保，要么期限很长、要么还没开始生效；
负面反应：这么大的融资体量、生态担保，一旦商业化不及预期一定会爆一个大的。

所以整体上来看，
部分半导体上半年抛物线形态、但基本面商业化趋势远远好于2000年时期。
虽然整体债务、承诺担保规模庞大，但是周期很长、然后也没实质性违约。达不到2008年、可能也就05年。而且未来如果商业化继续加速、商业化增速超过资本开支增速、这种潜在风险回比消除很多。

所以当下是这对债务风险和28年开支断崖的担心，然后中选后政治生态剧变带动政策逆转的强烈担心，导致集中仓位出清。
但就此照搬零零年和零八年也并不准确。

短期看仓位出清程度，
还是引用推文聊的中长期看：
1）油价/通胀走势决定联储利率走向；
2）新政治生态下AI政策比当下市场预期的要更收紧和会略缓和些；
3）AI商业化是不是继续处于加速状态；

quoted_text:
中期选举惨败引发的市场崩塌，昨晚美股大跌纳指已经把今年全年涨幅跌没了从最高点下来跌了-19%多、大饼更是跌破6万点，算是真正意义上市场崩了。个人角度11月5号纳指一根大阴线以来这一波大跌核心原因就是共和党中期选举惨败导致美国政治生态变化以及一系列连锁反应引发市场对于产业政策和党争的激烈定价。上周在“倒黄“事件梳理https://t.co/5XFhdDw5IO，以及本周三在币安广场AMA里有聊过，再展开下

1、共和党的惨败程度
都知道这次中选共和党惨败，但是惨败到什么程度呢？
1）共和党参议院丢掉9个席位，导致民主党拿下56个参议员席位、这是民主党自1958年以来最大参议院净增席数。这也导致了虽然民主党不是绝对多数，但是争取几个共和党中间派和建制派议员实现60票以上的可能性大大增加。
2）众议院全国普选票差距，
众议院选举民主党约56%，共和党约42%，差距约14%，这是1974年水门事件以来最大的中期选举普选票优势，也是近50年最大差距。
3）深红州被翻盘
得克萨斯：参议院和州长双翻盘（州长是1990年代以来民主党首次）。
堪萨斯参议院：1932年以来首次民主党胜利。
南卡罗来纳、密西西比、爱荷华、俄亥俄等也出现翻盘，这已经不是边缘波动，而是广泛支持流失。
4）州一级
（1）民主党净增约6个州长席（包括佐治亚、爱荷华、内华达、俄亥俄、得克萨斯、阿拉斯加等），民主党获得多数州长席位（约30-20）。
（2）多个议院翻盘，民主党新增多个“三权合一”（州长+两院）
共和党几乎没有成功翻转任何民主党控制的参议院席位
本次中期选举投票率约49%，民，是1914年以来第二高中期投票率（仅次于2018年）。即使共和党进行了中期重划选区、也遭遇了大败。

两院失守且席位被大幅拉开、14点普选票优势 、深层红州翻盘 、州长与州议会大面积失利，这些都指向了这是近几十年最严重一次中期选举失败。选举结果刚出来的时候，我是远远低估这次失败的严重程度，以及惨败之后的一系列连锁反应。

2、惨败的连锁反应
1）最直接的就是川普在共和党的威信与影响力被极大的削弱
之前川普可以依靠自己的威望和影响力，死死压住党内的不同意见，其他声音都不能完全冒头。但这次惨败趟则让川普的影响力大打折扣，通胀民生和AI发展数据中心建设潮的负面声音就被放大，因为这是惨败的直接原因、因为都败成这样了、川普也不能不承认。

之前共和党内的政治人物都需要川普背书，但现在的问题是背书效应已经大打折扣、24年川普背书的议员赢得大选概率是89%，现在已经不到50%，川普背书已经不是助力而是阻力了，那么共和党内持不同主张的政治人物都开始活跃并强硬起来。

2）“倒黄”事件就是川普威望和影响力被削弱的直接连锁反应之一。
现在大家都清楚，这次“倒黄”主力不是民主党，而是共和党内对华强硬派，卢比奥、贝森特还有共和党国会几个委员会主席。之前他们可都不敢忤逆川普的意愿，但是这次即使川普再三帮助老黄发声，但效果甚微。

老黄离开市场自然对英伟达的未来很悲观、技术迭代速度可能放缓、产业生态支持力度也会大幅减弱。这些都让担忧一步步加强

3）产业政策的大逆转
民主党不仅大幅度领先优势拿下国会多数席位、现在还有三十个州长位子，那么市场就会但心川普过去两年积极推动的AI和加密的产业政策会被逆转：
AI监管会更加严格、AI基建会大幅放缓；
加密立法几无可能、加密清算更加猛烈；
这种预期的改变，对无论是对冲基金和长线资金信心的影响和动摇是巨大的，所以我们看到的没顾上对冲基金在大幅度砍仓，然后长线资金也是不断减持仓位。
币市则表现为中期选举后比特币ETF连日大额净流出、稳定币发行量持续下降。

4）然后就是美联储官员的激进表态
你看川普影响力一被削弱、FOMC票委们的表态就大胆起来，这里典型就是沃勒、之前还算是鸽派、现在已经完全转变成了强鹰派，连12月50个基点的加息论调都提出来了，多名票委的鹰派发言，自然也让市场对12月以及明年初的利率走势更加悲观。

当然核心也是现在美伊博弈在中期选举还没有明确的说法，市场也很担心通胀的走势。

可以看到“倒黄”事件，产业政策被逆转的担忧、联储官员的鹰派很大程度上都是这次中选共和党惨败带来的连锁反应，一系列悲观情景下资金也是连锁踩踏，最后也止不住连锁出清，是市场大跌底层逻辑。

3、接下来怎么看？
看配图2，也是周三在币安广场AMA里聊到的三个变量：
1）油价/通胀走势决定联储利率走向；
2）新政治生态下AI政策比当下市场预期的要更收紧和会略缓和些；
3）AI商业化是不是继续处于加速状态；

当然从个人角度核心是前两者、第三点当下看还是处于加速之中。

从另一个角度看市场一方面是对产业政策逆转和党争做悲观的定价、另一方面也是“死给你看”倒逼两党表态、特别是民主党到底要对AI政策逆转到什么程度？资金看不清、只能做悲观定价但说最悲观还要再看

text:
In September, 10,000 AI agents solved a Millennium Prize problem in 88 hours.

Dwarkesh's latest argument: math was the warm-up. Any domain where output can be checked gets compressed the same way. AI research is next. After that, most cognitive work with a verifiable result.

So the useful question moves from "when" to "who gets paid."

Roughly 60% of income goes to labor today. Production needs people and capital at the same time. Once an agent does the work for the cost of compute, that split breaks.

Capital wins. Which capital is the question we want to bet on.

Intelligence commoditizes. A handful of labs competing on price pushes token margins down. Generic AI exposure may capture surprisingly little of the value it creates.

Value pools at the bottlenecks code can't copy:

> power that can be connected this decade
> chips, HBM, advanced packaging
> licenses, because someone still has to sign
> distribution and trust
> data about the physical world

The last one is underpriced imo. The more decisions automated systems make, the more a wrong input costs. Verified real-world data ends up sitting under every automated decision.

Consumers get the largest absolute gain. Everything gets cheaper.

Your living standard goes up. Your share of output goes down. Both at once.

text:
Glad to see OpenRouter moving to privacy-preserving technologies! Privacy with pure math (like FHE) is the holy grail: you almost wouldn't have to worry about infrastructure security anymore, but its overhead compared to plaintext is still too large for business today.

That makes TEEs the only practical option right now: easiest to set up, with the lowest overhead.

But there's a big misconception about what TEEs actually offer.

By default, they encrypt VM memory, making it very hard for the host operator to inspect the machine and extract data. That helps when you don't trust the underlying provider (i.e. you are worried about AWS or Google looking in your VM). That's not the threat model OpenRouter is interested in here.

The main threat is bugs, misconfigurations, or exposed interfaces in the software itself allowing attackers to extract sensitive data, and a TEE does nothing to prevent that. Once you look past host-level snooping, the only remaining protection a TEE adds is remote attestation: a cryptographic guarantee of which exact software is running inside the machine.

Mentionning things like "encrypted TEE" (memory encryption is already built in) or "E2E encrypted" also oversimplify how TEEs work. Prompts still have to be decrypted inside the enclave to run inference. So, put the same vulnerable software that got hacked into a TEE, and you add zero security against software flaws; you just get a way to prove to users which exact software you're running.

The way to make this actually work is:
- harden and intensively audit the stack (with TLS terminating inside the enclave and attestation verified before routing),
- either open-source it with reproducible builds so anyone can verify the code behind the hash,
- or go the Apple / Google route: rely on trusted auditors and public transparency logs (like Apple's Private Cloud Compute) to vouch that a specific build hash is genuinely secure and privacy-preserving.

Either way, the security and privacy engineering has to be just as solid as if we were simply trusting providers to implement it properly. A TEE doesn't replace that work, it simply gives you verifiability that the audited stack is what's actually running.

So: Use of TEE to enforce ZDR and prove that this policy is respected sounds like a great match, this adds trust. But by no means do TEE add security / privacy by default. The encrypted memory feature is not that important.
author: randhindi
quoted_text:
Providers’ data-handling claims have mostly relied on self-attestation. This isn't going to be sufficient.

Just as continuous benchmarking and monitoring transformed the quality and reliability of inference both on and out of OpenRouter, we expect technical validation, auditing, and continuous testing to do the same for data policy enforcement.

Encrypted TEE (Trusted Execution Environment) inference will be a great way for providers to accelerate this.

We will keep raising the bar, and providers that want to be on OpenRouter will need to meet it.

quoted_text:
Pro tip: See traces from Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi in one place. 

In just 2-steps:

1 - Start Lens with Docker. You could use the curl command from here: 
https://t.co/8TT2v6Xej3

2 - On the LiteLLM gateway, set `general_settings. tracing. store. type` to lens. Each model call is then sent to Lens as a trace, owned by the key, user and team that made the call. Users see their own traces and their team's, and admins see all of them.

Now, when you open Lens, a coding session replays as a thread, the same way it looked in the terminal. Subagent work shows as a branch, and a divider marks where the context was compacted.

author: Carlitoswa_y
quoted_text:
the power of being nice 

london breakpoint was probably my tenth irl crypto conference. three years ago i walked into nfc lisbon alone, slightly uncomfortable. now i travel the world with an entourage and walk into rooms where people genuinely want to hang out with me. some take pictures for clout, or for reasons i'd rather not second guess. i never compromised my morals or pretended to be someone else. being willing to travel the world and meet online degens opened doors i never knew existed.

people remember how you made them feel. at a dinner during breakpoint i suggested we play credit card roulette. all phones and cards stacked in the middle, the waiter picks one, and the winner pays for everyone. right then i got a message and my phone lit up. bottom line, i paid for the whole table because the waitress liked the photo of my dog on my lock screen. best money i spent all week.

it's been about eighteen months since i left my family business. i traded stability for uncertainty. my parents told me not to do it. my friends echoed them. i went ahead anyway, all in on the most unstable industry there is, where people hide behind animal pfps pretending to be the ultimate shit.

i questioned that decision a lot. i doubt myself so much that i question everything. i deliberately took twelve months to think about what i wanted before i felt confident enough to walk away from the family business and the safety that came with it, to build something of my own. that something is my personal brand. i'm not here to sell you anything.

i've never really applied for a job. i don't even have a cv. i know people, and somehow that has always worked out. but there were moments when i thought it wouldn't, and those moments scared me. what if what comes next is actually... worse?

this morning i had coffee with an old friend. we talked about influencers and how i make a living these days. he's married to a very wealthy woman now, yet he still runs his business day to day like nothing changed. i do the same. the money from selling my earlier businesses is mentally out of reach for me. i can't spend it. it's locked in systems built to multiply themselves. what i live off now is online money. i know the rest is there, like he knows his wife's money is there. neither of us has raised our spending or our standard of living. we're happy where we are, with no need to show off to people we don't like.

we don't have a garage full of ferraris or a box full of watches. what we do have is a diversified portfolio. if we liquidated, neither of us would ever have to work again. we could drive around in a ferrari with two aps on each wrist. but in one of those quiet moments we asked ourselves: would that make us any happier?

most influencers, and most people who got rich quickly without really working for it, think peak life is showing what they could never afford to those who still can't afford it. instead of looking up, they're content bathing in the admiration of plebs.

a society is defined by who it puts on a pedestal. it used to be generals, adventurers and poets. now it's athletes at best and fame seekers at worst. we give our time and attention to fake personalities and scripted drama, all to avoid looking into ourselves.

my dad has told me this story since i was a kid. i still remember it vividly: alexander the great once stood over diogenes, who lived in a barrel, and offered him anything he wanted. diogenes asked him to step aside, because he was blocking the sun. the most powerful man in the world had nothing to offer a man who needed nothing. alexander supposedly said that if he weren't alexander, he'd want to be diogenes.

so i'm here because i want to be here. i don't have to be. i don't have to take any gig or promo i don't stand behind. i don't have to beg or suck up to anyone. my free will brought me here, and what i did earlier in life gives me the freedom to be who i want to be. few people can say that.

i'm grateful for this journey and excited for what's still to come. if you're my friend and you support me along the way, i'll always have your back.

everyone thinks of epicurus as the pleasure guy. in reality he lived on bread, water and friends in a garden outside athens. he said that of all the things wisdom gives us for a happy life, by far the greatest is friendship. 2,300 years later, it's still the best trade one can make.

few probably read all of this, if you did, i'm proud of you and just wanted to say thanks! :)

six months ago I wrote that propAMMs could redraw the power map of DeFi. well they did. six months from an emerging idea to billions in weekly volume. amazing work @class_lambda @gattacahq @alignedlayer @polfinance_ 

today propAMMs are processing 2.24 billions dollars in weekly volume on @ethereum, roughly 35% of Uniswap's 6.4 billions dollars.

a propAMM is basically a digital market where professional market makers continuously update their buy and sell prices in real time, so traders can get prices closer to what an asset is actually worth right now. binance has to run the entire financial marketplace itself. on ethereum, thousands of applications share the same underlying financial infrastructure, so a market maker can focus almost entirely on offering the best possible price.

there are three ways a product grows:
1. better marketing (Liquid Death, Red Bull)
2. better product (macOS/iOS, Claude)
3. better technology that creates better economics

we are doing the third. we just connect companies with better tech and since we provide better technology people just use us

ethereum produces a block every 12 seconds, but markets move in milliseconds. our infrastructure lets market makers continuously update their prices while the block is being built. this dramatically reduces the risk of trading against stale prices, which lets them quote tighter spreads and gives traders better execution

better technology changes the economics of the market

we will soon do $100 billion through this infrastructure without marketing and without a consumer facing product. we don't need to convince people to use it. since the price is better, the flow follows

we're just getting started. we will make Ethereum the best place to trade on earth

We've been working on something similar with @LambdaClass, @alignedlayer and @polfinance_ since @EthCC, great work by @kubimensah and @titanbuilderxyz.

This will change things very fast. The bid ask spread is the hidden tax every trader pays on every trade. Tighter spreads mean better prices, more volume, and deeper liquidity.

Right now Uniswap owns DeFi, Binance owns CEX, and Solana ate part of Ethereum's lunch.

If PropAMM brings spread compression to Ethereum onchain, things change entirely and Ethereum will become the best place to trade. Traders follow liquidity, liquidity follows better prices. Better prices come from tighter spreads.

All of it gets contested: Uniswap's dominance, Solana's momentum, Binance's volume. PropAMM on Ethereum could redraw the entire power map of this ecosystem.

text:
it's high time you admit that you're playing the wrong game in crypto.

you can't spend all day doomscrolling on x, getting your alpha from the same KOLs as everyone else, buying the same tokens, and somehow expect to consistently outperform the market.

crypto is one of the most aggressive PvP markets in the world, yet some people are playing a game you don't even know exists.

a few days ago, i came across the story of @3i, a trader who claims he and his friends made over $6m trading CASHCAT and PONS.

these guys were monitoring BitGo's public GitHub repo, tracking Wintermute wallets and studying patterns from previous Robinhood listings. they spotted a code update for CASHCAT 10 days before Robinhood announced its listing.

anyone could have seen that code update. very few would have understood its significance.

that's the kind of edge people are competing with in this industry.

look at someone like Cbb0fe. from farming Blur to arbitraging equity perps on Hyperliquid against TradFi markets, he keeps finding ways to make money without necessarily having a directional thesis on the asset he's trading.

meanwhile, some of you are emotionally attached to tokens because you've convinced yourselves that good tech automatically translates into price appreciation.

the market doesn't owe you money for being intellectually right about a project.

crypto is mostly game theory and mechanism design played by irrational actors in a PvP format.

you and a VC can be bullish on the exact same project, but your cost basis and incentives are completely different. by the time you're celebrating a 2x, the VC could be sitting on a 50x and looking for liquidity to exit.

human psychology explains why people refuse to buy something at a $50m valuation but suddenly develop conviction in the same thing at $500m.

copywriting and distribution explain why mediocre products sometimes attract more capital than products with superior tech.

on the uglier side, you have hackers who understand certain pieces of infra better than the devs who built them, and dishonest KOLs who have figured out how to monetize the financial desperation of their followers.

you need to understand that these are some of the people you're up against.

and no, the solution isn't necessarily to become a better trader. some people have had the balls to start building because they've realized there's more money to be made solving the problems traders have than competing with them every day.

even the little i've managed to achieve in this space came from refusing to follow the crowd and being willing to go the extra mile. learning copywriting, understanding DeFi and figuring out distribution opened doors for me that buying the right token never did.

of course, going the extra mile comes at a cost. you could spend six months learning something without making a dollar from it. you could build something nobody wants. hell, you could do everything right and still lose money.

but imagine spending five years in crypto and the only skill you've developed is knowing which accounts to follow for alpha.

in an industry where people are increasingly outsourcing their thinking to KOLs and AI, curiosity and the ability to figure things out independently are becoming more valuable.

if your entire strategy depends on someone else discovering an opportunity and being generous enough to tell you about it, you're probably the easiest player to beat in this market.

text:
I recently set up a Health Coach with Grok @bot.

Here is how I use it:
- Track food I eat (I send photo of each meal)
- Track all workouts
- Track all sleep metrics
- Track daily weight

The bot is useful because it can receive information, while also giving specific instructions and adjustments.

Some of the data is manually inputted like workouts and food. Other data is automatically sync'd from Apple Health, Garmin, Eight Sleep, or other measurement tools.

On top of the bot interface, I had the bot build a dedicated website and dashboard so I can see visuals of how things are changing/improving over time.

Lastly, the bot has scheduled tasks to keep me on track. 

If I don't upload a meal or workout, the bot proactively reaches out asking for the information. The bot also orders me the same lunch meal every day at the same time, so I don't risk straying from the plan. 

This type of health coach is really simple to set up and I am surprised at how effective it has been. 

My goal is to use the Health Coach bot for 1 year. It will be interesting to see what happens to my health over that time. 

If you have built anything similar, please send me any ideas or suggestions you have. I would love to continue improving this setup.

text:
The fastest way I know to expose shallow security knowledge is to ask someone to build the mechanism they are reviewing.

When you implement the state transitions yourself, vague audit questions become concrete:

What must always remain true?
Who can change it?
Which external input can break the assumption?
How does the system recover?

That is why I like the build → audit → launch loop. Building is not separate from security training. It gives the reviewer a model precise enough to attack.

text:
Blessed Sunday Booelievers 🕊📖

On November 22, 1977, a handful of engineers achieved something extraordinary.

They made three completely different computer networks communicate as one.

No grand celebration. No billions of users watching.

Just a few people proving that systems built independently could still find a way to work together.

They were helping lay the foundations of what would become the internet.

49 years later, the world is still living on the foundations they built.

Think about that for a moment.

The friendships formed across oceans.

The families brought closer despite thousands of miles between them.

The knowledge placed within reach of a child born in a remote corner of the world.

The countless dreams that became possible because a few people believed computers should be able to communicate beyond their own networks.

They didn't know our names. Yet their work changed our lives.

And today, Ethereum carries that same spirit into a new frontier.

An open network where people who have never met can exchange value, verify ownership, and build applications upon shared, programmable infrastructure.

Where a developer with little more than a computer and an internet connection can create something the entire world can use.

Not because someone powerful opened a door for them.

But because the door was built to be open.

And perhaps that's what the greatest technological revolutions have always been about.

Not making a handful of people more powerful.

But giving millions of ordinary people possibilities they never had before.

The internet helped humanity share information across borders.

Ethereum is helping humanity coordinate, exchange value, and build together across those same borders.

Different generations. Different technologies.

The same belief that the world becomes better when we connect rather than divide.

And somewhere today, someone is building something on Ethereum that may change the life of a person who hasn't even been born yet.

They may never meet.

They may never know each other's names.

But that is the beauty of building something greater than yourself.

You don't need to witness every life you change for your work to matter.

You only need to leave the door open for those who come after you.

Blessed are those who build what others will inherit.

Blessed Sunday Booelievers. 🙏📖⟠

text:
Crypto 最有意思的地方，也许不是它创造了多少财富，而是它把人性压缩进了一个高速运转的实验场

贪婪、恐惧、虚荣、信任、背叛、理想主义、机会主义……

现实世界可能需要十几年才能暴露的东西，在 Crypto 里有时只需要一个市场周期

有些人通过牛市认识财富，通过熊市认识风险

有些人通过成功认识自己的能力，通过失败才认识自己的局限

也有人经历了很多轮周期，却始终没有改变，因为他们只记住了价格，没有真正理解发生了什么

所以我觉得，一个人在 Crypto 待了多少年，其实没有那么重要。

重要的是，这些年究竟让他变得更自由，还是更依赖市场；更理解世界，还是更擅长迎合世界

这也让我想到原文最后一句：

Crypto is life.

它不一定意味着 Crypto 就是人生的全部

也可以理解为：Crypto 只是人生的一面放大镜。你在这里如何面对金钱、欲望、信任和不确定性，大概率也反映了你如何面对生活

而我认为还能再往前走一步：

真正的自由，不是拥有足够多的钱从而不必参与任何游戏，而是即使身处游戏之中，也不会忘记自己为什么而来
author: yueya_eth
quoted_text:
Lessons learned from 15 years in crypto:

1) Run your race and focus on reality over the perception game. Can’t tell you how many founders and VCs who looked “legit” here at one time have come and gone. If the timeline is shilling a narrative, it’s a good time to take the other side of the bet. The best bet is on yourself.

2) Believe in something more than money and attention. The money and attention comes and goes but long term belief in a broader mission is what will keep you engaged and growing and is the only way to win.

3) Lead with curiosity. Understand products, don’t just believe narratives. Understand what the narratives are too but be skeptical when they are projected on you too strongly. Double down on what you like.

4) Bet on people who are similarly running their own race with a belief in something more and curious mindset.

These apply outside of crypto too of course. Crypto is life.

text:
推荐好文。非常通透的讲清楚了AI/半导体集体暴跌的原因，非常细腻。

分享几个我很认同的观察
1. 市场突然转向的根本变化为CapEx资金结构
CapEx从内部造血转向外部融资，五大云厂中已有四家（AMZN、GOOGL、META、ORCL）单季自由现金流被 CapEx 击穿转负。

这意味着 AI 基建正在从科技巨头依靠自身现金流扩张，逐渐转向依赖外部股权与债务融资。

2. 订单乘数为产能过剩埋下了伏笔

100 美元的真实模型算力需求， 模型厂向大云厂购买 100 美元算力，大云厂向 Neocloud 转租 80 美元算力。

最终 100 美元的终端需求，可以在产业链不同环节形成 180 美元的收入记录。

这有点像银行的“货币乘数”。

3. 牛鞭效应，下游 CapEx 降 20%，上游订单可能降 40%–60%

假设五大云厂将年度 CapEx 从 8,200 亿美元降至 6,500 亿美元。

对云厂而言，只是减少新增投资，存量业务仍可增长；但对上游芯片、存储和光模块厂商而言，去库存、取消重复锁单和削减新订单可能同时发生。

4. 产能周期错配：2027–2028 年的潜在风险

当前大量晶圆厂、先进封装线和存储产线需要 1.5–2.5 年建设。

如果这些产能能在 2027 年下半年至 2028 年集中释放，恰好遇到云厂放缓 CapEx，中游制造商就可能面临双重挤压：新产能投产即降价，同时新增折旧开始侵蚀利润。

5. 长期订单不等于长期利润保障

当上游供应商高度依赖少数几家云巨头时，即使有长期采购协议，也未必能完全抵御需求逆转。

一旦客户无法消化既定采购量，供应商可能被迫接受延期交货或重新议价。

缺货时掌握定价权的是供应商；供过于求时，议价权又会迅速回到大客户手中。

6. 宏观端，AI从“化债解药”到“系统性脆弱源”

AI 原本被寄望于通过生产率革命，支撑美国经济增长并缓解债务压力。

但在商业回报尚未完全兑现之前，巨额 CapEx 已经开始挤压企业现金流、推高融资需求，并加剧电力、能源和基础设施的供给压力。成为了民众的假想敌。所以限制CapEx其实也是为了解决民生和内部矛盾。

结论就是，CapEx限速基本势在必行，而上游高毛利的硬件公司会首当其冲，很多27、28的盈利前瞻都是bullshit，不用看了，肯定大打折扣。

The Riemann hypothesis has stood for 167 years. Today an Anthropic mathematician claimed a proof with Claude, released only as 17.4 million lines of Lean.

ζ(s) = 0 implies Re(s) = ½ for every nontrivial zero. Trillions of zeros have been checked and all lie on the critical line; the first ten appear in the plot as green dots on Re(s) = ½. In August Claude lifted the proven density of zeros on that line from 41.6 % to 67.2 %. The new claim asserts the remaining gap is closed, and the same argument also settles the generalized hypothesis.

A machine-checked formalization still awaits human review. The Clay prize requires a published paper and two years of community acceptance.

A computer can now certify what no human has yet fully understood.

text:
So The Altruists on Netflix is making people who were actually involved in the FTX collapse come out and share their side of what happened.

This time it was Yi He, co-founder and co-CEO of Binance, who shared some interesting details about SBF and his relationship with Binance.

Apparently, SBF personally sponsored the first Binance Blockchain Week dinner, and the person he was most interested in meeting at the time wasn’t CZ, but Justin Sun.

According to Yi He, SBF looked up to Justin so much that he later recreated the billboard campaign in San Francisco where Justin had paid to have his own face displayed.

But what’s particularly interesting is what happened as FTX started growing.

According to Yi He, SBF bought back equity at a price far below the market valuation before securing large-scale funding at a much higher valuation.

At the same time, he was:

- Making political donations to both parties in Washington
- Lobbying US politicians
- Running a negative PR campaign targeting Binance

We move to November 2022, when SBF called CZ asking for help, he told him that FTX was simply experiencing a liquidity problem.

But according to Yi He, in less than 24 hours, FTX executives were leaving the group chat and resigning one after another.

Not a single one of them could figure out how much money was actually missing, and they couldn’t even locate the stablecoins,

The court would later disclose that the shortfall exceeded $8B

text:
Clanker Builders: you don’t need KOLs or an FNF of trenchers to support your launch.

They will only farm you because your incentives are fundamentally unaligned. 

You want to bootstrap yourself to build something interesting. They want to make a quick trade. Neither is wrong. You’re just playing different games.

My advice for would-be clankers: 

🤖 Stealth launch your token in the middle of the night, before you even make a public X account and definitely before you breathe a word to anyone outside the team (except maybe the Clanker team for launch support).

🤖 If this is a token for a project you plan to build on, take at least 10% of supply, ideally 20%, and lock everything above 5% of total supply in a multi-month, uncancellable vesting contract using something trusted like Sablier. This shouldn’t be difficult to do with a dev buy. If you can’t afford 10%, get at least 5%, lock all of it, and use every penny of your post-launch WETH fees to get to 10% minimum.

🤖 Once the token is live and you’ve accumulated the supply you need, start planning the public launch. Push the site to prod, make the X account, pay dex. If your team is vetted and trusted and the idea is good, we can help amplify it then.

Let the FNFs and trading groups prove they’re real trenchers by finding your idea on the open market like everyone else. 

(btw if you’re just making a meme, probably most of this doesn’t apply. Send it.)

Now you’ve got a setup where:

- Snipers can get fucked (respectfully) 
- Traders prove their worth by catching your launch signals when you’re ready.
- People who actually want to support your project have a shot at getting in at a reasonable mc.

I think this playbook would’ve eliminated 90% of the issues we’ve seen with recent @clanker_world launches from good teams.

So if you’re about to slide into my DMs for launch help, please read this first.

text:
it's high time you admit that you're playing the wrong game in crypto.

you can't spend all day doomscrolling on x, getting your alpha from the same KOLs as everyone else, buying the same tokens, and somehow expect to consistently outperform the market.

crypto is one of the most aggressive PvP markets in the world, yet some people are playing a game you don't even know exists.

a few days ago, i came across the story of @3i, a trader who claims he and his friends made over $6m trading CASHCAT and PONS.

these guys were monitoring BitGo's public GitHub repo, tracking Wintermute wallets and studying patterns from previous Robinhood listings. they spotted a code update for CASHCAT 10 days before Robinhood announced its listing.

anyone could have seen that code update. very few would have understood its significance.

that's the kind of edge people are competing with in this industry.

look at someone like Cbb0fe. from farming Blur to arbitraging equity perps on Hyperliquid against TradFi markets, he keeps finding ways to make money without necessarily having a directional thesis on the asset he's trading.

meanwhile, some of you are emotionally attached to tokens because you've convinced yourselves that good tech automatically translates into price appreciation.

the market doesn't owe you money for being intellectually right about a project.

crypto is mostly game theory and mechanism design played by irrational actors in a PvP format.

you and a VC can be bullish on the exact same project, but your cost basis and incentives are completely different. by the time you're celebrating a 2x, the VC could be sitting on a 50x and looking for liquidity to exit.

human psychology explains why people refuse to buy something at a $50m valuation but suddenly develop conviction in the same thing at $500m.

copywriting and distribution explain why mediocre products sometimes attract more capital than products with superior tech.

on the uglier side, you have hackers who understand certain pieces of infra better than the devs who built them, and dishonest KOLs who have figured out how to monetize the financial desperation of their followers.

you need to understand that these are some of the people you're up against.

and no, the solution isn't necessarily to become a better trader. some people have had the balls to start building because they've realized there's more money to be made solving the problems traders have than competing with them every day.

even the little i've managed to achieve in this space came from refusing to follow the crowd and being willing to go the extra mile. learning copywriting, understanding DeFi and figuring out distribution opened doors for me that buying the right token never did.

of course, going the extra mile comes at a cost. you could spend six months learning something without making a dollar from it. you could build something nobody wants. hell, you could do everything right and still lose money.

but imagine spending five years in crypto and the only skill you've developed is knowing which accounts to follow for alpha.

in an industry where people are increasingly outsourcing their thinking to KOLs and AI, curiosity and the ability to figure things out independently are becoming more valuable.

if your entire strategy depends on someone else discovering an opportunity and being generous enough to tell you about it, you're probably the easiest player to beat in this market.

quoted_text:
Sharing my pstack NSWF prompt. Your repo will never be the same...in a good way of course:

Use /poteto-mode on this repo. First, find the mistakes agents and humans keep repeating here: read the git log, past bug fixes and review comments. Then make each one impossible instead of documenting it. Try architecture first, then types, then a lint whose error names the fix, then a test. Delete comments that restate code, and encode the constraint behind any comment that matters (/no-comments). Where concurrency, retries or state machines cause real bugs, write a formal model that replays a past bug and fails on it (/create-formal-verification-skill), and run it in CI. Replace unit tests that pin implementation with those models plus real DB and e2e tests, but keep every test that guards security or legal behavior. Ship one verifiable PR per step, and prove each check catches a real past mistake before you trust it.

text:
BTC跌到5.5万，很多人已经在问是不是彻底凉了。

我的看法是，现在已经接近可以下手的位置了。但真正的底部，可能还要等AI那边再出一次问题。

先说币圈。

我不觉得这个行业死了。

合约、预测市场、meme还是有人玩，稳定币和RWA也在被传统金融认真推进。DTCC在做证券代币化，银行和交易所也都在试。

币价跌成这样，但这些东西反而在慢慢进入传统金融系统。

所以我觉得，币价跌和行业有没有未来，不能完全画等号。

再看BTC现在的位置。

200周均线已经失守，MVRV也快到1了，市场情绪差到很多人连账户都懒得看。

这些信号在过去几轮熊市里，基本都是接近大底的时候才会出现。

当然，不代表这次一定一样。但至少现在这个价格，已经值得认真考虑了。

真正让我觉得还可能有最后一跌的，是AI。

这几年AI吸走了太多钱。科技公司借钱建数据中心、买GPU，大家都在赌未来算力需求会一直增长。

但钱已经花出去了，未来能不能赚回来，其实还不知道。

而且现在AI行业很多融资是互相绑在一起的，一旦某个环节出问题，可能就不只是几家公司亏钱那么简单。

如果真的出现大规模去杠杆，美股、信用市场都会受影响，BTC大概率也逃不掉。

流动性紧张的时候，华尔街不会管你是不是数字黄金，能卖的都会卖。

所以我一直在想，BTC最后那个大底，会不会根本不是币圈自己跌出来的，而是AI出事之后被一起砸出来的。

但后面还有另一层逻辑。

AI现在已经是美国的国家战略了。

芯片、数据中心、电力、金融机构，太多东西都绑在上面。

如果AI真的出现系统性危机，美国能眼睁睁看着它崩掉吗？

我觉得很难。

最后大概率还是会想办法救。降息、提供流动性，严重的话甚至可能重新扩表。

当然，救市不一定马上等于放水。但如果最后真的走向大规模宽松，那才可能是下一轮BTC上涨最大的动力。

所以我现在比较倾向的判断是：

未来半年到一年，AI可能先把BTC砸出最后一个底，然后救AI的钱，又把BTC推上去。

当然，也可能完全看错。

AI可能根本不会出大问题，也可能就算出问题，美联储也不会大规模放水。

还有一种可能是，这轮周期真的变了。AI吸走了太多资金，币圈再也回不到以前那种疯狂的状态。

这些都有可能。

但最近我一直在想一件事。

AI发展得越快，很多东西反而越不值钱了。

以前写文章、做视频、写代码，都需要花不少时间。现在AI几分钟就能做出来，以后可能连很多人的工作都能替代。

当越来越多的东西可以被无限生产，真正稀缺的东西，会不会反而更值钱？

这也是我一直看好BTC的一个原因。

它就2100万枚，没有哪个公司能决定多发一点，也没有哪个政府能因为缺钱就让它增发。

当然，稀缺不代表一定涨，没人愿意买，再稀缺也没用。

但如果未来AI真的让很多东西变得过剩，那这种不能随便增加供应的资产，我觉得可能会越来越有意思。

我不知道5.5万是不是底，也不知道后面会不会跌到4万甚至更低。

只是觉得，接下来半年到一年，可能是很值得关注的一段时间。

很多人以前在BTC十几万的时候说，跌到5万一定买。

现在真跌到这里，又开始担心它归零。

其实我也能理解。价格一直跌的时候，谁都会怀疑自己是不是看错了。

但对我来说，现在真正想验证的不是BTC什么时候反弹，而是一个更简单的问题：

如果AI让这个世界越来越多的东西变得不值钱，那种无法人为增发、谁也控制不了的资产，会不会反而越来越值钱？

买不买，每个人自己决定。

我只是觉得，这个位置，值得认真看一眼。

⚠️ALERT: Hackers are now running ads in 47 countries that can STEAL CRYPTO SEED PHRASES from iPhones.

Security firm Confiant tracked the group, MoldyRoost, across more than 480 ad domains since May.

On a vulnerable iPhone, simply opening the page behind one of its ads is enough to trigger the attack.

You're at risk if your iPhone runs iOS 18 or older and you use crypto wallets like MetaMask, Phantom or Trust Wallet.

The flaws are in iOS itself, not in the wallet apps.

It reads your iOS version, then picks 1 of 4 exploit kits that Confiant calls "nation-state-grade."

They're built to take:

1. Wallet seed phrases
2. Passwords saved in your keychain
3. Messages and photos

One kit is aimed at fully updated iOS 18 phones, and its range runs all the way to iOS 26.

Confiant says it has seen no iOS 26 exploit code, and Apple had patched all 6 DarkSword flaws by iOS 26.3.
