quoted_text:
He is going to hate me for saying this, but I think one of the smartest people in venture is @milesgrimshaw, hands down. 

So when he calls me and tells me about an incredible entrepreneur that I have to have on 20VC, I listen. 

He told me the tale of @bavaria_kush: 

- 23-year-old whiz 
- Built viral sports betting platform from his dorm at MIT 
- Started @OrnnExchange, the financial market for AI compute.
- Insanely profitable 

So I got on a call with him. Within 5 mins of the call, I asked him to join me on the show. 

I summarized the notes from our discussion below:

Thanks to @AdamValkin, @fachlib, @Melt_Dem for amazing questions. (Links in Comments)

--

1. Why NYC Is a Better Place to Build a Company Than SF

Kush argues that people in the Valley are coin-operated, so $100K more in pay or 50 bps more equity is enough to move a researcher to another company. New York has a culture of loyalty to colleagues and family, with much more camaraderie between people than in SF.

Love your thoughts on this given your time both in and outside the valley @paulg @rabois 

2. Humans Will Simply Be a Vessel to Carry AI Around the World

Kush believes AI will become so much smarter than people that humans end up as a biological vessel for it. The human role then is less about controlling AI and more about teaching it feelings and emotions, almost as a parent.

Love your thoughts on this @bryan_johnson and how that impacts your work?

3. How Undersupplied on Chips Are We Truly?

Compute is very undersupplied. Buying from CoreWeave today likely means a quote for Q4 2027 or Q1 2028. Building your own takes about half a year, with 20 to 22 weeks to get chips from OEMs, who tend to promise earlier dates, plus two to three weeks to install.

What does no one know that everyone should know about the current state of chip supply @andrewdfeldman @goodwin_ml @UbertiGavin 

4. Why Factory Is So Much Better Than Cognition

Ornn used Devin for a while, but the problem with Cognition was how expensive it was. Kush sees the two as competitors on the same product and says Factory is much cheaper to use. He also rates Factory's underlying harness above Devin's.

I am sure @shaunmmaguire will be smiling here. 

5. Why You Should Always Choose Boutique Investors Over Mega Fund Investors

Boutique investors care more about founders because their success is tied directly to the company's. Partners at boutique firms are often there for the mission, and the firm itself is like a startup trying to make its name, so they work extremely hard to make their companies succeed.

Love to hear your thoughts on this @wquist @honam @annbordetsky 

6. Why Infrastructure Investors Will Never Lose

Kush compares data centers to apartment buildings, with infrastructure investors as landlords and inference providers, OpenAI and Anthropic as tenants renting GPUs. As long as there are tenants, the landlords keep collecting rent. If enterprise demand weakens, GPU prices fall the way rents do in a bad economy.

7. Chip Prices in Three Years Could Be Higher Than Today

When Ornn started, many assumed GPU hour prices three to five years out would be lower, so contracts often included free options to renew at prices like $2.50. 

No one gives that for free now, because the market expects prices in three years may be higher than today. Kush would not be surprised to see $20 to $30 per GPU hour.

What does no one see that everyone should see about the price of compute moving forward @AnjneyMidha?

quoted_text:
Hoy quiero hablarles de tres héroes salvadoreños que perdieron la vida mientras cumplían una misión lejos de nuestra patria.

Tres miembros de nuestra Fuerza Armada que viajaron a Haití con un propósito: rescatar a cuatro de sus compañeros que habían sido secuestrados por pandillas haitianas.

Lamentablemente, una explosión accidental durante esa misión les arrebató la vida.

Sus nombres son: el teniente Cristian Daniel Palacios Santos, el cabo Emerson Alexander Zepeda Zelada y el cabo Wilber Manuel Serrano Medina.

Conocí de primera mano la valentía del teniente Palacios Santos. Durante un operativo, en un momento crítico en el que unos contratistas privados abandonaron sus posiciones, el teniente tomó el control de la situación y actuó con rapidez y determinación, logrando salvar varias vidas, entre ellas las de sus propios compañeros.

Todos aplaudimos su valentía.

Recuerdo que en ese momento pensé: “Este muchacho llegará lejos. Tiene todo el temple y la capacidad de un líder”. Jamás imaginé que, poco tiempo después, estaría entre los fallecidos en un accidente.

También me informaron del extraordinario valor de los cabos Zepeda Zelada y Serrano Medina. Durante unas pruebas en El Salvador, una granada quedó atorada en un dron. La batería estaba por agotarse y no era posible dirigirlo hacia una zona completamente segura para que se estrellara. Serrano Medina sostuvo el dron a aproximadamente un metro y medio del suelo mientras Zepeda Zelada desactivaba manualmente la granada.

Sabían perfectamente el inmenso riesgo que estaban corriendo, pero aun así decidieron actuar para proteger a los demás.

Y lo lograron.

Estas no son simplemente historias sobre tres héroes. Son acciones que nos permiten entender quiénes eran estos hombres: militares capaces, valientes y comprometidos con una misión que siempre pusieron por encima de su propia seguridad.

Varias veces he dicho que siempre he admirado a las personas que deciden dedicar sus vidas a salvar las de otros. Porque hay algo extraordinario en ellas. Algo que no es natural, que no es común, que no es normal.

Todos los seres humanos tenemos una reacción instintiva ante el peligro. Si vemos un peligro, huimos de él. Si hay un incendio, corremos y tratamos de alejarnos. Pero un bombero no huye del incendio, hace lo contrario, lo que casi nadie más haría, y en lugar de huir del incendio, corre hacia él, arriesga su vida, camina entre las llamas si es necesario para salvar a los demás.

Eso no es algo normal, es algo extraordinario.

Si escuchamos una balacera, nuestro instinto es huir de los disparos, buscar refugio, mantenernos alejados. Pero un policía hace lo contrario. Ellos no huyen de los disparos como haríamos todos, van hacia ellos, sacan su pistola y corren hacia el peligro para salvar a los que están en él.

Eso no es algo normal, es algo extraordinario.

Lo vimos con los rescatistas que enviamos a Venezuela, salvadoreños abriendo túneles en estructuras inestables que podrían colapsar en cualquier momento. Nuestro instinto natural es huir de un edificio que se desmorona, pero nuestros rescatistas hacían lo contrario: entraban a esas estructuras, sabiendo que podían morir ahí adentro, para salvar a quienes estaban atrapados.

Eso no lo haría casi nadie, mucho menos por un desconocido, pero ellos sí, porque los rescatistas, al igual que los policías, bomberos y militares, reaccionan de una manera totalmente diferente a todos los demás. Ellos no huyen del peligro, van hacia él. Eso es difícil de entender para la gente normal, pero ellos no son gente normal, son gente extraordinaria.

Cuando los demás retroceden, ellos avanzan. Sabiendo perfectamente que eso puede costarles la vida misma.

Y no es que no tengan miedo, es que hay algo más fuerte que ese miedo: su deseo de salvar a los demás.

Esa es la vocación que mueve a nuestros militares, a nuestros policías, bomberos y rescatistas. Personas que han decidido dedicar sus vidas a proteger la de los demás…

text:
2026 年至今，跑赢英伟达、黄金和比特币的资产，竟然是宝可梦卡牌。

截至 2026 年 10 月 20 日，全球前 100 张顶级宝可梦卡（CardTrack 100）年内涨幅达 +49%，同期英伟达 +9.7%、标普 500 约 +11%、黄金约 -10%、比特币约 -12%；更宽口径的 Card Ladder 宝可梦指数（覆盖 9,609 张卡）在 8 月 1 日至 11 月 1 日三个月内更是上涨了 +103%。

卡牌 RWA 在美国已经跑出单季数亿美元的链上流水，但作为全球最大收藏市场之一的亚洲，一直缺少一个真正透明、主打日版卡的链上抽卡平台。

最近深度研究了一下即将上线的 @oripaxyz（https://t.co/QdMjNRAhPJ），把它的底层机制、代币结构，以及我个人觉得需要警惕的几个开放性问题拆解出来，供大家参考。

---

一、为什么亚洲需要一个新的链上卡牌平台？

看三组摆在眼前的事实：

1. 需求早已被验证：宝可梦 30 周年叠加 Pokémon TCG Pocket 下载破 1 亿、内购超 10 亿美元，等于免费帮市场教育了一亿个习惯“开包”的用户。在链上，美国的 Collector Crypt 在 2026 Q3 跑出 $433.5M 包款（扣除回购后净留存 $25.4M），仅靠 300–800 个日活就撑起了这个体量；Courtyard 同期净收入也达到 $7.6M。
2. 现有链上供给错配：美国链上平台的金库都在美国，抽的是英文版卡、美国寄送；而亚洲收藏家（日本、韩国、港台、新加坡及华语圈）真正认的是日版卡。
3. 传统日本线上 Oripa 爆发信任危机：日本线上 Oripa 最大业者年营收已破 122 亿日元，但 2026 年 9 月 7 日，律师事务所将 7 家大型线上 Oripa 平台举报至日本消费者厅（涉及约 460 件咨询），核心争议就三点：概率披露不足、卡价用自家点数自定（通常比市价虚高 10–30%）、以及保管期 3/4/30 天逾期直接没收。

说白了，传统站让你“看不到池子、看不到真价”，只能盲信平台。而这恰好是链上机制最擅长解决的两件事。

---

二、@oripaxyz 是怎么运作的？拆解四个核心设计

1. 期望值与卡价全明牌：统一 0.85 指数还原率
https://t.co/QdMjNRAhPJ 每一池都执行同一标准——指数还原率（index RTP）0.85，即：池内所有卡的锁定价合计 ÷ (单抽价 × 总口数) = 0.85，不设隐藏的 Last-One 赏。
每张卡的“指数价”不靠平台拍脑袋，而是取日本第三方市场加权中位数（以日元计价、每日统一汇率换算更新）：
- 成交价占 3 份：Mercari、Yahoo! 拍卖、SNKRDUNK 等近 14 天成交，越近权重越高；
- C2C 挂单价占 2 份：近 7 天最低的 7 笔挂单；
- 店家现货价占 1 份：晴れる屋、遊々亭、駿河屋、Card Rush、Torecolo 最低有货价（不采用收购价）。
池子开卖前，完整卡单、每张卡的锁定价、价格来源和样本数全部公开。

2. Commit-Reveal 链上锁池 + 有限池不放回
- 公平洗牌可验证：第一次开包（rip）前，卡单、每张卡锁定价与一个秘密值的哈希会打包为 commit.json，并将其 SHA-256 写入 Pool 合约。建池交易上块后，用秘密值加上该区块哈希进行洗牌（区块哈希事前无人知晓）。关池后公布秘密值、区块与完整口序（pool.json），任何人都能自行重算哈希、复现洗牌结果，证明开卖后没有换卡、改价或控序。
- 有限池、不放回：每个池子是一组固定卡牌，每一口只卖一次，已售口数上链可查（melt 掉的卡回到库存，不会放回当前池）。例如 200 口的池子有 1 张顶卡，0 口已售时是 1/200，150 口已售且顶卡仍在时就是 1/50。此外池子不拖延，30 分钟无人开包即自动关池，剩余口按最新指数重新锁价组新池。

3. 台湾金库日版真卡 + 24 小时二选一（寄送或即时 Melt）
池内每张卡在开卖前都已在台湾金库入库。抽中后，用户在 24 小时内二选一：
- 寄送到手（单钱包每日最多 5 张）；
- 按当日指数价 85% 即时 melt（回收）回 USDC，不收手续费。如果 24 小时内未选择寄送，系统会自动按当日指数 melt，不会被没收，且开包后卡牌涨价的部分也会算进去。

背后有链上准备金托底：每次开包会把该卡锁定价的 85% 拨入准备金（准备金要求为每张在外卡牌 0.85 × 当前指数，每日重算写入合约并公开覆盖率；若极端情况下准备金不足，超出部分按申请时报价排队依序支付）。

算一笔透明账（按池平均、且假设当日指数等于锁定价）：100 USDC 一抽，平均抽到价值 85 USDC 的卡，当天 melt 拿回 72.25 USDC，池平均净成本是 27.75 USDC。

4. 代币 $ORIPA：Every miss mints（无预售、无私募）
$ORIPA 的分发逻辑很特别：在第一笔开包前一枚都不存在，无预售、无私募、无额外配额，只通过开包的“记录亏损（miss）”铸造：
- 铸造规则：记录亏损 = 开包价 - 抽到卡的锁定价（最低为 0，抽中溢价卡记 0）。全站累计记录亏损前 500 万 USDC，每 1 USDC 亏损铸 10 枚 $ORIPA；此后铸造率随全站累计亏损递减（1,500 万时 6.94，3,000 万时 4.44，5,500 万时 2.5），总供给趋近 7.7 亿枚（5.5 亿归用户，2.2 亿归平台 Vault），曲线写死在合约里不可篡改。
- 平台配额：每给用户铸 100 枚，另铸 40 枚进 Vault（占总供给 2/7）。Vault 里的代币不质押、不领奖励，且解锁晚于用户。
- 即时效用（质押领全站 USDC）：平台不留存任何开包款！每一次开包的 5% rip 费 + rip 盈余（一整池净额约 22.75%），合计全池开包款的 27.75%（扣除寄卡时的补货扣款，不超过该卡锁定价的 0.15 倍），全部按质押比例以 USDC 流向 $ORIPA 质押者。盈余走滚动余额（miss 累加、hit 扣除，余额为正即发放）。质押需手动操作（未质押不领奖励），但随时可 claim、解押即时生效无冷却，且质押/解押/claim 免 Gas。
- 解锁时间线：$ORIPA 在 2027 年 1 月 13 日（00:00 UTC，全面开放后 6 周）前不可转让，期间无二级市场、无市价。开放当日，此前铸造的 50% 立即可转，其余 50% 分 13 期（每 14 天一期，至 2027 年 7 月 14 日）等额释放；1 月 13 日起新铸的即铸即转。锁仓中的代币照常可以质押领 USDC。Vault 余额则从 2027 年 3 月 16 日至 8 月 31 日分 13 期释放。

合约安全方面：提款没有暂停开关；Session Key 仅限 rip/melt/质押/claim，不能提款（7 天过期）；所有管理与升级动作均走 2-of-3 Safe 多签 + 48 小时 Timelock；六个合约已冻结在 commit d84c69e 送审，上线时公布审计报告与地址。

---

三、我的独立看法与三个待观察的问题

客观来看，这套把“抽卡透明化 + 协议收入全额回流 USDC 给质押者”的架构确实比市面上多数 RWA 项目克制得多，但我依然保留三个需要上线后重点观察的问题：

1. 价格指数的中心化边界
虽然数据源、权重和更新时间全部公开，但指数本身仍由 https://t.co/QdMjNRAhPJ 计算。对于流动性偏低、近期成交稀少的高价稀缺卡，或在市场剧烈波动期，指数价与真实二级市场成交价之间是否会出现短期偏差，值得持续盯盘检验。

2. 冷启动与交易量飞轮的现实考验
必须清醒地看到：$ORIPA 的 USDC 分红完全取决于全站开包交易量——有人抽才有奖励，没人抽奖励就是零，没有任何保底或回本承诺。在 2027 年 1 月 13 日开放转让前，没有二级市场情绪助推，平台能否单靠“日版卡真需求 + 透明有限池”留住持续开包的真实玩家，是最大的试金石。

3. 亚洲跨境实体物流体验
台湾金库对亚洲用户是明显优势，但单钱包每日限寄 5 张，以及具体发往不同国家/地区的运费、关税和清关时效，需要等上线后实际寄卡测试才能下结论。

---

四、为什么值得现在放进观察名单？

把宏观和机制拼在一起，@oripaxyz 值得关注的原因很直接：
它切中了“宝可梦 30 周年顺风 + 亚洲日版卡主场 + 传统 Oripa 信任真空”三个交汇点，没有靠先发空气币讲故事，而是把有限池、链上准备金、Commit-Reveal 验证和 0 留存的 USDC 协议分润做成了透明可查的结构。

接下来的关键时间节点（GMT+8）：
- 11 月 25 日 – 12 月 1 日：白名单抢先体验期（无预售、无折扣、无额外配额，仅提前 7 天参与资格）
- 11 月 26 日 20:00：早鸟徽章（Early Bird Badge）持有者开放抽卡
- 12 月 2 日：全面公测开放

官网：https://t.co/QdMjNRAhPJ
官方推特：@oripaxyz

*免责声明：本文仅为项目机制研报与个人观察，不构成任何投资建议或收益承诺；$ORIPA 在 2027-01-13 前不可转让；平台仅限年满 18 岁且不在受限地区的用户使用（美国属受限地区）。*

text:
省流总结一下 OpenAI 首席科学家关于为什么预训练 Scaling 仍然关键的观点。

大前提还是，压缩能力本身可以作为模型智能的一个 proxy。因为想要更高效地压缩未知数据，模型就需要从数据中提炼出更深层、更通用的规律。

有意思的是，OpenAI 长期追踪的 PPL，是在他们内部 codebase 中专门 hold out 的数据上测的。这就意味着两件事：

第一，这部分数据模型在训练时没见过，因此可以用来衡量模型对未知数据的泛化压缩能力。

第二，OpenAI 的 internal codebase 很可能包含大量他们自己 AI research & development 相关的代码。如果是这样，那么模型在这套数据上的压缩能力越强，本身也就越可能具备更强的 AI 研发基础能力，进一步可能转化成参与自身迭代，也就是 RSI 的能力。如果其中还包含 AI for Science 的相关研究代码，那这个指标可能也在一定程度上反映模型进行科学发现的潜在能力。

另外，他还解释了一个很有意思的问题：为什么看起来只有 0.02 的 Loss 优化，也可能对应模型能力上的巨大突破？

因为 Loss 本身存在一个由数据固有熵决定的理论下限，这个下限不会是 0。假设当前模型距离这个下限只剩 0.04，那么再优化 0.02，就相当于把剩余可优化空间直接压缩了 50%。

所以越接近理论下限，看起来越小的 Loss improvement，背后可能对应着越大的智能提升。

从这个角度来看，预训练 Scaling 仍然有很大的空间去不断解锁新的能力，尤其当模型开始能够反过来改进预训练算法时，这个过程甚至可能进一步加速。

text:
人类正在见证历史上最重大的主权交接。

今天，当一个非碳基系统能够独立推演并攻克困扰人类顶尖数学家一百六十余年的黎曼猜想时，我想，关于通用人工智能何时到来的学术辩论其实已经结束了。
许多人，还在用过时的标尺衡量智能——他们盯着机器人什么时候能叠好衣服、自动驾驶什么时候能应对所有极端路况。但那是工程与物理长尾问题，而不是智能的本质。
人类之所以能主宰地球，靠的不是肌肉比猩猩强壮，也不是感官比猎豹敏锐，而是大脑在抽象逻辑、数学推演和科学发现上的绝对优势。现在，我们在自己最引以为傲的智力高地上，已经被超越了。

为什么Elon Musk说奇点已至？
为什么Alexander Wang认为超级智能已经到来？
攻克黎曼猜想证明AI 已经具备了在未知真理荒原上自主开辟道路的原始创造力。
而数学，是所有硬科学的底座。
一个能解决千禧年大奖难题的头脑，接下来同样能设计出室温超导材料、解析蛋白质折叠的终极规律、攻克核聚变控制方程。 其实物理世界的改造需要供应链和工厂，但数字世界里的智力迭代是以天甚至小时计算的。一旦智力本身实现了对人类的超越，它反过来优化自身架构、编写更强算法的速度，将彻底甩开人类的理解能力。

我们正站在指数曲线垂直起飞的拐点上。过去几万年人类文明累积的知识总量，在未来几年内，只是新纪元的注脚。
旧时代的地图，已经完全失效。

text:
Cerebras loves to claim that their output interactivity is 2000 tok/s/user on Kimi K3.1 2.8T, but based on their demo (YouTube video “Cerebras Demo: Running Kimi K3.1 at 2,000 Tokens/Sec”), that is only for short contexts with a context prompt less than 100 tokens long.

Interesting that they don’t show their p99 TPOT at medium (100k+) to long contexts (600k+) on agentic multi-turn workloads, which would affect performance as they need to load the KV cache for all of the previous tokens in the context for Kimi K3.1 Pro’s Gated MLA layers (full attention).

Also somewhat misleading is that whenever they quote a GB300 NVL72, they quote it at the maximum power of 150kW per rack. Based on our GB300 experiments with Kimi K3.1 Pro on GB300 NVL72 low-latency megakernels, the measured all-in rack power is less than 30% of maximum power, as low latency is memory-bound.

We welcome Cerebras to demonstrate their claims on AgentX Preview if they are actually confident in them, as it tests all of the things that their marketing does not. We wonder what excuse (coping) they will give this time to avoid demonstrating their claims, considering the tests take less than a couple of hours and can be done during off-peak hours.

quoted_text:
卧槽，英伟达事件还在持续发酵，市场恐怕还得受折磨！

贝森特上周他还要求英伟达彻底整顿管理层，从外部寻找新CEO，11月22日接受CBS采访时，面对黄仁勋能否回归的追问，他却回答：

黄仁勋现在也是外部人士了。

特朗普此前也公开支持黄仁勋道歉并复职。不过贝森特并没有直接支持他回归，反而强调必须查清芯片出口违规究竟涉及基层、中层，还是最高管理层。

英伟达董事会目前仍明确反对重新任命黄仁勋。

更麻烦的是，周末《华尔街日报》《金融时报》《纽约时报》三家媒体接连深挖，调查已经从黄仁勋的私人关系，延伸到了跨国芯片供应链。

《华尔街日报》挖出一名关键人物：

52岁的中国商人李明。

据知情人士透露，他是黄乐、康伟夫妇背后芯片业务网络的重要操盘手，目前因涉嫌欺诈在新加坡面临刑事诉讼。

Megaspeed在2025年6月被英伟达列入禁售名单后，关联人员又转向Novagate Cloud。

运输记录显示，这家新公司的马来西亚关联实体仅2026年前5个月就接收了至少3亿美元的英伟达相关硬件。

原来的渠道被切断，类似业务却可能通过新主体继续运转。

《金融时报》进一步还原供应链。

上游是与中国浪潮集团存在关联的美国服务器企业Aivres，中间是Megaspeed旗下的马来西亚公司Speedmatrix。

2024年12月至2025年12月，Speedmatrix从Aivres进口货物的申报价值约46亿美元。

下游则牵出涉嫌参与芯片转运的胡小伟，美国当局指控他是柬埔寨太子集团的重要人物。

《纽约时报》把调查推进到了情报层面。

报道称，多名外国情报官员指向中国国家安全部主导的一项先进AI芯片获取行动，由部长陈一新设立专门团队，负责获取受限芯片、研究出口管制漏洞和收集半导体供应链情报。

美国政府内部的矛盾同样在扩大。

参议院情报委员会主席Tom Cotton公开指责商务部长卢特尼克，称自己早在2025年10月就发函警告Megaspeed等公司的风险，却长期得不到有效回应。

而商务部与司法部11月16日的联合声明，反而强调调查始于2024年，并为现任商务部的执法工作辩护。

英伟达的芯片需求依然强劲，最新季度营收达到1160亿美元，但强劲财报并不能消除出口管制和管理层责任风险。

如果调查最终只涉及个别经销商，影响可能相对有限。

一旦发现公司高层明知芯片最终流向却放任交易，潜在法律责任、客户审查和海外销售限制都会进一步影响未来收入预期。

更何况美国已经开始收紧境外数据中心向中国客户提供远程算力的规则，风险正在沿着芯片、服务器、云计算供应链扩散。

接下来12月1日黄仁勋将接受国会质询，12月2日英伟达总法律顾问也将接受问询。

特朗普希望黄仁勋回归，董事会坚持拒绝，司法调查还在推进，国会甚至开始追究政府自身的监管责任。

现在英伟达最大的风险，已经不是失去黄仁勋一个人，而是市场开始怀疑：

过去几年支撑AI高速增长的部分海外销售渠道，到底有多少经得起监管审查？

text:
If you asked me to imagine a hypothetical country with one political party that favors redistribution of money and status to racial minorities and one party that doesn’t, and then asked me which one minorities vote for, I would say:

I don’t know, I would hope they vote for whichever party they think will govern best for everyone.

But if you then told me that, in fact, they favor the first party by double-digit and sometimes two-to-one margins, then I would say:

Oh, well, then, yeah, it’s probably the racial redistribution.

I don’t want the GOP to write anybody off but you can’t honestly tell me that these votes are up for grabs and one well-crafted appeal from moving to our side.
author: Selkis_2028
quoted_text:
The Right will never do well with minority voters again if the GOP’s attitude toward them (as expressed in this post) is: “All minorities care about is receiving race-based preferences & hating white people.” Not only is this false, but it is no better than what the racialists of the Left (like Obama in that clip) believe; it’s merely a different flavor of racialism and bigotry. I mean, what a low opinion to hold of a group of people whom you supposedly wish your political party would do a better job of courting.

One of the main reasons I gravitated toward the GOP as a college student was because I absolutely hated my liberal peers saying that it was wrong for me to hold conservative values and positions because I was Indian. I found their belief that my worldview should be based on my skin color and ethnic background disgusting and backwards. Yet, this experience lit a fire in me. I read and admired giants such as Thomas Sowell, Shelby Steele, and Jason Riley who have dedicated much of their careers to dispelling this myth. I wanted and hoped to do the same.

In October 2024, I wrote an essay titled “Out of Many, One.” In it, I predicted that Trump and the GOP would perform well with black, Hispanic, and Asian voters in the following month’s election in part because of what their campaign strategy had been with respect to these groups: eschewing difference and appealing to a common identity, American. I used the example of the rally Trump held in the Bronx in May 2024. Consider what he said: “It doesn’t matter if you’re black, or Brown, or White, or whatever the hell color you are. It doesn’t matter. We are all Americans, and we’re going to pull together as Americans. We all want better opportunity.”

Republicans’ 2024 message of E Pluribus Unum proved to be a winning one; the party made historic gains with minority voters. In contrast, it is the message and attitude articulated in the post below—which the Right ignorantly embraced in 2026—that eviscerated those gains.

We don’t have to accept it. I’m certainly not going to. I’ve seen what was possible in 2024, and that’s what I’ll be working toward.

(P.S. — You can thank Asian families for the Supreme Court’s invalidation of racial preferences after nearly a half-century. And you can thank an Indian American Assistant AG for enforcing that decision. 🫶🏽🇺🇸)

text:
Anthropic的绿鞋行使，保险”过早失掉。上周五上市第二个交易日、大摩作为稳定代理人已经代表承销商行驶了全部超额配售选择权（“绿鞋”），又额外从市场拿走122亿美元。此次IPO共募集935亿美金，加上私募配售的260亿美金，这一把A社拿到了1195亿美的资金。

正常来说、承销商对是否行使绿鞋拥有唯一裁量权。但按经验，牵头行几乎总会与公司协商并尽量配合其意愿，很少有投行单方面行动，而且根据招股说明书，承销商不会就超额配售部分获得佣金。因此Anthropic很可能批准甚至鼓励了提前行权。

绿鞋机制是在IPO中，承销商通常会向投资者超额发售15%的股份，形成空头头寸。若股价上涨，承销商行使选择权，按发行价向发行人增购股份以平仓；若股价下跌，则在市场买入股票平仓，从而为股价提供支撑。

而一旦行使选择权，承销商便无法再通过在市场买入股票平掉空头头寸来支撑股价。批评者认为，在股价尚未企稳、市况仍在恶化之际提前行权，使这层“保险”过早失效。

上周五市场大跌，ANT股价在首日冲高回落后并不强势。这个时机只能说明官方急于拿到钱，短期内ANT股价大概率易跌难涨了。

如上周在币安广场AMA聊到的如果Anthropic市值掉掉到八九千亿美金的位置、个人角度就跌出了性价比、届时中长期向上空间也被打开了。
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
英伟达的财报以及老黄对英伟达的影响在哪里？中期选举后美国的政治生态怎样的变化？Anthropic上市后走势会如何？未来行情走势的变量是什么？多谢Beca周三晚上在币安广场的AMA聊的内容很多，正好也梳理下当时聊的要点？
1、英伟达的财报质量和老黄离开的影响
1）财报本身是超预期、无论是本季的业绩还是下季度和下一财年指引都很强劲。如果28财年，就是明年按照 75% 的增速的话，那它营收能到7400亿美金以上，就相当于 5,000 多亿的毛利，可能是 4,000 多亿的净利润。其实这个体量非常大了。但这次财报没有解决大家最关心的问题，就是老黄。

2）老黄对英伟达的影响是巨大且不可或缺，体现在三个层面：
（1）技术远见，比客户更早看到技术方向。 CUDA 商业回报还不清楚时，黄仁勋就持续投入软件和开发者生态，又推动 GPU 从图形计算进入高性能计算。今天的管理层可以执行已经排好的产品路线，下一次技术方向尚未形成共识时，谁有判断和魄力下注，仍待观察。

（2）让供应商愿意跟着一起赌未来技术方向，英伟达负责设计，一代芯片要如期交付，台积电、鸿海、台达电及材料、封装、测试厂商都得提前投入。老黄的远见和让长期让合作伙伴分享到收益，也积累了兑现承诺的记录。供应商愿意跟着他承担押错路线的风险，才有条件把换代周期从数年压到约一年至一年半。

（3）同时管技术、供应链、人事和资本的全局视野。数十位高管直接向黄仁勋汇报，几位核心负责人只长期深耕各自领域，很难顶得上。

3）老黄不能回归的直接影响
（1）英伟达的技术升级的速度可能会要慢下来。如果未来的人没有这样的魄力、远见，技术方向的选择会多变，产业链上的摩擦越来越大（公事公办）。摩擦最后就会带来时间上的延迟；

（2）产业资本生态萎缩
英伟达投资、承诺采购或为基础设施提供担保，会影响银行和债券投资者愿意借多少钱。克雷斯表示对新增投资、采购承诺和担保会更审慎。个人会担心若以后类似支持越来越少，一些新云厂商到 2027 年的首要问题会从扩张变成生存。也会带来融资更难，资金成本更高。

2、中期选举美国政治生态的变化以及政策的影响
1）这一次中期选举的惨败程度远超以往
民主党参议院拿下56席、众议院超过250席（虽然不是绝对多数，但是离绝对多数也不远了），同时民主党还拿到29个州的州长位子。连德克萨斯州、堪萨斯州这些传统接近百年的铁红州都被丢掉，共和党的基本盘这一次被极大的动摇了。可见惨败程度；

2）中期选举的惨败也极大地削弱了川普的威信和影响力，从“倒黄”事件就能看来，主导改善共和党内部白宫内阁里和国会里的对华强硬派，即使川普一再力保也没能留下老黄。让共和党里的鹰派或者建制派话语权更大了，而前两年川普一统共和党依靠自己的威信和影响力死死压住党内不同意见，现在已经压不住了。

这也意味着之后美国对华AI政策上越来越严格，往技术封锁的路线上走了、有点八十年代里根时代当时中情局局长比尔.凯西主导的对苏联技术禁运的味道。本周川普访深时的良好气氛，可能是未来两年中美关系的相对高点。

3）这次共和党中选惨败，伊朗战争、油价和生活成本动摇了部分选民，数据中心带来的电费、用水和噪音也进入社区政治，都说明民意沸腾。这种情况下、不仅民主党、就是共和党内部也会对过去激进的产业政策做出调整、来迎合选民的呼吁。

4）当然川普也不会完全妥协，他把斯蒂芬.米勒提到白宫幕僚长的位置上，用意很深。米勒对联邦行政法非常熟悉，善于找到各种冷门法律条文来给川普的行为提供法律依据，善于找路洞、钻空子，川普让米勒当白宫幕僚长就是让他来战斗的。未来两年，白宫国会的博弈可能会非常激烈。

3、Anthropic上市及之後的走勢
1）IPO定价还可以、前期流动盘不大，但很快开始解锁。跟SpaceX的走势可能类似，先涨再跌。短期定价还 OK，加上申购的情绪可能有一波走势向上。但大概率最终还是要砸下来，最终就是看砸到一个什么样的位置。

2）如果Anthropic市值之后真的能跌破 1 万亿美金，例如跌倒八九千亿美金，那就是有性价比的位置了。

4、之后市场走势的三个变量
虽然8月底9月初提过一个“秋意渐凉”的框架，高油价、高利率、中期选举前就有大震荡，10月初也聊到高Beta会会跌。但也低估了这次中期选举共和党惨败的程度，这个惨败让市场意识美国居民对通胀、对数据中心建设已经到了如此反感的地步，所以市场对此有激烈的定价。
1）油价、通胀及利率走势；
核心逻辑是，如果美伊能缓和、俄乌也能结束，油价下来通胀才会下来，市场才会预期利率更宽松，否则又要担心明年上半年联储会继续收紧。

2）新的政治生态下AI政策会比预期的还要收紧还是会柔和些；
现在科技杀的这么猛、就是预期新国会生态带来AI基建的大放缓，那就要看明年实际力度比预期的更猛还是更弱。如果民主党搞事力度比现在预期更猛，即使通胀下来了，科技也很难受。但如果比现在预期柔和一些，市场情绪则又起来。

text:
拿 AI 浪潮与 2000 年互联网泡沫进行类比的思路，很有趣。

核心点一句话：美联储的宽松与紧缩周期叠加科技浪潮，催生了繁荣与萧条。
我们可以看到一系列指标归根到底都是三个层面： 产业周期、货币政策、资本市场

——而三者紧密交织，形成了一轮又一轮经济周期。

目前来看，这次流动性危机更多像是为加息做提前的风险定价；但由于美联储还没有完成加息，所以这只是预期层面的问题，离真正刺破泡沫还有一段距离要走。

所以有一种剧本是：这一次阶段性回调之后迅速修复，一路创新高。

那么这其实会是一个很坏的局面——就是在 27 年到 28 年达到繁荣的顶点，最终迎来可以对标 2000 年互联网泡沫的大危机。
author: imsongshu
quoted_text:
AI技术没有泡沫，但 AI 资本市场是有泡沫的。

同样的事件发生在类似之前 2000 年互联网泡沫，它们基本按照类似的逻辑：
 1.产业突破+美联储操纵：产业突破背景下，美联储先降息后加息，引发资本市场极度狂热。
 2.单一产业狂热+美债利率上行：由于资本市场过度狂热，使得单一产业资金过分聚集，伴随而来的就是美债利率上行。
 3.赛道估值极高：赛道整体估值极高，最终诞生了史上最大的 IPO 事件。
 4.崩盘：最后在历史的顶点处迎来崩盘。

但需要承认的一点是：现在没有集齐危机与崩盘所需要的全部条件。
尤其是美联储角度，加息还没有完全释放，远远不到刺破泡沫的地步。

而且如果想继续推进美债利率和估值上修，就要把如今的牛市继续持续下去。所以我的判断和文中类似，目前应该有两个剧本：

（1）纳指 V 反，利差同步收窄（2025 年 11 月路径）：短期舒服，但泡沫没出清。市盈率和美债收益率继续往 2000 年的水平爬，按现在的速度，明年底到 28 年初就能到。到那时再来一次回调，可能直接腰斩。

（2）二探或延后见底（2018Q4 路径），跌 30% 以上并且持续一段时间：短期难受，但等于提前放气，我反而觉得是好事。

纳指的修复能力不用怀疑，迟早会修回来。

但是用时间换空间的事情不能去做—— 要知道，互联网泡沫破裂后的 5 年后，互联网才真正开始出现应用；十几年后资本市场才又回到之前的估值，这已经过了整整一代人。

币圈有强周期性，行情波动大，大部分项目和交易所在牛市利润丰厚，而进入熊市后收入会大幅降低。

text: 循环贷没有问题，关键是这个杠杆加的方向对不对
author: minglaugodel
quoted_text:
老黄的循环贷，本质上就是企业上杠杆。
但核心在于，这个贷款未来需求是不是能迎合未来技术发展的方向。
如果能迎合，这就是成功的。
如果不能迎合，这就是泡沫。

恰好黄仁勋是个顶尖的技术营销人员。
什么叫技术营销人员？
就是能随时能干研发的销售大神。
这些人对技术非常熟悉，并且理解客户需求的技术。
但营销重于技术这在企业是常识。
所以这种人最善于把握未来的产业方向。

循环贷是老黄撑起来了。
是否成为烂账关键看英伟达的产品方向：是否能符合未来的市场需求，而且更有技术竞争力，而不仅仅依靠提供担保来获得竞争优势。
老黄从生产、资本和产业应用三方面着手，为未来的AI发展指明了方向。
但关键在于，这种远见大概率也只有老黄能深刻理解，
这种战略定力，大概率也只能老黄能坚持，
就和当年他采用CUDA一样。

很有可能最后的结局就是：
英伟达的庸才（我不认为那些顶级CEO会来接管英伟达，因为这些人知道自己的能力边界以及和黄仁勋的能力差异，他们并不愿意把英伟达作为职业生涯中的滑铁卢，这些人并不缺钱，更在意名声）最终由于产品方向把循环贷搞砸了，然后正好把这一盆子屎扣在老黄身上：看看，就是这家伙胡来，我们当年不过是帮他捅穿了AI泡沫。

这就类似做空英伟达的Michael Burry，现在黄仁勋被赶跑了，可以很神气的说：英伟达就是狗屎，利润就是假的，我早就看出来了。

text:
Hochul is the number one recipient of gambling lobby cash in New York State.

I dissected this story a few months back -- analyzing 61 million rows across 14 lobbying, political, and financial datasets.

This story explains why Hochul is fighting prediction markets (especially Kalshi) in New York.

But the implications are way bigger than that.

Here is the story again:

For the past five years, Hochul has been by far the biggest recipient of gambling lobby cash, stripping out every other person or organization, in the entire state of New York. By miles. [1]

My analysis indicates that in the fourteen months between Hochul's unexpected ascension and her first election, her campaign committee received 30.2% of every identified dollar the gambling industry gave in New York state politics, and 40.5% counting the state party she controls. [2]

I have excavated every single dollar I could find that the gambling industry has put into Kathy Hochul's political operation.

14 datasets. 21 official sources. 61 million rows of government data. [3]

Every. Single. Penny. Cross-tabulated and analyzed.

All publicly available data are included, transparently, in a repository, the link to which you can find below. This project is open data. All datasets have been included in the repo, and every query, and instructions for how to reproduce the analysis. Throw it into an AI system. Have that AI system test every single line.

What follows has never been reported as one story putting together all of the pieces:

The campaign donations sit in the Board of Elections database. The lobbying sits with the state lobbying commission. The super PAC money sits in a third system, its personnel filings in a fourth, the court fight in a fifth. Reporters have covered pieces of each. Nobody had joined them. The contributions database doesn't know what the lobbying database knows. The lobbying database doesn't know what the PAC filings know.

The industry counts on that.

That's why the money moves under names like "DK Crown Holdings" and "FBG Enterprises Opco," names built to defeat exactly what I have done.

This post connects everything together.

It explains why Hochul has recently gone into a hysteria about Kalshi.

Kalshi is a prediction market. And it threatens the casino industry. And Hochul is loyal to that industry.

ACT I. 2021-2024.

August 2021.

Hochul becomes governor. Hochul was never elected to the job in 2021. She was lieutenant governor, and she ascended automatically on August 24, 2021, when Andrew Cuomo resigned over the sexual harassment findings in the AG's report. [4]

She arrived with no statewide war chest of her own (Cuomo's fundraising machine wasn't hers), and she faced her first actual gubernatorial election just 15 months out: a June 2022 primary and November 2022 general.

She needed to raise a lot of money, fast. And everyone with business before the state knew it.

One industry, in particular, had half a billion reasons to help.

And they did.

You see, a 2013 constitutional amendment in New York authorized up to seven commercial casinos.

Four upstate licenses were issued in the 2010s; three downstate (NYC-area) licenses were deliberately held back. [5]

By 2021, everyone knew these licenses were the next -- and last -- prizes.

Each expected to require a $500M license fee and billions in investment. [6]

It was big, big money. For the casinos, and for the State of New York.

When Hochul took office in August 2021, those three licenses had not yet been put in play.

But the bidders were already assembled and publicly jockeying.

Fall 2021 to 2022.

The casino license aspirants proceeded to max out political donations to Hochul over the next 14 months, hitting her with $1.58 million in donations. [7]

She received $401,900 across 7 gifts to her state party from the gambling lobby. [7]

And $1,181,463, also from the gambling lobby, across 79 gifts to her campaign committee, Friends for Kathy Hochul. [7]

During this 14-month period, Hochul specifically received 30.2% of the total gambling industry donations in the entire state of New York, and 40.5% including the state party that she controls as governor. [2]

Hochul was the #1 target of the gambling industry lobby during this 14-month period.

And it wasn't even close.

The runner-up recipient in the entire state -- the Assembly Democrats' campaign committee -- took less than a third of what Hochul did. [8]

Casino billionaires dumped it straight into Casino Kathy's war chest.

Now, understand that the legal maximum was then $69,700 per donor -- which is why the checks below come in pairs. A husband and wife could put $139,400 into one campaign. [9]

And understand that Hochul's campaign was coming up, while who to dole these last three licenses out to was sitting on her desk.

Now look at these numbers:

August 25-27, 2021. Three days into her governorship. Marc Holliday, CEO of SL Green -- the office landlord partnering with Caesars on a Times Square casino bid -- writes his first two checks, $17,749, before Hochul has been governor a week.

By election day he's given $69,329, a few hundred dollars short of the legal maximum. [10]

October 8, 2021. Steve Cohen -- the Mets owner planning a casino next to Citi Field -- and his wife Alexandra give $136,700 on a single day: she maxes out at $69,700, he comes within $2,700 of it. Hochul has been governor for six weeks. [11]

November 4, 2021. Jeff and Lisa Blau follow the same playbook.

Jeff is the CEO of Related Companies, the Hudson Yards developer bidding with Wynn Resorts for a casino on the project's western half; the couple maxes out together -- $69,700 each, $139,400 total. [12]

November 12, 2021. Stephen Ross, Related's billionaire founder and chairman, adds his own single maximum check: $69,700. [13]

January 2022. Larry Silverstein -- the developer who rebuilt the World Trade Center, with a Manhattan casino bid of his own -- and his wife Klara complete the pattern: $69,700 each, $139,400 together.

That makes three bidder couples and five principals at or near the ceiling in four months. [14]

June 20, 2022. James Allen, chairman of Hard Rock International -- the operator attached to Cohen's Citi Field bid -- gives $25,000.

This one we can see behind the curtain of: reporters later surfaced a Hard Rock email soliciting donations for Hochul's campaign in connection with the New York casino push.

People connected to Hard Rock ultimately gave her more than $100,000. [15]

August 29, 2022. John Cordo, the Albany lobbyist Genting pays $90,000 a month to represent its Resorts World casino at Aqueduct, gives $25,000 -- a personal check from the hired advocate himself. [16]

June and October 2022. Genting's orbit gives again, obliquely: a PAC calling itself the "Catskills Support Committee," registered in Mount Kisco -- home of Kien Huat, the Genting founding family's holding company -- delivers $69,700 in two installments: $23,100 on June 13, $46,600 on October 19.

It gives the state party another $25,000 on November 1.

And when the contribution limit resets to $18,000, the same PAC comes back in March 2024 with a check for exactly $18,000 -- the new maximum.

They maxed out under the old limit, then re-maxed under the new one. [17]

November 1, 2022. One week before election day, eight days before the maximum drops from $69,700 to $18,000. Three DraftKings checks arrive together: CEO Jason Robins, Shannon Robins, and chief legal officer Stanton Dodge, $25,000 each. The sportsbook era of Hochul's donor file opens with $75,000 squeezed in under the dying limit. [18]

November 3, 2022. Fanatics gives $5,000 under a name no voter would recognize -- "FBG Enterprises Opco, LLC," its betting subsidiary's legal shell -- with another $1,000 to follow in March 2024. Small money, but the pattern it introduces (corporate legal names that hide consumer brands) is the same one that will conceal the sportsbooks' $5.25 million committee in 2026. [19]

And what happened with the licenses the money surrounded? Her first budget, in April 2022, put them in play -- it established the framework and the timeline for the downstate awards.

Then, in November 2024, when the legislature passed a bill by Senator Addabbo to speed up the awards, she vetoed it -- writing that a faster timeline "would likely have the impact of helping certain bidders and hurting others." [20]

Read that veto however you like. What it indisputably did was keep the prize pending, and the timeline in her hands, for four full years -- four years in which the bidders kept giving.

Over her governorship to date, Hochul's campaign committee has taken $1.78 million in identified gaming-industry money, and the state party she controls another $1.2 million -- together about 11 percent of everything the industry has given in New York politics since 2021. [21]

No candidate and no party committee took more. The only entities in the state that out-collected her were the industry's own: the casino workers' union's political accounts -- and the sportsbooks' war chest you'll meet in Act III. [22]

Cue the new entrant, Kalshi.

Kalshi is a New York-based startup with a different kind of gambling license -- a federal one. It is regulated by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the agency that oversees futures markets, and it runs a "prediction market": a place where users trade contracts on the outcomes of real-world events. [23]

Will the Fed cut rates? Who wins the election? And -- the product that started this war -- who wins the game.

But when Kalshi began listing sports contracts, it became, functionally, a sportsbook.

Except for two things: it holds no New York license, and it pays none of the 51 percent tax on revenue that DraftKings, FanDuel, Caesars, and bet365 pay the state. [23]

To the licensed gambling companies, that's an existential threat -- a competitor without the license fee or the tax bill.

To the state, it's a threat to a billion-dollar revenue stream, especially if that competitor takes market share.

Consider why that revenue stream matters so much to New York state politicians.

New York runs chronic structural deficits -- its comptroller and fiscal watchdogs have said for years that spending, led by Medicaid, grows faster than revenue.

And when COVID blew a $39 billion hole in the state's four-year financial plan, Albany didn't close the gap with spending discipline.

It legalized mobile sports betting. [24]

Consider what Cuomo said when critics objected in January 2021:

"I'm not here to make casinos a lot of money. I'm here to raise funds for the state." [25]

New York's mismanagement forced its doors open to casinos.

The gambling industry aren't just Hochul's donors.

New York state opened the doors to casinos because it was bleeding money.

And losing that money may start the bleeding up again.

So when Kalshi walks through the door and doesn't want to pay the fees, because it is a prediction market governed by federal law, not a casino governed by state -- and when it threatens the business models of the casinos -- New York's politicians' hackles go up.

And so do Hochul's.

Casinos are her -- and her state's -- benefactors helping to save it from fiscal collapse.

And so, Hochul flies into a hysteria and starts accusing Kalshi of hurting cancer patients.

That's how desperate she is.

Not for the patients.

For the money.

ACT II. 2025. THE INCUMBENTS GET THERE FIRST.

In New York, lobbying is a public record.

Every time a company pays someone to influence a state official, it must file a disclosure with the state's lobbying commission -- who was hired, how much they were paid, what subject they pushed, and which official they targeted.

I pulled those records. All of them.

And they show something remarkable.

In addition to the political donations above, from January 2025 through June 2026 -- eighteen consecutive months -- the Sports Betting Alliance, the trade group of DraftKings, FanDuel, Fanatics, and bet365, filed disclosures naming as the party lobbied "Governor Kathy Hochul," personally. [26]

Not "the Executive Chamber." Not "state officials."

Her.

By name.

Kathy Hochul.

Continuously. Roughly $1.19 million in lobbyist compensation across six different firms. [26]

The sportsbooks had a standing, paid, direct line into Hochul's office for a year and a half straight.

And here's something else that's never been reported.

May and June 2025. Caesars Entertainment -- a licensed casino operator, a licensed sportsbook, and one of the billionaire-backed bidders from Act I -- files its routine lobbying disclosure.

Subject of the lobbying:

"CFTC prediction markets on sports events."

Party lobbied: "Governor Kathy Hochul." [27]

So, in May 2025, a casino company paid a lobbyist to walk into the Governor's office and talk to her about Kalshi's product category -- five months before any New York regulator lifted a finger against Kalshi.

The "Kalshi problem" was not discovered by New York's government.

It was delivered to the Governor, by her donors, through paid channels.

We have the receipts.

And where was Kalshi while this was happening?

Nowhere.

I checked -- exhaustively.

The complete file of every disclosed lobbying contact with the Governor's office from 2019 through mid-2026 is 9.2 million records.

Kalshi appears in it zero times. [28]

No lobbyist. No registration. No meetings.

Nothing.

We have no record of the company being defined as a menace inside the Governor's office having ever once been spoken to.

Not once.

October 24, 2025. The State Gaming Commission orders Kalshi to stop taking sports bets from New Yorkers. [29]

Kalshi doesn't wait to be sued. Three days later -- October 27 -- it sues New York in Manhattan federal court, arguing that federal law governs its exchange, not state gambling law. The state agrees not to enforce its order while the court decides. [29]

The enforcement freeze will last nine months.

And during those nine months, the real war happens somewhere else entirely: in the State Capitol, in money, on paper.

I have all of it.

ACT III. THE MONEY WAR. NOV 2025 - JUL 2026.

With enforcement frozen, the industry went shopping.

Here's who it paid and what it bought.

November 2025. A bill appears in the Assembly: the ORACLE Act, sponsored by Assemblymember Clyde Vanel. It is meant to do one thing: crack down on prediction markets in New York. [30]

It is, functionally, the anti-Kalshi bill -- the sportsbooks' dream legislation.

The Senate version is carried by Joseph Addabbo Jr. of Queens. [30]

Remember that name. Addabbo chairs the Senate's gaming committee. Every gambling bill in New York goes through him. He is the single most important gambling gatekeeper in New York's legislature. [30]

Now the money.

December 15, 2025. Polymarket -- Kalshi's biggest rival -- hires an Albany lobbying firm.

But you won't find "Polymarket" in the records. It files under its legal corporate name: Blockratize, Inc. [31]

Remember the trick from Act I -- Fanatics giving as "FBG Enterprises Opco"? Same move.

The brands you know don't appear in the files. The shell names do. That's how this industry moves money and influence in plain sight, making it hard for journalists and investigators to connect the dots.

February 12, 2026. Kalshi -- at last -- hires its first Albany lobbyist. One firm, $10,000 a month. [32]

Set that against the other side of the ledger: an industry spending $1.19 million on six firms to work the Governor's office alone.

The industry outspent Kalshi's entire Albany operation by roughly twenty to one. [32]

March 25 - July 3, 2026.

Here's the big one.

First, a thirty-second civics lesson. New York allows something called an independent expenditure committee -- a PAC that can accept unlimited money and spend it campaigning for or against candidates, as long as it doesn't coordinate with them.

Unlimited. No $18,000 cap.

Now *that* is where serious industry money goes.

During the enforcement freeze, a brand-new one appears: "New York Future."

Into it, in four months, flows $5,250,000 -- from exactly four sources, every one filing under a legal name no voter would recognize: [33]

"DK Crown Holdings Inc" -- that's DraftKings. $2.25 million.

"Fanduel Inc" -- FanDuel. $2.25 million.

"FBG Enterprises Opco" -- Fanatics. $500,000.

"Hillside (Shared Services US)" -- bet365. $250,000.

The four Sports Betting Alliance sportsbooks. The same four whose trade group was lobbying Hochul by name. $5.25 million, ahead of the June 2026 legislative primaries.

And New York wasn't special: nationally, these companies have poured over $40 million into state-level political vehicles, and reporters have documented their super PACs deliberately obscuring who's behind the ads. [34]

What you're watching in New York is the local franchise of a national playbook.

And the state's own disclosure records show exactly which candidates that money supported. Two of them should make your jaw drop:

~$148,000 in digital ads supporting Clyde Vanel. The sponsor of the anti-Kalshi bill. [35]

The sportsbooks bought ads for the author of their dream legislation while his bill was pending -- seven weeks before the state sued Kalshi.

~$71,000 supporting Joseph Addabbo. The gaming chair. The Senate sponsor. Who, in the same election cycle, was also cashing personal checks from DraftKings' CEO and chief legal officer. [36]

The machinery wasn't even hidden well. The firm running New York Future's ad spending -- The Parkside Group -- was simultaneously registered as the Sports Betting Alliance's lobbyist on Addabbo's Senate bill. The same firm, paid to push the bill and paid to re-elect its sponsor. [37]

And the supporting cast kept growing.

Delaware North -- the Buffalo-based gaming giant owned by the Jacobs family, which gave Hochul $135,000 across sixteen checks in 2025 alone -- lobbied both versions of the ORACLE Act. Robinhood, the stock-trading app, quietly lobbied both bills all spring (it has prediction-market ambitions of its own). [38]

Robinhood's lobbying firm? Also Delaware North's lobbying firm. By spring 2026, Albany firms were billing both armies of the same war. [38]

And hovering over the whole map, one last pattern. The only big independent committee spending for Hochul in 2026 -- $11.9 million, all of it Uber's money -- is run by a principal of Moonshot Strategies, one of the seven firms on Genting's lobbying payroll. The biggest committee of the 2025 city elections lists Genting's $90,000-a-month lobbyist -- John Cordo, the man from Act I -- among its principals. And the chief legal officer of Genting's Resorts World casino has his own committee registered and waiting, empty, in Queens. [39]

Whoever wins any race in New York, the casino lobby's operatives are already standing inside the machinery.

ACT IV. TWENTY-FOUR DAYS. TWO POSTS. (JUL - AUG 2026)

July 7, 2026. The federal judge rules. Kalshi's request to block New York is denied: gambling regulation is a "traditional police power" of the state, and -- the line that mattered -- "there is nothing preventing Kalshi from obtaining a license pursuant to New York law." (Kalshi is appealing.) [40]

The enforcement freeze is dead.

July 31, 2026. Twenty-four days later. Hochul and Attorney General Letitia James sue Kalshi in state court for running an unlicensed sports-betting operation -- seeking penalties of up to $100,000 per unlawful bet. Total potential exposure: $36 billion. Not a cease-and-desist. A corporate death sentence. [41]

The lawsuit itself was always coming -- the state had been fighting Kalshi in court since October.

The money bought everything around it.

The bills waiting in the legislature, written by sponsors the industry financed with $5.25 million during the enforcement freeze.

The direct line into her office -- six firms, $1.19 million, eighteen consecutive months of lobbying her by name.

The framing of prediction markets as a menace, delivered to the Governor by Caesars' paid lobbyist, on exactly this subject, more than a year before her lawyers filed.

August 3, 2026. Per the Wall Street Journal, the state had spent weeks negotiating with Kalshi before it sued.

Kalshi's offer on the table: a 6 percent tax on its trades projected at ten billion dollars for New York over five years.

The talks broke down. The state sued instead. [42]

The outsider's money, offered openly as tax revenue, is framed as a bribe to be refused on principle.

Ten billion wasn't enough. Hochul wanted thirty-six.

Yet the insiders' money -- $1.78 million into her campaign, $1.19 million lobbying her office, $5.25 million into their war chest -- arrived through channels that I had to meticulously sift through the public records to find.

She never mentions *that* money.

Curious.

I mean, you have to hand it to Hochul.

She has got a lot of nerve swinging at that level of hypocrisy.

August 5, 2026, 2:07 PM EDT. The tech site Futurism publishes a story about Kalshi listing markets tied to cancer-drug trials. Within hours, the Governor's account posts: [43]

"There are some lines you don't cross. Turning cancer patients into a prop bet is one of them. And it's exactly why New York won't let companies like Kalshi break our laws."

Three facts sit under those 41 words.

I've verified all three against the primary documents.

One. The lawsuit she's describing -- the "exactly why" -- never mentions cancer. I searched the state's entire complaint against Kalshi. Cancer: zero mentions. Clinical trials: zero. Drugs: zero. FDA: zero. It is a sports-betting case about licenses and taxes.

The Governor stapled a same-day viral outrage onto a lawsuit that says nothing about it. [44]

She is misleading the public. Demonstrably lying. To her voters. To her constituents.

Shame on Casino Kathy.

Two. "Prop bet" -- the thing she calls morally uncrossable -- is her donors' flagship product. Prop betting is the core business of DraftKings, FanDuel, Caesars, and bet365: the companies behind the $5.25 million committee and the eighteen-month lobbying line into her office. Their allied gaming chair -- Addabbo, the man their $71,000 supported -- sponsors legislation to expand legal prop bets. [45]

Her position isn't "don't bet on people."

It's "don't bet on people outside the licensed, taxed, donor-occupied channel if I don't say so".

That's bad.

She does not care about the people.

What she cares about is the money.

Three. The first entity in the entire public record to define prediction markets as New York's problem was not a regulator, legislator, or a grieving family.

It was Caesars Entertainment -- in a paid lobbying visit to Governor Kathy Hochul, on "CFTC prediction markets on sports events," in May 2025 -- five months before the state acted, fourteen months before the lawsuit, and fifteen months before she discovered her conscience on a Tuesday afternoon, two hours after a random blog post. [27]

Step back again for a second.

The industry funds the Governor -- more than any candidate or party committee in the state -- while her office controls its licenses.

It pays six firms to lobby her, by name, for eighteen consecutive months.

When a federally regulated competitor appears, a casino delivers the "problem" directly to her office through a paid lobbyist, months before any regulator acts.

When enforcement freezes, the industry pours $5.25 million into electing the legislators writing the anti-competitor bills -- including the bills' own sponsors -- through the same firm it pays to lobby for those bills.

And when the courts finally clear the way, the state's $36 billion lawsuit and the Governor's moral outrage arrive perfectly aligned with her donors' commercial interest.

Every link in that loop is a public filing. That's the system.

Now, what this record does not show:

There is no traced quid pro quo.

Campaign funds are not personal income, no dollar is followed from a donor's check to a government decision, and the lawsuit's timing tracks the court calendar.

I can't prove that anyone said to anyone else: "If you give me this, I'll give you that."

Because the record doesn't show that.

Despite that, the record is damning.

I'm also not neutral in this fight, and I won't pretend to be.

I think what's being done to Kalshi is exactly what it looks like.

Everything above is built so you don't have to take my word for anything.

Every claim above is footnoted -- to 61 million rows of the state's own records across 14 datasets, to 7 more official filing systems, and to the primary documents: the lawsuits, the lobbying filings, the veto, the court opinion.

All linked below.

See for yourself.

text:
A few personal takes here:

Really appreciate that proposal and agree with a lot of it. But i think the ranking of ppl caps vs compute caps hinges on something nobody knows well: the return function -- how much easier is to find better algorithms per unit of intelligence increase? A ppl cap targets the outcome directly, so it holds up whatever that curve looks like, whereas compute caps don't.

1. Under many versions of that function, compute caps just don't bind. They only work if capability gains stay compute-hungry. but if models can solve Riemann, they can probably invent the transformer, and inventing the transformer didn't take much compute. There's probably a transformer++ out there to find. Architecture and optimizer search is the most math-like part of ML, and the most direct way to use models to make models more powerful. A cap on R&D compute share might not even catch it, and the cap loosens exactly as models get more efficient. So i worry that aiming for something like 10% compute caps in 6 months could be too little, too late.

2. Arguably, compute caps are also directionally wrong or at least insufficient. If the goal is keeping humans in control, they only make sure we walk off the cliff instead of running off it.  They also tax the compute we might actually want: elicitation, post-training, better products and user experiences, pointing the intelligence we already have at science. I think today's frontier is already enough to radically transform science and the economy https://t.co/6ZQcc4fZtM. We should incentivize spending capabilities compute directing that intelligence at important problems, not climbing on compute multipliers to advance raw intelligence further.

3. Diffusion matters as much as pacing. Once a model above the "can find transformer++" threshold has spread through open weights, distillation or theft, compute caps and deployment lags at frontier labs may not do much. At that point the cat is arguably out of the bag. so we should be doing everything we can to keep capabilities above that level from diffusing, not just worrying about future models, secrets and compute.

That all said, I do think overhang is a real worry with a ppl cap, and that compute caps are a reasonable standalone option especially as a short-term stopgap.  What we really want is probably a portfolio of options, potentially including ppl, ECI, and compute inputs. But if we want humanity to stay in control, I think we need to figure out how to limit advances in raw intelligence, and something like ppl is the best handle we currently have on that.

text:
This is wild.

Tesla is running a real-time ~1B diffusion world model in the car that generates a photorealistic view of the world from the same vision features that drive the car.

The fact that this is shipping in production right now is kind of insane. https://t.co/xxQ0xg5h1x
author: camiinthisthang
quoted_text:
In case anyone is curious:

We’ve had a ~pixel-perfect world model since last year, which is critical for synthetic data generation. 

The (much) smaller version of that in the car is a conditional mean-flow model, based on the recent sequence of Tesla Universal Vision Encoder features, which are the same ones that are plugged into the 3B encoder model that produces the driving actions. 

We fork off from these UVE features, then run a separate ~1B diffusion model. This takes in the previous reality-view generation with added noise and then denoises it to the current visualization. 

It then produces a small video chunk (8 images at 36 fps, at the resolution of the UI screen). This work is done by 1/2 of a TRIP engine every UVE frame at 18 hz and is spread over 4 cycles. 

Currently, the latency is a bit high due to compute constraints, but we have ways to interleave newer UVE features along the diffusion transformer layers to cut roughly 35% of the latency.

text:
You got some things right and other things wrong, but in general, your overall construct is incorrect.  It is not the case that the other alts contributed all of their performance fees to their public companies, and that our shareholders don't benefit from the investment performance generated by our funds.  

It is true that Pershing Square Inc. ($PS) is structured differently from the other alternative asset managers (alts) like Blackstone, KKR, and others. Our unique structure is highly beneficial to our company and our shareholders, as I explain below.

In short, when Blackstone and the other alts went public, they contributed a substantial portion -- typically 40% to 60%, but not all of their incentive, performance, or promote compensation to the public company and retained the balance to compensate their employees.

The outcome of this approach has been suboptimal.  First, promote income, particularly from private equity funds, is highly volatile. It is only earned and paid when funds generate a return in excess of a preferred return and when a liquidity event happens, that is, when portfolio companies and/or the funds' real estate assets are sold. As a result, analysts and investors in the alts value the highly volatile income from incentive fees at a low multiple. 

Wall Street likes recurring and growing fee streams like management fees. It does not like volatile incentive fee income.

By contributing so much of their incentive fees to their public companies, the other alts did not retain enough incentive fees to pay their teams. The result is that the other alts grant large amounts of equity compensation to their employees in addition to the promote income they pay to their employees. This equity compensation dilutes reported earnings by as much as 20% or more.

In order to address these concerns, when we structured Pershing Square Inc. (PS) in anticipation of its public offering, we bifurcated the performance fee differently. Rather than giving Pershing Square Inc. a pro rata slice of our performance fees, we gave the public company a senior interest in our performance fee income -- what we call Preferred Performance Fees -- and employees retained a subordinate interest in the incentive fee income, what we call Subordinated Performance Fees. 

PS retains the performance fees on the first five percentage points of returns net of management fees from our funds that charge performance fees, and our employees receive the performance fees on returns above 5% if there are any.  

If our funds do not earn a return in excess of 5% in any year, any unpaid Preferred Performance Fees accrue into a future year or years until they are earned and paid.  In other words, the company and our shareholders get paid first before our employees.

As long as investors believe we can earn a gross compound return of 6.5% -- the 5% preferred return plus the 1.5% annual management fee -- over the long term (a high likelihood, in our view, in light of our investment strategy that has generated gross returns of nearly 20% for the last 23 years), Preferred Performance Fees are effectively economically equivalent to management fees and therefore deserving of a similar valuation multiple.

We believe our high-return investment strategy will allow us to not only earn the Preferred Performance Fees over time, but also enable us to continually earn Subordinate Performance Fees that we can use to compensate, recruit and retain high quality talent. As a result, we don't need to issue large amounts of stock and option compensation to employees like the other alternative investment managers, minimizing the risk of dilution to shareholders.

[PS also benefits from the fact that, as is typical in the hedge fund industry, we earn incentive fees from both realized and unrealized gains so we are not forced to sell assets in order to generate returns.  Our funds generate performance fees as long as our annual performance net of management fees is positive, which makes our performance fees much more recurring than those from private equity or private real estate funds.]

While in a great performance year, the amount of performance fees earned by Pershing Square Inc. is effectively capped by our structure, the growth in assets that occur from great performance years inure to the benefit of all shareholders in that year and in future years.  

For example, if, in one year, we generate 30% net returns, while PS only receives performance fees on the first five percentage points of return, its cash flows and intrinsic value grow substantially due to the net 30% increase in fee-paying assets that is generated from our investment performance.  

Because 98% of our capital is in permanent capital vehicles, nearly all of our net performance is continually reinvested and compounded in our funds and additive to the growth of our fee-paying assets in that year and in future years.

With respect to your claim that this structure creates a conflict, I disagree. 

First, the structure was clearly explained to all investors in the IPO and in our public filings, and investors and analysts have found the structure extremely favorable, particularly when compared with the other alts.  

Second, our structure incentivizes us to generate excellent investment returns and enables us to attract and retain the best talent without burdening the company with excess G&A, restricted stock or option expenses.

Third, any new funds we launch which generate performance fees will have the same Preferred Performance Fee structure and therefore benefit PS in the same manner as do our existing funds.  

Fourth, our employees own the substantial majority of our shares creating further alignment.  We own a greater percentage of our company than do the employees of any of the other alternative asset managers.

Fifth, since we have retained, effectively outside of the company, sufficient performance fee income to compensate, retain and recruit employees, we are able to manage PS with a relatively modest amount of general and administrative expense of about $50 million. This has enabled us to operate with the highest operating margins of any of the publicly traded alternative asset managers. 

Thank you for the taking the time to write your post, which has given me the opportunity to clarify the concerns that you raised.  

I welcome any further questions or concerns that you or other shareholders may have.

X for the win.

This is the largest commitment of capital as a percentage of funds managed of any of the alts and one of the largest dollar amounts invested by employees, which is  particularly notable in light of how small our employee base is at less than 1% of the number of Blackstone employees.

博卡奇卡的工地上，立着第一台全尺寸星舰原型。2019 年 11 月 20 日下午，它在低温加压测试中裂开了：上部储箱的封头崩开，一团白雾从顶上冲出来。不锈钢罐体大体还在，表皮起了皱，没有人受伤。

quoted_text:
Why is the market tanking?

Here is what my two smartest hedge fund friends and their teams have to say about it. In their own words, but with structure added:

1) The main fear is over-earnings in the semis supply chain (and power): even if you keep growing, at some point supply catches up = more competition = lower margins = lower E. The bulls say tech P/Es are low (“XYZ is cheap”), but that’s on peak earnings. If E collapses, it can take a long time for growth to catch up. And that assumes growth.

2) Overbuild / CAPEX cycle turning. The stocks de-rate at the top, while earnings are still growing. Then the overbuild leaves excess capacity, customers stop ordering to digest it, and that’s when earnings get cut. Semis have always been cyclical. “This time is different” never actually works.

3) OpenAI’s situation and its ripple effects. They are genuinely worried it will never be able to IPO. According to them, its financials are a lot worse than Anthropic’s. A lot of the CAPEX spend, and the debt funding it, is tied to OpenAI. If it can’t IPO, it could end up starved of capital / distressed. One said “it will end up being sold to Microsoft for ~$200bn”. Leveraged neoclouds too: bust or acquired.

4) Defensibility of the frontier: they believe switching costs are very low (one of their teams is fully model agnostic and moves usage quarter to quarter for high performance trading use cases). With the latest Google models getting better, very hard to underwrite the labs’ market share.

5) Rates and financing bottleneck. Sticky inflation and a Fed that’s back to hiking = tighter credit markets / higher yields = less money around to fund the buildout.

6) China / US controls. The new US export controls now require a license to ship AI chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil, i.e. the routes into China. On paper Nvidia’s direct China exposure is small (~2% of revenue). But a short seller claims 20%+ of Nvidia’s AI compute revenue ends up in China. And with Jensen out, the new CEO potentially has a clean slate to shut it down and reset the numbers.

I don’t necessarily share all those views - and my investment horizons are much longer. They tend to change their minds quickly as well. But I like to consider what smart people have to say in any case - and in this case, they did turn negative a few weeks ago. So sharing in case it’s useful for your own thinking.

text:
You got some things right and other things wrong, but in general, your overall construct is incorrect.  It is not the case that the other alts contributed all of their performance fees to their public companies, and that our shareholders don't benefit from the investment performance generated by our funds.  

It is true that Pershing Square Inc. ($PS) is structured differently from the other alternative asset managers (alts) like Blackstone, KKR, and others. Our unique structure is highly beneficial to our company and our shareholders, as I explain below.

In short, when Blackstone and the other alts went public, they contributed a substantial portion -- typically 40% to 60%, but not all of their incentive, performance, or promote compensation to the public company and retained the balance to compensate their employees.

The outcome of this approach has been suboptimal.  First, promote income, particularly from private equity funds, is highly volatile. It is only earned and paid when funds generate a return in excess of a preferred return and when a liquidity event happens, that is, when portfolio companies and/or the funds' real estate assets are sold. As a result, analysts and investors in the alts value the highly volatile income from incentive fees at a low multiple. 

Wall Street likes recurring and growing fee streams like management fees. It does not like volatile incentive fee income.

By contributing so much of their incentive fees to their public companies, the other alts did not retain enough incentive fees to pay their teams. The result is that the other alts grant large amounts of equity compensation to their employees in addition to the promote income they pay to their employees. This equity compensation dilutes reported earnings by as much as 20% or more.

In order to address these concerns, when we structured Pershing Square Inc. (PS) in anticipation of its public offering, we bifurcated the performance fee differently. Rather than giving Pershing Square Inc. a pro rata slice of our performance fees, we gave the public company a senior interest in our performance fee income -- what we call Preferred Performance Fees -- and employees retained a subordinate interest in the incentive fee income, what we call Subordinated Performance Fees. 

PS retains the performance fees on the first five percentage points of returns net of management fees from our funds that charge performance fees, and our employees receive the performance fees on returns above 5% if there are any.  

If our funds do not earn a return in excess of 5% in any year, any unpaid Preferred Performance Fees accrue into a future year or years until they are earned and paid.  In other words, the company and our shareholders get paid first before our employees.

As long as investors believe we can earn a gross compound return of 6.5% -- the 5% preferred return plus the 1.5% annual management fee -- over the long term (a high likelihood, in our view, in light of our investment strategy that has generated gross returns of nearly 20% for the last 23 years), Preferred Performance Fees are effectively economically equivalent to management fees and therefore deserving of a similar valuation multiple.

We believe our high-return investment strategy will allow us to not only earn the Preferred Performance Fees over time, but also enable us to continually earn Subordinate Performance Fees that we can use to compensate, recruit and retain high quality talent. As a result, we don't need to issue large amounts of stock and option compensation to employees like the other alternative investment managers, minimizing the risk of dilution to shareholders.

[PS also benefits from the fact that, as is typical in the hedge fund industry, we earn incentive fees from both realized and unrealized gains so we are not forced to sell assets in order to generate returns.  Our funds generate performance fees as long as our annual performance net of management fees is positive, which makes our performance fees much more recurring than those from private equity or private real estate funds.]

While in a great performance year, the amount of performance fees earned by Pershing Square Inc. is effectively capped by our structure, the growth in assets that occur from great performance years inure to the benefit of all shareholders in that year and in future years.  

For example, if, in one year, we generate 30% net returns, while PS only receives performance fees on the first five percentage points of return, its cash flows and intrinsic value grow substantially due to the net 30% increase in fee-paying assets that is generated from our investment performance.  

Because 98% of our capital is in permanent capital vehicles, nearly all of our net performance is continually reinvested and compounded in our funds and additive to the growth of our fee-paying assets in that year and in future years.

With respect to your claim that this structure creates a conflict, I disagree. 

First, the structure was clearly explained to all investors in the IPO and in our public filings, and investors and analysts have found the structure extremely favorable, particularly when compared with the other alts.  

Second, our structure incentivizes us to generate excellent investment returns and enables us to attract and retain the best talent without burdening the company with excess G&A, restricted stock or option expenses.

Third, any new funds we launch which generate performance fees will have the same Preferred Performance Fee structure and therefore benefit PS in the same manner as do our existing funds.  

Fourth, our employees own the substantial majority of our shares creating further alignment.  We own a greater percentage of our company than do the employees of any of the other alternative asset managers.

Fifth, since we have retained, effectively outside of the company, sufficient performance fee income to compensate, retain and recruit employees, we are able to manage PS with a relatively modest amount of general and administrative expense of about $50 million. This has enabled us to operate with the highest operating margins of any of the publicly traded alternative asset managers. 

Thank you for the taking the time to write your post, which has given me the opportunity to clarify the concerns that you raised.  

I welcome any further questions or concerns that you or other shareholders may have.

X for the win.

text:
founders: if you haven't created a company.md yet, 
do it right now.

VCs are already running your deck through AI. they drop the PDF into Claude or ChatGPT and start asking questions before they ever talk to you.

the problem: decks are built for eyes, not agents. charts become pixels. the AI fills the gaps with guesses, and then it diligences the guesses.

so we built something for their agents instead.

our company.md is a ~1000 line plain text file (and growing by the day). it's the deck, plus everything a technical partner would spend three weeks of diligence digging for:

• the deck, slide by slide, in words
• our full tech stack, layer by layer. surfaces, connectors, agent harness, fleet orchestration, models, skills, MCP, strategy authoring, runtime, exit engine, simulation venue, data pipeline, signing, telemetry, billing, infra, security model
• for every layer: what it is, how it works, the main technologies, its scale, and what's proprietary vs open source
• every MCP tool and every agent skill, listed and linked to the public repos
• a repo map: what lives where, public and private
• anonymized profiles of our top customers. what they build, how they pay, how they use their own AIs to drive ours. including the ones who left, and why
• every number carries the date it was last checked

so a partner can ask their Claude "how does order signing work?" or "what's actually proprietary here?" or "which customers churned and why?" and get a real answer in our words, not a guess from a screenshot.

what we learned building it:

1. write it for AI readers, and say so in line one
2. date every number. models trust what they can place in time
3. mark proprietary vs open source on every layer. it's the first thing a technical investor asks
4. include the customers who churned. an agent trusts a doc that isn't all good news
5. one link that always serves the latest version, on every slide of the deck
6. keep it in sync with the deck. any mismatch is the first thing their agent will flag

it's become the most effective tool in our pitch arsenal.

Before: Investors skimmed the deck prior to the meeting:

Now: 
+ agent take the first meeting and prep their human investors

text:
感谢 OpenAI 发布的决定性证据，验证了我 8 年前的猜想。当时我猜想模型越强大，它压缩文本的能力也就越强。衡量一个外星文明的智能程度，可以根据它能把大量文本压缩得多短来估计。

这是学界非常知名的 “压缩即智能” 理论。OpenAI 发布的数据表明，预训练模型的智能程度与其 Perplexity（困惑度）高度相关，Perplexity 越低，它预测文本下一个 token 的准确率也就越高，压缩率也就越高。

我在 2024 年有个错误的判断，感觉 log perplexity 到 0.9 以下就很难继续降低了，剩下的部分是世界的随机性，很难预测。这也是业界很多人认为 pretraining scaling 撞墙了的时候。

没想到 T 级参数量的模型可以把 log perplexity 推得更低，并且这些模型有更多的 emergent behavior：安全专家、前端专家、解决千禧年难题。pretraining scaling 还远远没有到头。

text:
The bears are having their moment.

After predicting a top in the AI trade every month for the last 4 years, the bears finally got their moment last week.

However, in 3 to 6 months, we are going to look back at this correction and realize it was just that: a correction.

There is a widespread narrative right now that Nvidia, $NVDA, is quite literally going to collapse. This is a stock that was trading at a record high on October 6th, worth nearly $6 trillion, and the inventor of the most advanced chips in the world (it's not even close).

That's how deeply pessimistic sentiment has become over the last seven weeks.

Even if Nvidia produced half as much revenue as they are guiding for their next fiscal year, this company would still produce close to $400 billion in annual revenue.

Meanwhile, the S&P 500 has posted three consecutive quarters with earnings growth above 25% and eight straight quarters of double-digit growth.

And, sentiment flipped so quickly that the S&P 500 closed the week 4.1 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average on Friday. Not even 2020 and 2008 saw such an occurrence.

The reality is that AI truly is the "next big thing" and the AI buildout is only accelerating.

Bears will sound smart, bulls will make money.

AI search chats (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude etc.) recommend the brands that many sites write about

> an agent lists the creators your customers follow and checks if their audience fits
> it drafts the outreach, then you run campaigns in waves, since customers need several touchpoints before they trust you

3. power users get harder to reach

more products launch, and they all compete for the same early users

4. employee-led content brings in more growth

buyers trust people more than brand accounts

5. more video, filmed raw by real people

as more content gets made with AI, raw videos from real people stand out

> an agent finds trends and customer pain points for your next video
> you film it yourself
> AI edits it and handles ops like scheduling

6. more companies open-source their tools

a free, open-source tool introduces people to the problem your paid product solves

as software gets easier to replicate, your edge is no longer the product itself but how many users you can get interested, and most of them will never host themselves = your solution wins in the long run

author: jefftangx
quoted_text:
The Humanity Project 

People always ask me: if we want to cure all diseases with AI, shouldn't we be building a huge robotic warehouse to run closed loop experiments on mice, human cells, and so on? From a naive outside perspective, this may seem like the obvious thing to do, analogous to what Periodic Labs is doing for materials and what the robotics companies like Physical Intelligence are doing for laundry and so on. 

The problem is, for most diseases, experiments in cultured cells, mice, and other models are poorly predictive of success in actual humans. If you synthesize a material in the lab and find it has a certain conductivity, then that’s the conductivity; by contrast, if something works in a mouse, you still have to test it in a human, and mouse biology is so poorly predictive of human biology that for some diseases success in mice actually anticorrelates with success in humans. Closed loop reinforcement learning in mice might be a great way to learn how to cure mouse diseases, but the only way to cure human diseases is to run more experiments in humans.

To cure all diseases, in other words, what we actually need is a massive, centralized effort to scale up clinical trials testing new AI-generated therapeutic hypotheses. Such an effort would serve several goals: it would identify novel mechanisms for treating diseases; it would train AI systems to understand human biology; and it would build the infrastructure needed to streamline and accelerate clinical trials going forward. Centralization would allow us to minimize duplication, maximize data availability for training, and ensure the resulting infrastructure is shared. An effort of this scale -- which would dwarf the genome project and consume resources similar to the entire NIH budget -- is not just our best chance to cure all diseases. It is also our best chance to remain ahead in biotechnology, where the US is rapidly losing ground to China. I call it the Humanity Project, and I describe it in a new essay, linked below.

The first emphasis in the Humanity Project is on novelty. Medicine moves forward when we identify new therapeutic mechanisms -- think GLP-1s, CAR-T cells, and checkpoint inhibitors. Within a few years, AI agents will be as good as or better than humans at proposing novel therapeutic mechanisms. However, testing novel therapeutic mechanisms is risky and rarely pays off, so most biopharmas largely avoid it. Instead, 96% of clinical trials today are aimed at obtaining approval for new drugs that use existing therapeutic mechanisms, rather than testing new ones. If we want to cure all diseases, we need to massively expand the number of clinical trials we run that examine novel hypotheses, both as a way of identifying novel therapeutic mechanisms and as a way of training AI models to better understand human biology.

This brings us to the second emphasis of the Humanity Project, which is on scale. The Humanity Project would be a centralized project to run 2000 drug programs testing novel, AI-generated therapeutic hypotheses through clinical proof of concept over 5 years. The Project would cost between $50B and $200B -- equivalent to the amount allocated for the California High Speed Rail, or the 5-year budget for the NIH --, would increase the number of first-in-class drug trials by 400% to 800% over that period, and would benefit from various advantages of AI in proposing and prosecuting clinical trials. In the process, the Project would lay down the infrastructure needed to accelerate and scale future trials run by the private sector, accelerating US biotechnology as a whole.

The logistical challenges associated with such a problem are intense. We need better infrastructure to recruit and identify patients; we need to streamline regulation to make it easier to get drugs into patients faster while ensuring safety; we need to scale up and accelerate manufacturing; and we need to plug all of this infrastructure into AI systems that can efficiently integrate information, generate hypotheses and plan experiments, and learn from outcomes. The Humanity Project would work on developing these, and would make the resulting infrastructure available subsequently to accelerate US biotech as a whole. And, importantly, if we are serious about curing all diseases in the coming decades and maintaining US leadership in biotechnology and medicine, there is no alternative. With all the wealth and value set to be created by AI, finding the resources to accelerate medicine in this way should be straightforward. We should begin now.
