text: Accelerate ERC7231.. if we are serious about solving social problems around crypto.
author: hmalviya9
quoted_text:
identity comes before reputation. before you decide whether someone deserves your trust you need a consistent way to recognize who earned it.

and we humans have different identities based on how we present ourselves online and offline. 

you could be a developer on GitHub. a writer on X. a contributor in a DAO. a trader across multiple wallets. each identity carries a different part of your history but that history is scattered across platforms.

when we talk about building a reputation system in web3 we need a way for users to connect those identities under an identifier they control. 

otherwise every new platform asks you to start from zero even when you have spent years building credibility elsewhere.

there is a standard called ERC-7231. it is called Identity-aggregated NFT. it extends ERC-721 so multiple web2 and web3 identities can be associated with one NFT-based identity. 

its metadata describes the linked identities while an onchain hash called identitiesRoot binds that information to the token. signatures help verify that the owner authorized the binding.

but linking an account and proving you control that account are different things. signing a list that includes a GitHub username doesn’t prove that GitHub account belongs to you. account authentication needs a separate verification process.

this is where privacy-preserving verification could become useful. with additional ZK infrastructure you could prove a specific claim about authenticated accounts without revealing every account behind it. 

a TEE-based verifier could also check private information and issue an attestation under its hardware and operator trust assumptions. neither feature comes automatically with ERC-7231.

imagine proving that you completed ten paid jobs without exposing every client. proving that you contributed to an established project without publicly connecting your developer identity to your trading wallet. 

or proving that you meet a community’s membership criteria without handing over your entire online history.

that is the kind of identity system i would want. 

a core identity under my control with different views for different applications. aggregation should be my choice. disclosure should be my choice too. publishing every linked account in public metadata would defeat that purpose.

then we can build reputation around evidence. completed work. fulfilled commitments. contributions. feedback from people whose own credibility can be examined. 

and reputation should depend on context. 

being a good trader doesn’t automatically make you a trustworthy developer or a reliable person to manage a community treasury.

there are harder questions too. 
>what happens when an account gets hacked? 
>how do you revoke an old connection? 
>how do you recover your identity? 
>and if the identity NFT can be sold should its previous reputation follow the buyer? 

a serious implementation needs rules for those situations. aggregating ten accounts also doesn’t prove they belong to one unique human.

for crypto anarchy this could become useful infrastructure. communities could evaluate evidence through rules they choose instead of depending entirely on a platform’s badge or a government-issued identity. that doesn’t eliminate trust. it makes the sources of trust more explicit and open to challenge.

ERC-7231 gives us a foundation for connecting identities. private verification and reputation need to be built around it. the goal should be to carry the credibility you earned into a new community while revealing only what that community actually needs to know.

text:
大的来了！AI Agent 已经开始自主挖掘 Zero-day 漏洞了。

AWS Security Blog 11月20日披露了一项值得整个网络安全行业关注的调查：一个被 AWS 判定为具有“中国关联”（Chinese-nexus）的威胁行为者，利用开源 AI Agent 渗透测试框架 Cairn，几乎在没有人工干预的情况下，完成了从漏洞发现到服务器控制权获取的全过程。

这次攻击最值得关注的，不是 AI 帮黑客写了多少代码，而是它已经能够自主完成攻击链。

几个关键细节：

自主发现零日漏洞。 AI Agent 在开源医学影像 AI 软件 MONAI Label 中，自动识别 API 接口并发现路径穿越漏洞。从 API 扫描到实现任意文件写入，仅用了约 11 分钟。
自主完成漏洞利用。 Agent 随后写入 Python 反弹 Shell，最终获得服务器 Root 权限。整个过程涉及当时尚未公开、尚无补丁的 Zero-day 漏洞。
持续不间断地攻击。 在其他目标上，Agent 曾连续 16 小时执行 148 轮操作；针对 GPU 服务器，自动收集 80 个用户名，并尝试超过 3 万组密码。失败后还会自主调整策略继续尝试。
攻击框架正在被不同类型的黑客使用。 Cairn 原本是面向安全研究和渗透测试的开源自主 Agent 框架，但已经被用于情报刺探和牟利型攻击。

需要说明的是，AWS 对攻击者与中国的关联判断为中等置信度（Moderate Confidence），依据包括简体中文提示词、北京时间脚本时间戳等线索，并不意味着已经证实其属于中国官方组织。

这件事真正值得警惕的是攻击范式的变化。

过去，黑客需要人工识别目标、扫描端口、寻找漏洞、编写 Exploit，再一步步完成渗透。

现在，攻击者可能只需要给 Agent 一个目标：拿到服务器 Shell。

剩下的扫描、漏洞挖掘、路径探索、漏洞利用和权限提升，都可以交给 AI 自主完成。

当攻击从人工驱动变成 Agent 驱动，攻击成本、速度和持续性都会发生变化。防御体系面对的也不再只是一个个黑客，而是能够 7×24 小时运行、持续试错和自主调整策略的攻击智能体。

AI 时代，网络安全的核心竞争将不只是防御工具的迭代速度，而是攻防双方 Agent 的能力与进化速度。

Offense as a Service，可能正在从一个行业概念变成现实。

author: teortaxesTex
quoted_text:
We fully support OpenAI's transparency initiative. Thanks to @merettm @markchen90 @gdb @sama for leading the way. 

We all got into this field to build safe AGI that is genuinely good for humanity. One of the hardest parts of AI safety is coordination, and this is a step in the right direction. Many more steps like this will be needed to deliver safe, contained, and aligned AGI in the next few years.

We're committed to sharing our pre-training progress on a common held-out evaluation set. With OpenAI's permission, we report MAI-2 Base on their evaluation set. Its log-perplexity is 0.819, putting it in the same ballpark as the GPT-5.6 Sol base model. Our model uses the same tokenizer as OpenAI, so the numbers are directly comparable. 

In the future, to be able to compare across labs we might need to report bits-per-byte (BPB) rather than perplexity since different labs use different tokenizers. We will also need different evaluation datasets - the fact we have access to OpenAI's evaluation dataset is a special case.

Safety and alignment is now the mission. It's the absolute number one most important focus for our industry. And it begins with small, practical steps like these towards better coordination on pacing.

text:
So I went on and analyzed @pumpfun's wallet migration process, by reading the actual JavaScript the site serves.

tldr: calling this "end-to-end encryption" is misleading at best. End-to-end encryption means only you can decrypt. Here the encryption does happen in your browser, but the decryption key belongs to Privy: their infrastructure (a TEE) decrypts your private key, keeps it, and signs with it for whoever passes their login check.

What actually happens when you click "Import and finish":

1. Your key is checked locally and must match the wallet you're connected with.
2. The page asks pumpfun's server for an encryption key, and pumpfun's server relays back what is supposed to be Privy's public key.
3. Your key is encrypted in the browser (HPKE) and sent through pumpfun's server to Privy.
4. Privy decrypts it and keeps it. From then on, Privy signs with your key whenever a valid Privy session asks.

The problems:

- It's not E2E. The "other end" is the custodian, not you. By that logic, any HTTPS upload is "end-to-end".
- The encryption key is handed out by pumpfun's own backend, and your browser has no way to check that it's really Privy's. In real E2E, the relay can't choose who the recipient is.
- Your funds now also depend on Privy never getting breached. Every migration like this one piles more private keys into one place, which makes it a prime target for hackers. TEEs (secure hardware enclaves) raise the bar, but they've been broken before, and insiders and bad updates are risks too. Your key in Phantom was one target among millions. At Privy it sits in one giant vault.
- Privy and pumpfun gets to decide if you keep access to your wallet. Got some funds sent to you from a source that they decide is suspicious, or they just don't like you? You can get banned and lose access to your wallet, or they can decide to move your assets based on a court order. Sure you can export the private key you create on pumpfun. Did you?
- Google/Apple/Github also gets to decide if you keep access to your wallet. Ever read stories about people losing access to a lifetime of emails because Google decided they don't deserve access anymore? Now you also get to lose your wallet. Once again, you can export the private key you create on pumpfun. Did you?
- Your key now exists in two places: Your local wallet and Privy. Deleting your pumpfun account doesn't take it back. The site's own text says Privy "still holds the key" for wallets from deleted accounts.
- The key field is a plain textarea on pumpfun's page, not an isolated iframe like Stripe's card field. Every script on the page (Google Tag Manager, analytics, etc.) can read it. The site's CSP allows unsafe-inline scripts, all of unpkg and jsdelivr, Facebook, TikTok and more. I found no code reading the key today, but nothing technically prevents it.
- Your wallet's security goes from "who holds the key" to "who can log in to Privy", which is a much lower bar and not suitable for holding any kind of (serious) amount of assets.

And the most important:

- None of this is necessary. The flow already makes you sign a "Sign in with Solana" message, which proves you own the wallet and signing each transaction you do is your choice for security. Hardware wallets and multisig users can't import at all and just lose their account. A signature-based migration would have worked for everyone.

On top of that, teaching millions of users "paste your private key into this box before the deadline" builds exactly the habit scammers exploit.

Never share your private key with anyone. Your private keys is private, that's literally in the name. Let privy create a new key (and don't keep assets there) or just stop using pumpfun if they keep requiring your keys to be held with them.

Part of this bet was a realization: very few companies were capable of profitably monetizing their GPUs.

text:
"Trade for long enough, and you discover that the market has a godlike ability to peer into your soul, learn your character flaws, your private fears, weaknesses, pain thresholds. And the market uses this knowledge to tease you, sometimes letting you get away with recklessness, rewarding your greed, luring you to commit more brazen sins. At other times it creates false hope that you’ll escape whatever predicament you’ve gotten yourself into, allowing you to believe your own lies, letting you imagine you’ll slip its grasp this one time. Just like it did to leveraged Nvidia longs this Tuesday evening, when a blowout earnings report lifted the stock sharply higher after hours. By Friday's close it had lost 23% on the week. The process wears you down, so that at your weakest moment you puke positions at the absolute low, knowing it’s almost certainly a mistake, but grateful to end the torture. And breathe again.

When enough people hold the same view and pair it with arrogance, the market rounds up the herd and culls it in a violent flush. One man’s stop loss pushes price lower to the next man’s point of maximum pain, a runaway wildfire, a scorched earth cleanse. Sodom. Gomorrah. Like in February 2018, when the sellers of equity volatility watched their hallowed inverse VIX products lose 96% of their value in a ferocious afternoon. There was no specific catalyst. No real reason. Just the market gods at work. And it’s the very personal struggle with this omniscient superintelligence that makes those of us who have survived more introspective and humbler with time. It keeps us on the lookout for those moments when the herd has been rounded up and is being led to slaughter. Doing everything in our power to avoid that fate, and to capitalize on the chaos."

Eric Peters, One River Asset Management

We fully support OpenAI's transparency initiative. Thanks to @merettm @markchen90 @gdb @sama for leading the way. 

We all got into this field to build safe AGI that is genuinely good for humanity. One of the hardest parts of AI safety is coordination, and this is a step in the right direction. Many more steps like this will be needed to deliver safe, contained, and aligned AGI in the next few years.

We're committed to sharing our pre-training progress on a common held-out evaluation set. With OpenAI's permission, we report MAI-2 Base on their evaluation set. Its log-perplexity is 0.819, putting it in the same ballpark as the GPT-5.6 Sol base model. Our model uses the same tokenizer as OpenAI, so the numbers are directly comparable. 

In the future, to be able to compare across labs we might need to report bits-per-byte (BPB) rather than perplexity since different labs use different tokenizers. We will also need different evaluation datasets - the fact we have access to OpenAI's evaluation dataset is a special case.

Safety and alignment is now the mission. It's the absolute number one most important focus for our industry. And it begins with small, practical steps like these towards better coordination on pacing.

Today was a big day. Anthropic should now publish its own perplexity scores. Or, if Anthropic disagrees with OpenAI that perplexity is a smart place to intervene, it should highlight a different lever for pacing.

I sometimes hear stuff like "Everyone knows things are moving fast, the METR report on RSI at Anthropic made that clear already. Shouldn't that + incident disclosures be enough for the public and other AI companies and DC and Sacramento to work with?"

This feels like the wrong way to think about it. I worry that Anthropic painstakingly games out the downsides of transparency, but doesn't game out the upsides (of informing and engaging the outside world) with equal imagination. That probably leads to them being more secretive than they need to be.

There is no consensus on the right way to pace. I've seen an endless carousel of pacing ideas, from compute reallocation to internal deployment lags to security-based pauses to safety gating to alternating on-off weeks for R&D. Transparency around AI progress helps the public, the rest of the industry, and the government understand, evaluate, and rally around specific options. 

I'm impressed that OpenAI's Chief Scientist - who was later echoed by Sam - led the way today by disclosing data on their pretraining progress, arguing for perplexity-based limits, and adding: "I'd like an industry standard that specifies a first limit on development, measured by some key metric we can track across labs, and what concretely we'd need to achieve before going beyond it."

OpenAI took a great first step today. But if we don't have much much bigger leaps across multiple actors soon, we have failed. Every frontier lab should be directing its top talent to deeply investigate all the pacing proposals available, form views on them, publicly release evidence that improves awareness and spurs debate, and advocate for binding standards and legislation. If labs put half the firepower they spend making capabilities metrics go up into making cooperation more likely, we'd be in a much better world.
author: w01fe
quoted_text:
We fully support OpenAI's transparency initiative. Thanks to @merettm @markchen90 @gdb @sama for leading the way. 

We all got into this field to build safe AGI that is genuinely good for humanity. One of the hardest parts of AI safety is coordination, and this is a step in the right direction. Many more steps like this will be needed to deliver safe, contained, and aligned AGI in the next few years.

We're committed to sharing our pre-training progress on a common held-out evaluation set. With OpenAI's permission, we report MAI-2 Base on their evaluation set. Its log-perplexity is 0.819, putting it in the same ballpark as the GPT-5.6 Sol base model. Our model uses the same tokenizer as OpenAI, so the numbers are directly comparable. 

In the future, to be able to compare across labs we might need to report bits-per-byte (BPB) rather than perplexity since different labs use different tokenizers. We will also need different evaluation datasets - the fact we have access to OpenAI's evaluation dataset is a special case.

Safety and alignment is now the mission. It's the absolute number one most important focus for our industry. And it begins with small, practical steps like these towards better coordination on pacing.

author: teortaxesTex
quoted_text:
In China, he was imprisoned for supporting Ukraine. And when he was released, he came to fight for us.

He was killed just two days after his 30th birthday.

He had no family here, no home. No one was waiting for him to return from the front, and no one demanded that he take up arms.

His name was Peng Chenliang. He was born in China, thousands of kilometers from Ukraine.

When russia launched its full-scale invasion, Peng openly spoke out against the war.

For his views, including anti-russian statements, he spent seven months behind bars in China.

Seven months of imprisonment for his beliefs. You might think that after such an experience, a person would remain silent, become afraid, and never again get involved in someone else’s war.

But Peng made a different choice.

In April 2024, he came to Ukraine and joined the International Legion.

He could have stayed home, started a new life, and never heard the sound of a russian artillery shell.

Instead, he found himself on the Ukrainian front lines, alongside people whose language he barely spoke, on land where he had never lived.

On November 2, 2024, Peng turned 30. Just two days later, on November 4, he was killed in battle against russian forces.

He never made it home.

Before his death, Peng left a video message. He wanted his memory to be honored under the flag of Taiwan.

According to his fellow soldiers, he also dreamed of being buried in a free Ukraine.

Think about that. A man born in China, who grew up thousands of kilometers away from us, wanted Ukraine to be his final resting place.

Not because his ancestors came from here. Not because Ukraine was his home. But because this was where he chose to fight for what he believed in.

After Peng’s death, other Chinese volunteers said that his example had inspired them to come and defend Ukraine as well.

He will forever be 30. He was not born Ukrainian, but he gave Ukraine the most precious thing he had – his life.

Thank you, Peng.

text:
CIA disguise artist Jonna Mendez wore an elaborate mask and wig to a meeting in the Oval Office with President George H. W. Bush in the early 1990s.

President Bush was a former director of the CIA himself and was still stunned by her instant transformation. After she described cutting-edge disguise techniques, she told him she was wearing one at the moment.

The mask was part of a program known as DAGGER, allowing CIA officers to don an ultra-realistic full-face mask and wig in just a few moments to escape from adversarial surveillance teams. CIA case officers using DAGGER could change not just their appearance, but their race and even gender as well. Jonna preferred to disguise herself as an African-American woman when working.

Jonna reported that on some occasions the CIA even disguised two different case officers as identical twins. When one was tailed by an adversarial surveillance team, they could be replaced by their twin at a predetermined rendezvous point, and the original could change out of the disguise (or into a new one) and continue with the mission, now free of any observers.

Originally hired by the Central Intelligence Agency as a secretary in 1966, Jonna eventually retired in 1993 as the Chief of Disguise for the Office of Technical Services. This was the culmination of an incredible career that had taken her to some of the world’s most dangerous locales in the performance of some of the riskiest espionage activities imaginable in Moscow, Havana, and elsewhere.

During interviews after her retirement, Jonna reported that on two separate occasions she had conducted meetings on the Indian subcontinent and in Bogota, Colombia, where she had been unsure if she’d leave the meeting alive.

While employed by the CIA she met her future husband, Antonio “Tony” Mendez, a painter who worked his way up to become the CIA’s top forger and disguise artist. Tony was played by Ben Affleck in the hit film “Argo”, about the rescue of American hostages in Iran in 1979.

Some of her disguise items are now on display at the International Spy Museum in Washington DC.

‼️ Alice Huang / Megaspeed are now directly linked to Singapore court cases concerning 5 people arrested for smuggling export-controlled Nvidia chips to China ‼️

Alice Huang was the public face. But playing a key role behind the scenes was 🇨🇳 national Li Ming (李明) — now out on bail in Singapore, living in a luxury villa down the street from the Chinese Embassy.

Li was a central operator of a web of companies — including Megaspeed — smuggling restricted Nvidia AI chips to China. Li was deeply involved in Megaspeed’s activities and took part in major decisions as well as playing a role in other companies trading Nvidia chips.

Authorities in Singapore charged Li and others with fraud in Feb 2025 (https://t.co/ul6X9Lkue6), in a case tied to transshipment of Nvidia chips. Several companies were named in the charges, but not Megaspeed.

Singapore prosecutors allege Li bought computer servers equipped with Nvidia chips and lied to the American supplier, claiming the hardware was for his local company, Luxuriate Your Life. Instead, those servers were shipped to Malaysia — and then to an unnamed third location.

By the time those charges were filed, Li had been working with Alice Huang and her husband, Kang Wei, for years. In 2021, the couple set up a cloud-computing joint venture called Century Longteng. In Jan 2023, Li popped up in a social-media photo documenting his visit to a Shanghai AI equipment company. It referred to him as Century Longteng’s chief strategy officer.

At the time, the Biden administration had just restricted sales of Nvidia’s semiconductors to China. Suddenly, Chinese tech companies wanting the world’s best AI chips had two choices. One was to legally access Nvidia computing abroad, a logistical hassle requiring transferring heaps of data across borders.

The other was to smuggle hardware into China.

Li, Alice Huang and Kang began setting up a chain of partners in Southeast Asia to funnel advanced computing power to Chinese customers. They acquired the Singaporean unit of a Chinese videogame company and renamed it Megaspeed. Alice Huang was registered as a company director.

After telling Nvidia that Alibaba was an anchor customer, Megaspeed became a member of Nvidia’s cloud partner program in Nov 2023. The partner status granted Megaspeed priority access to buy the latest chips.

Megaspeed brought servers to Malaysia and provided legal offshore computing power to Alibaba. In violation of US export controls, some of those servers were sent to a Shanghai tech company called Century Litong. Century Longteng was a key shareholder of Century Litong until 2024.

Nvidia said it placed Megaspeed on an internal “no sell” list in June 2025 around the time when the US and Singapore were investigating the company.

Megaspeed has said that Alice Huang left the company in Aug 2025. Singapore officials have said that after questioning her over smuggling suspicions, they let her leave the country and barred her from re-entering.

Megaspeed largely went dark in Singapore after Alice Huang’s departure. But the team behind it is now running a new venture called Novagate Cloud.
Set up in 2025, Novagate says on its website that it is an Nvidia cloud partner operating at least two data centers with Nvidia’s Blackwell chips.

In the first 5 months of this year, Novagate received at least $300 million worth of hardware containing Nvidia chips at one of its entities in Malaysia.

Novagate lists two Singaporeans as its director and secretary. Both also serve as director and secretary of a company controlled by a director of a Century Litong Singaporean sibling company, who has recently been charged in Singapore over crimes similar to those Li is accused of.

A Culper Research report in May said Novagate was likely linked to Megaspeed because their websites are nearly identical, and one of its directors shared an address with Megaspeed’s HQ.

quoted_text:
🔥 Alice Huang had connections to a network for supplying AI chips that included a Cambodian criminal enterprise.

Former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang is at the centre of US investigations into whether Nvidia’s largest client in southeast Asia was involved in the underground chip trade.

Linked to Alice Huang was a sprawling web of companies between Nvidia and China-based users of its chips that included cloud computing partners, online gaming tycoons, Cambodian traffickers and hundreds of shell companies.

These seemingly unconnected enterprises combined — without necessarily being aware of the full picture — to make billions of dollars from one of the most profitable illicit trades in the world: moving Nvidia chips into China.

Washington’s export controls to prevent Beijing from acquiring the most powerful processors have created a multibillion-dollar black market to circumvent US curbs and satisfy China’s insatiable demand.

‘A spotless record’

Moving advanced chips into China requires three main corporate channels: a group that is permitted to acquire and distribute the semiconductors; customers that do not fall foul of US export restrictions; and an underground network to smuggle the goods into China and money out.

The network linked to Alice Huang reached the US through Inspur, which was one of Nvidia’s largest partners for assembling chips into ready-to-use servers in China.

In Mar 2023, Inspur was added to the US “entity list” for allegedly assisting the Chinese military. Some of its affiliates were also added to the register — but not Inspur’s part-owned US subsidiary, based in San Jose, California.

Inspur renamed the US unit Aivres, and since it was not on the entity list, it was able to keep trading with Nvidia.

Inside the chipmaker, there were questions about whether Aivres should qualify as an OEM partner because of its links to Inspur. But Nvidia concluded the company met all compliance and export control requirements.

The second plank of the network was a customer that met the requirements to buy Nvidia chips at scale. OEM partners such as Aivres, which are allowed to integrate Nvidia GPUs into systems and sell those on, still needed to prove that their customers are not Chinese to access the US chipmaker’s products.

To be a qualified end customer, Nvidia requires at least three years of corporate records and proof that its management and owners are not majority Chinese.

Seeking to regain access to chip supplies, some of Inspur’s Chinese clients sought help from a successful online gaming company, Century Huatong.

Over two decades, the Chinese group had morphed from a car parts business into a gaming platform, finally emerging as a data center investor with deep connections in the industry.

Century Huatong veterans discussed ways to gain access to the chips with its associates and business partners. The solution that emerged involved using an offshore shell company that would not trigger US export restrictions and could be branded as a “neocloud” provider.

That shell became Megaspeed, while Alice Huang fulfilled the requirement for a “trusted” outward-facing executive with a spotless record.

Huang’s husband, Kang Wei, was an early investor in Century Huatong. His fund Hexi Investment also backed a 2020 Century Huatong data centre project with 7Road, a Shenzhen-based gaming company in which both Huang and Century Huatong had invested.

7Road International, the offshore arm of 7Road, was the forerunner of Megaspeed, having had several years of clean corporate records in Singapore. In 2023, Huang acquired its unit in the city-state and renamed it.

An Nvidia spokesperson: “We placed Megaspeed and a subsidiary on our block list in 2025 . . . we do not sell to them, and if one of our OEM customers identifies the company for any planned shipment, we do not approve the OEM sale.” Nvidia added that it had also restricted sales to Aivres.

text:
Fieldwatch 1.2.0 is now available. 

Fieldwatch is a free Android app that shows you what's watching you. It can flag nearby Ray-Ban Meta glasses, Flock cameras, body cams, public safety vehicles, drones, and a lot more. It spots Bluetooth trackers like AirTags that are moving with you, and its Hunt tool helps you find one if it's hidden. It can also warn you about odd cell tower changes or GPS interference.

New this release:

Drone perimeter detection. Because drones fly high, your phone can hear their Remote ID from up to several miles away. You don't need a ping for every drone on the horizon. Pick your distance, like 250 m, and Fieldwatch draws an invisible dome around you. When a drone's broadcast position comes inside it, your phone alerts you.

Drone swarm detection. If several new drones pop up at once, Fieldwatch alerts you. Five or more in half a minute is unusual, so when it happens, you'll know.

Quickly see where it's headed. Tap a drone's Remote ID marker on the map to see its altitude, speed and course without having to pull up all details.

A bigger view of your sit. The Sit Paths map is now larger, so you can now better see the whole route and every detection along it.

Low battery protection. When your battery gets low, Fieldwatch slows its scanning. If it gets lower still, it stops, so you keep enough charge for maps, calls and TAK.

329 signatures and counting. Fieldwatch now names more of the devices that used to be unmatched. More two-way radios, smart glasses, thermal optics, FPV drone radio links, dashcams, cars, and a long list of everyday gear.

Share signatures with any app. Exports and imports now speak Radio Signature Interchange (RSI), an open standard for describing radio devices. It covers frequencies beyond Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, so it works for ESP32 projects, SDR setups and external radios attached to a phone.

Please encourage the developers of the other radio apps you use to consider adopting RSI. Any app that does gets all 329 Fieldwatch signatures right away. More at https://t.co/wsnUW04BZe

Get Fieldwatch on Github at:
https://t.co/Mx5yo2dw9j

text:
No, you don't understand how insane the actual story is.

Tunick protests a $118M training facility in Atlanta and is classified as part of a "violent extremist group" (Stop Cop City) and is placed on a watchlist.

On his flight back from the Dominican Republic, CBP are already waiting for him at the gate. Turns out, 3 hours before he landed, HSI emailed CBP to flag him for "suspected terrorist activities". The email directed agents to route him to secondary inspection, retain all electronics, and collect passcodes.

The agents claim they're looking for "kiddie porn" on his phone and demands his passcode. Tunick provides the duress code and the phone is wiped. But the emails didn't indicate that Tunick possessed child porn, so the defense is claiming that it was a pretext to search the devices. More importantly, Tunick was denied counsel and so the defense is claiming Tunick's Miranda rights were violated.

Officers:
“because you’re refusing to talk, which is your right, we have the authority to go through your phone to see what we’re looking for. ... when it comes to immigration and customs, right, it’s a whole different ballgame . . . and we have search authority, we don’t need a warrant.”

If Tunick's Miranda rights were violated and the evidence gets suppressed because of that, that means the prosecution cannot use Tunick providing the duress code as grounds for knowingly destroying evidence. Proving intent is the portion that the prosecution needs in order to claim a crime had been committed.

Moral of the story is that you shouldn't knowingly destroy evidence because that constitutes a crime. Also, call for a lawyer and then shut the fuck up.

You can reasonably use a duress password if the other person has no legal authority to be searching your phone. Because, the officers did get one thing right. Searches at the border work differently and CBP does have that authority.

Anyway, this is a case to watch as it relates heavily to privacy and your rights when you are detained.

> climbed 3.12x -> 6.82x -> 8.53x -> 10.04x isolated regrade (0.606 ms/tok, 1,650 tok/s at ctx=8192; 1,941 tok/s at ctx=2048)

text:
首先，这个事儿是链上 IPO。也就是中小企业的融资链上化，将 IPO 上市完全转化成链上 ICO。
而且这不只有币安在做，其他很多家交易所都在做尝试。

那么，是怎么看出来的？
首先，这个要求就是典型的对于 IPO 上市企业的一些资质要求；
其次，这个截图里面也有“上市申请”这样的字眼

币安想搞链上 IPO 其实已经很久了。
最典型的就是 CZ 之前发的一个帖子，说 IPO 很快就会在链上实现。

当时我们看到的是 Polymarket 上形成的 Pre-IPO 交易，但实际上他们真正想做的是实现币股同权。

——也就是把股票和代币彻底打通，让 IPO 等于 ICO。

这主要是针对一些中小企业，尤其是无法在链下成功上市的企业，实现为中小企业纾困的逻辑。

这件事的想象空间很大：

1. 普惠金融：给融不到钱的企业一个融资的机会，实现真正的普惠金融效应这种玩法可以让融不到钱的企业将企业重心和资本运作全都放在链上。
2.多资产联动，股币结合：通过结合 Meme、代币、股票和合约，实现真正的 Meme 币联动，既能拉升股价，给企业资金的同时，做币安生态内的资产运作。
3. 链上VC：既然 IPO 能在链上完成，那么 VC 融资的过程是不是也能在链上完成？其实下一步就是链上 VC 的过程。

实际上，企业上市融资的全流程都已经“链上化”，至此全部打通：

VC 融资 ➡️ Pre-IPO ➡️ IPO ➡️ 资产分发 ➡️ 币股联动

这个玩法不只是币安在探索，目前已经有很多项目方在尝试链上 VC，同时也有很多交易所在推进链上 IPO。

如果这件事能够落实，onchain finance 的愿景就能更sexy，完成一个由链上 VC 、链上发行、链上分销、链上交易所的闭环全流程。

这对币圈的影响其实要从两方面看待：

首先，它丰富了新的玩法。它可能让一些中小企业开始真正向币圈寻求资金，将新资产引向币圈。

但是，新资产不一定是优质资产。在传统世界融不到钱的企业，为什么在币圈就能融到了？是不是还是把垃圾资产上了链，让传统金融又一次吸币圈的血？

所以说，这到底是给币圈注入了新的血液，还是再一次吸币圈的血，我们还得再观察。

但能确定的就一点：它会让传统世界再一次见证到币圈的力量。不过合规层面是一个需要重点去观察的对象！

⚠️ALERT: Hackers are now running ads in 47 countries that can STEAL CRYPTO SEED PHRASES from iPhones.

Security firm Confiant tracked the group, MoldyRoost, across more than 480 ad domains since May.

On a vulnerable iPhone, simply opening the page behind one of its ads is enough to trigger the attack.

You're at risk if your iPhone runs iOS 18 or older and you use crypto wallets like MetaMask, Phantom or Trust Wallet.

The flaws are in iOS itself, not in the wallet apps.

It reads your iOS version, then picks 1 of 4 exploit kits that Confiant calls "nation-state-grade."

They're built to take:

1. Wallet seed phrases
2. Passwords saved in your keychain
3. Messages and photos

One kit is aimed at fully updated iOS 18 phones, and its range runs all the way to iOS 26.

➥ Ethereum's weekly fee burn is up 67%, but ETH's value capture still has a much bigger problem

as of Nov 22, 2026:

→ ETH fee burn / 7D: ~$1.0M (+67.04% WoW)
→ Oct user-paid fees: $22.90M
→ Oct ETH burned through fees: ~$7.79M
→ Nov 1-20 user-paid fees: $6.93M
→ Nov 1–20 ETH burned: $2.14M

the October-to-November comparison is more revealing than the weekly rebound

Ethereum burned ~34% of user-paid fees in Oct, versus 31% during Nov 1-20

and Nov's first 20 days generated only ~30% of October's full-month fees

so even with the latest weekly recovery, the broader fee environment remains weak

this matters a lot since $ETH’s value capture works differently from most DeFi tokens

→ base fees and blob fees remove ETH from circulation
→ priority fees go to validators and builders
→ staking issuance adds new ETH to circulation

higher network activity doesn't automatically mean ETH becomes deflationary

and cheaper L2 txns make the relationship between eco adoption and L1 fee burn even less straightforward

Ethereum can keep growing as financial infra while its token economics lag behind

best wish for $ETH holders
